pages.text:
# Business Partners

We're always looking for new partners to help us better serve our Marines and family members.

The procurement of equipment, supplies, support services, revenue-generating services, and professional services is accomplished at both the Headquarters and the MCCS field activity level. To inquire about selling items through retail channels, such as the Marine Corps Exchange, [click here](https://www.mymcx.com/about/partnerships) to learn more.

## MCCS Contracting Office
Headquarters, U.S. Marine Corps
Business & Support Services Division (MR)
Attn: Procurement (MRB)
3044 Catlin Avenue
Quantico, VA 22134-5099

Email: hqmcnafcontracting@usmc-mccs.org

To be added to the source list and considered for future procurements, interested vendors must contact each MCCS Contracting Office. We do not use a standard source application; simply provide your company name, website address, contact information, and a short summary of products or services.

Examples of non-resale procurement accomplished by the MCCS Contracting Office include:

**Equipment & Supply Items:**
- Cell Phones and Service
- Food Service Equipment
- Retail Fixtures
- IT Hardware and Software
- Recreation & Fitness Equipment

**Support Services:**
- Grounds Keeping
- Printing & Advertising
- Distribution Services
- Small Construction
- Maintenance and Repair

**Revenue-generating Services**
- Barber and Beauty Shop Services
- Vending Machines and Products
- Golf Courses
- Laundry/Dry Cleaning
- Foodservice

**Professional Services:**
- Banking, Audit, and Credit Card Processing Services
- Feasibility Studies
- Employee Development Training
- Consultant Services
- Instructors

These goods and services are purchased for our Marine Corps Exchanges, clubs, lodging facilities, recreation activities and warehouse facilities.

Our non-resale procurement professionals may also order against other NAFI and Federal Government contracts, such as those issued by the General Services Administration and Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Purchasing Office (AFNAFPO).

It is our policy that procurement using nonappropriated funds be accomplished primarily through competition in a fair, equitable, and impartial manner, and to the best advantage of the MCCS. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does not apply to non-appropriated fund procurements, except when specifically required by DoD Directive, Instruction, or Component regulations.

## Contract Clauses/General Provisions Downloads
Listed below are the General Provision documents available for download. For the current MCX Terms and Conditions and Vendor Standards Guide, visit [https://www.mymcx.com/about/partnerships](https://www.mymcx.com/about/partnerships)

pages.title: About
pages.text:
# About

## Who We Are
Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is a comprehensive set of programs that support and enhance the operational readiness, war fighting capabilities, and life quality of Marines, their families, retirees and civilians. MCCS delivers goods and services at over 2,250 facilities with a staff of more than 12,000 employees worldwide.

## Our Mission
To take care of Marines and their families by providing quality of life programs, products, and services in support of the Marine Corps objectives.

## Our Vision
MCCS will be the first choice of products, services, and programs by exceeding our customers' expectations and building lifelong customers. To do this as an organization we must be:

- Employer of Choice to individuals who are dedicated to supporting our War Heroes and their families.
- Steward for promoting effective policy and business practices intended to support and complement our mission.
- Cross-functional and continually seeking synergy across all processes.
- Provider of premier facilities that promote personal and family readiness.
- Deliver quality programs and services to meet current and future needs.
- Responsive to customer behaviors and generate goodwill.

## Our Values
The Marine Corps holds true to the core values of honor, courage, and commitment.

## Contact Us
- [Send us an Email](mailto:mccslejeune-newrivernews@usmc-mccs.org): mccslejeune-newrivernews@usmc-mccs.org
- Newsletter Sign-Up
- Human Resources: 910-451-JOBS

Contact: Marine Corps Community Services Lejeune-New River
Phone (Human Resources): 910-451-JOBS
Email: mccslejeune-newrivernews@usmc-mccs.org

# Marine For Life Cycle

(Long page, shortened here: each section's opening only. Fetch the page for the full text.)

## First Permanent Duty Station (PDS) Checklist
Congratulations and welcome aboard! You have completed your initial training and finally arrived to your new home at your first PDS. You are probably busy checking in to your new unit and exploring your new installation. You will attend the Personal Readiness Seminar (PRS) where you will discover the services available to you throughout your Marine Corps career. Just as you learned to orient a map during land navigation classes, you must also orient yourself in your new location. Work through the checklist below to ensure you start your Marine Corps career off on the right foot.

## Reenlistment Checklist
Congratulations Marine! As you complete your enlistment there are many options available to you. Your decision to "stay Marine" comes with a completely new set of challenges and opportunities. Re-enlistment is a good time to reevaluate your Individual Development Plan (IDP). Consider meeting with a Personal and Professional Development Advisor to discuss opportunities and programs available to you. Perhaps you'd like to pursue new educational interests or explore credentials and apprenticeships, or maybe you will be receiving a re-enlistment bonus and would like to learn more about saving and investing. You may also be preparing to PCS or transition to a "B" billet.The topics below will assist you to make sound and timely decisions regarding this transition.

## Promotion Checklist
Congratulations Marine! Promotion is an exciting time. More responsibility and more pay! It's also a great time to evaluate your Individual Development Plan. Schedule an appointment with a Personal & Professional Development Advisor (P&PD) to discuss your goals. Do you have an emergency fund? Are you planning for retirement? Your income is growing; your Personal Financial Manager (PFM) or Command Financial Specialist (CFS) can provide workshops and one on one counseling to help you reach your financial goals. While you are adjusting to your new rank, it's not too early to begin preparing for your next promotion. Keep yourself technically and tactically proficient. The links below will help you achieve success.

## Deployment/Redeployment Checklist
Preparation is critical to a successful deployment. In addition to preparing your gear and your Marines, you must ensure your personal affairs are in order. Your command will provide opportunities to complete pre-deployment preparations. The topics below will provide additional resources to assist in your personal deployment preparation.

## Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Checklist
Whether this is your first PCS or your tenth, proper preparation and planning will make the process much smoother. It's never too early to begin setting aside a PCS fund to ensure those unexpected expenses don't result in financial hardship. Once you have received your orders you'll want to begin researching your new duty station and preparing your family and household goods for the move. Your new command will assign a sponsor to assist you as you settle in at your new unit.

# Camp Lejeune 4th of July Celebration

Celebrate America's 250th Birthday at W.P.T.

## PLAN AHEAD FOR THE HEAT
High heat and humidity are expected during the July 4th Celebration.

Coolers are allowed, and attendees are strongly encouraged to bring plenty of water.

Drink water often, wear sun protection, take breaks from the heat, and check on children, older adults, pregnant individuals, and anyone sensitive to high temperatures.

Limited cooling areas will be available on site, including the USAA Cooling Tent, VFW Cooling Trailer, and USO Trailer.

If you feel dizzy, weak, nauseous, confused, or overheated, notify event staff or medical personnel immediately.

Stay hydrated, stay aware, and celebrate safely.

## CAMP LEJEUNE 4TH OF JULY CELEBRATION EVENT ACCESS: UPDATED: June 29 at 8:30Am
MCB Camp Lejeune has updated guest access procedures for the July 4 Celebration on July 4, 2026.

The event is now open to Department of War-affiliated personnel and their escorted guests. DoW ID-card holders who are US citizens and age 18 and older, may each escort up to five guests onto the installation without prior registration.

Beginning at 2PM, July 4, DoW-affiliated escorts and their guests may enter MCB Camp Lejeune through **Wilson Gate, Holcomb Gate, Camp Johnson Gate, or Sneads Ferry Gate.**

For additional base access details, please visit: https://www.lejeune.marines.mil/news/article/article/4528631/camp-lejeune-updates-guest-access-procedures-for-independence-day-celebration/

The Visitor Center will be closed on July 3.

In case of inclement weather, this event will not be rescheduled.

## SCHEDULE OF EVENTS
- 3:30PM - Trams Start
- 4PM - Event Site Open | Food & Beverage Vendors | MCCS Family Fun Zone
- 4:30PM - Stage Entertainment Begins
- 5-7PM - Meet American football athlete Xavier Legette
- 8PM - MCCS Family Fun Zone Closes
- 8:45PM - Fireworks | Food and Beverage Sales Cease

*Times are approximate and subject to change.*

## MCCS FAMILY FUN ZONE
Games, activities, entertainment, and family fun.

- Open 4-8PM.
- Children ages 10 and younger must be accompanied by an adult.
- Please follow all staff instructions and posted activity requirements.

## Entertainment
**DYLAN SCOTT**

Despite a multi-Platinum story and six No. 1 singles, including two fresh smashes in 2025, Curb Records hitmaker Dylan Scott has always kept an underdog mindset. A rowdy roughneck with a romantic side – one whose modern edge was sharpened by timeless, emotional twang – the consummate family man broke out with the epic triple-Platinum devotion of "My Girl" in 2016 and followed up with scrappy, under-the-radar consistency. Chart-topping heart-forward anthems like "Hooked," "Nobody" and "New Truck" all reached RIAA-certified status, but 2025 has launched the crooner into the stratosphere. 1s in 2025 alone and six No. 1s overall, Scott wrapped 2025 as the third most-played country artist of the year at country radio and continues his hot streak with his current Top 10 single, Platinum-certified "What He'll Never Have." With nearly 5 billion career streams, legions of fans and countless sold-out shows to his credit, his stardom has somehow grown in relative stealth. Featuring 11 tracks, his signature vocal and vivid intensity take center stage on a set defined by personal truth – whether through heartbreak, romantic devotion or small-town dedication. The in-demand live act wrapped his Country Till I Die and Easy Does It Tours in 2025, headlining his biggest venues yet including his first-ever arenas and record-breaking attendance.

**HOT CHELLE RAE**

Hot Chelle Rae lit up pop radio since 2011 with massive hooks and unforgettable energy, breaking out worldwide with multi-Platinum hits like "Tonight Tonight" and "I Like It Like That."

With over 1 billion global streams, an American Music Award, and tours alongside Taylor Swift, Demi Lovato, and Justin Bieber, the band became a cultural staple of the recently resurgent 2010s pop-rock scene.

After coming back together over the past few years, they've been playing shows around the world — and the crowds are making it clear they've been waiting for HCR's next move.

The band's recently finished their first full-length album since 2011: a feel-good, high-energy record that has everything fans loved from the beginning with a fresh wave of Y2K alt pop inspo.

It's a new chapter, but the heart's the same — built on big melodies, good times, and the kind of songs people play on repeat.

**ZACH HARRINGTON**

Zach Harrington, a South Georgia native, brings a fresh, energetic sound shaped by real‑life grit and Southern roots.

He's joined on stage by Kaden Hudson, holding down the low end on bass, Jared Skinner on lead guitar, and Nehemy Pierre on drums — a tight, talented group whose chemistry drives their signature sound.

**MEET XAVIER LEGETTE**

**5-7PM**

This year's 4th of July Celebration marks America's 250th anniversary and features a special appearance by American football athlete, Xavier Legette, thanks to Visa and USAA! Join us Saturday, July 4th, at Camp Lejeune's W. Hill Field for an unforgettable day of patriotic festivities, complete with a meet-and-greet with Xavier Legette.

## Know Before You Go
**Who Can Attend**

Free event for DoW ID cardholders and their guests.

This event is open to Department of War-affiliated personnel and their escorted guests. DoW ID-card holders who are US citizens and age 18 and older, may each escort up to five guests onto the installation without prior registration.

**Plan Ahead for the Heat**

(Same text as "Plan Ahead for the Heat" above.)

**Inclement Weather**

In case of inclement weather on July 4, the event will be canceled and will not be rescheduled.

**Pets**

Pets will NOT be allowed in the venue area, with the exception of verified, registered service animals as defined in MCIEAST-MCB CAMLEJ Order 10570.2B.

## Parking
Main parking will be located at the Camp Lejeune MCX and Commissary parking lots. Parking in the grassy areas along the side of the road is not permitted. Free Tram service will be running from the designated parking locations to and from the event site beginning at 3:30PM.

Handicap accessible parking will be available at Bldg. 84. Vehicles must have a handicapped placard or plate to park in this area.

## Prohibited Items
- Personal fireworks or sparklers
- Glass Containers
- Personal Firearms
- Tents (to include shade tents/beach umbrellas)
- Controlled illegal substances and their associated paraphernalia
- Tasers
- Stun Guns
- Drones (UAS)
- Grills
- Pets (with the exception of registered service animals)
- Weapons, including knives
- Mace or oleoresin capsicum (i.e. pepper) spray

*Subject to change.*

## Frequently Asked Questions
**Can I bring items in a bag or backpack?**

Yes. However, all bags will be searched prior to entry.

**Is the event open to the public?**

Updated June 29, 2026

Beginning at 2PM, July 4, DoW-affiliated escorts and their guests may enter MCB Camp Lejeune through Wilson Gate, Holcomb Gate, Camp Johnson Gate, or Sneads Ferry Gate.

**Is this event free?**

Yes.

**What if I am staying at Inns of the Corps?**

Guests with booked lodging on this day will receive an Inns of the Corps Access Pass to be displayed on your vehicle dashboard.

**Will there be food & beverage available for purchase?**

Yes. Food and beverage sales will cease at 8:45PM.

**Is there seating?**

This is an open lawn seating event. Guests will bring their own seating (i.e.

**What do you recommend we bring?**

- Chairs, blankets
- Non-aerosol sunscreen and bug repellant
- Sunglasses and hat
- Coolers are permitted and subject to inspection (no glass containers)
- Cash (preferred), Debit, or Credit Cards
- Strollers

**May I bring a cooler?**

Yes. Coolers are allowed. No glass containers are permitted.

**Will there be a child lost and found area?**

Yes.

**Will there be restroom facilities?**

There will be port-o-letts available.

# Car Giveaway

## 2026 MCCS Lejeune-New River HolidayFest Car Giveaway
Enter to win below and check out the car you could win displayed at the Camp Lejeune MCX! Finalists will be contacted by MCCS and must be present to win at the MCCS Marine Chevrolet HolidayFest, presented by USAA & Raising Cane's on November 21, 2026 at the Camp Lejeune MCX.

Marine Chevrolet is your premier source for world-class vehicles, from cars and EVs to trucks and SUVs. Whether you're in the market for a new or used model, Marine Chevrolet's position as one of the leading Chevy dealers in NC ensures you drive off our lot with the ideal vehicle for all your Camp Lejeune drives at a price that fits your budget.

## OFFICIAL CONTEST RULES & REGULATIONS
**2026 MCCS Lejeune-New River HolidayFest Car Giveaway**
Sponsored by Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) Lejeune-New River
Commercial Co-Sponsor: Marine Chevrolet

## 1. PRIVACY ACT STATEMENT
**AUTHORITY:** 10 U.S.C. § 8013; 10 U.S.C. § 8041; DoD Instruction 1015.10, Military Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) Programs; Marine Corps Order (MCO) P1700.27B W/CH 1, Marine Corps Community Services Policy Manual; DoD 7000.14-R, DoD Financial Management Regulation, Volume 13; and System of Records Notice (SORN) NM01700-1, Department of the Navy (DON) General Morale, Welfare, and Recreation Records.

**PRINCIPAL PURPOSE(S):** To collect personal contact information necessary to register eligible authorized patrons for the MCCS Lejeune-New River 2026 HolidayFest Car Giveaway, verify patron eligibility, conduct random finalist drawings, notify finalists, and administer the final vehicle award.

**ROUTINE USE(S):** Information collected will be used internally by MCCS personnel and official event administrators to operate this drawing. Personal information will not be disclosed outside the Department of War, **except** that the name, email address, and telephone number of entrants who affirmatively and voluntarily provide written/digital opt-in consent on the registration entry form will be provided to the commercial sponsor, Marine Chevrolet, for promotional offers, vehicle incentives, and marketing communications. Additional disclosures may be made pursuant to the standard blanket routine uses established under SORN NM01700-1.

**DISCLOSURE:** Voluntary. However, failure to provide the mandatory information (Full Name, Branch/Status, DoW ID or Eligible Patron Identifier, Valid Phone Number, and Email Address) will preclude registration and entry into the giveaway drawing. Electing to share contact details with the commercial sponsor is strictly optional; opting out of sponsor marketing will **not** adversely affect registration status, eligibility, or odds of winning.

## 2. ELIGIBILITY
**1. Eligible Patrons:**

Open to authorized MWR patrons who are legal residents of the United States and are 18 years of age or older as of the date of entry. Authorized patrons include:

- Active-duty military service members and their lawful dependents
- Members of the Reserve Components (Ready Reserve, Selected Reserve, and National Guard) and their lawful dependents
- Military retirees and their lawful dependents
- Honorably discharged veterans possessing a valid Department of War (DoW) ID card or DD Form 214 verifying veteran status with base access

**2. Ineligible Individuals:**

- Civilian and military employees of Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) and Marine Corps Exchange (MCX)
- Employees, officers, directors, and commercial representatives of Marine Chevrolet
- Immediate family members (spouses, children, siblings, parents) and individuals residing in the same household (whether related or unrelated) of any of the excluded employees identified above

**3. Legal Compliance:**

This promotion is subject to all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Void where prohibited by law.

## 3. HOW TO ENTER
1. **Online Entry Period:** The giveaway registration begins at **10:00 AM EST on October 26, 2026**, and concludes sharply at **12:00 PM (Noon) EST on November 18, 2026** (the "Entry Period").
2. **Entry Method:** Eligible patrons must complete and submit the official online entry form accessible through the official MCCS Lejeune-New River website.
3. **Entry Limitations:** Entries are strictly limited to **one (1) entry per authorized patron**.
4. **No Purchase Necessary:** No fee, retail purchase, service charge, or commercial consideration at Marine Corps Exchange or Marine Chevrolet is required to enter or win.
5. **Technical Limitations:** MCCS is not responsible for lost, late, incomplete, illegible, misdirected, or mutilated entries, or for technical, hardware, or software failures of any kind, lost or unavailable network connections, or failed, incomplete, garbled, or delayed electronic communications.

## 4. SELECTION OF FINALISTS & VERIFICATION
1. **Preliminary Drawing:** On the afternoon of **November 18, 2026**, MCCS administrators will conduct a random computer-generated drawing from all eligible entries received to select **twelve (12) confirmed finalists**.
2. **Finalist Notification:** MCCS will attempt to contact each selected finalist using the primary telephone number and email address submitted on their entry form.
3. **Confirmation Cutoff:** Each finalist must respond and confirm their intent and ability to attend the live HolidayFest event no later than **12:00 PM (Noon) EST on November 20, 2026**.

## 5. GRAND PRIZE & LIVE EVENT DRAWING
1. **Grand Prize:** One (1) new, unused, untitled **2026 Chevrolet vehicle** (estimated retail value: $25,000), provided by Marine Chevrolet.
2. **Mandatory Attendance:** To be eligible to win the vehicle, finalists must be **physically present** at the HolidayFest main stage at the Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune MCX on **November 21, 2026**, checking in with MCCS event staff no later than the pre-designated call time announced in their confirmation packet.
3. **On-Site Forfeiture:** If any confirmed finalist is not present at the check-in desk or fails to appear on stage when their name is called, their eligibility is immediately forfeited without exception.
4. **Live Progressive Elimination Procedure:**
   - The on-stage finalists will participate in a live, random progressive elimination drawing administered by MCCS and co-emceed by command leadership and Marine Chevrolet.
   - In each progressive round, one finalist will be drawn and eliminated from grand-prize contention and awarded an official MCCS runner-up prize package.
   - The process continues through successive rounds until only one (1) finalist remains.

## 6. PRIZE CONDITIONS, TAXES, & TRANSFER OF TITLE
1. **Award Acceptance & Documentation:** The Grand Prize Winner must execute an MCCS Affidavit of Eligibility, Liability Release, Publicity Release, and an IRS Form W-9 prior to taking legal possession or title of the vehicle.

   - The Winner is solely and exclusively responsible for all federal, state, and local income taxes, sales/use taxes, luxury taxes, or any other tax assessments resulting from receipt and acceptance of the prize.
3. **Registration, Licensing, and Fees:**
   - Marine Chevrolet is responsible for all governmental title fees, license plates, vehicle registration fees and dealer documentary fees. The Winner is responsible for mandatory vehicle insurance required by state law prior to driving or removing the vehicle from dealer or base custody.
   - The Winner must possess a valid, government-issued driver's license and provide verified proof of adequate motor vehicle liability insurance before delivery will occur.
4. **No Cash Alternative or Transfer:** The prize is nontransferable, non-assignable, and non-negotiable.

## 7. GENERAL CONDITIONS & LEGAL DISCLAIMERS
1. **Limitation of Liability:** By participating, entrants and winners agree to release, discharge, indemnify, and hold harmless the United States Government, the Department of War, the United States Navy, the United States Marine Corps, MCCS, Marine Chevrolet, and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all claims, demands, damages, injuries, or losses of any kind resulting from entry in this promotion or the receipt, ownership, delivery, use, or misuse of the vehicle prize.
2. **Publicity Grant:** Acceptance of the prize constitutes permission for MCCS and the commercial sponsor to publish and broadcast the Winner's name, hometown, rank, and photographic likeness in official command publications, internal MCCS promotional channels, and sponsor media without further compensation or review, except where prohibited by law.
3. **Official Non-Endorsement Disclaimer:** This promotion is conducted by Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) and commercially supported by Marine Chevrolet.
4. **Reservation of Rights:** MCCS reserves the right, in its sole administrative discretion, to cancel, suspend, or modify the promotion or these rules if fraud, technical failures, software bugs, security breaches, or force majeure events corrupt the integrity, security, or proper operation of the giveaway.

pages.title: Semper Connected
pages.text:
# Semper Connected

The Semper Connected toolkit is a compilation of resources for military spouses and family members to use to help create social connections. The Semper Connected toolkit was created by Marine Corps spouses with support from Marine and Family Programs.

## What is the Semper Connected Toolkit
The Semper Connected Toolkit outlined here is designed to assist spouses/family members in the creation of a community social network to connect and support spouses/family members through engagement, social events, and periodic check ins.

Contact and similar information is collected with permission from incoming spouses/family members by another spouse/family members within the unit. This information may be shared with other members of the Semper Connected team and will be used as a resource to support individual spouses/family members. The provision of contact and similar information is completely voluntary but is highly recommended; connection with and support from other spouses/family members who understand the military lifestyle is the greatest resource!

This Toolkit shall be managed in accordance with record schedule 1000-23, "Morale and Welfare Program Management" of SECNAV M-5210.1. A complete list and explanation of the applicable routine uses is published in the authorizing SORN available at: https://dpcld.defense.gov/Privacy/SORNsIndex/DOD-wide-SORN-Article-View/Article/570630/m01754-5/

## How do I Use the Semper Connected Toolkit?
**1. Create a Social Roster**

**Step 1:** "Make a Copy" of the [Semper Connected Contact Information Google Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/u/5/d/1LwxMr7wle3xedCk9fkQ-rDAOWX8lzxTLkOESUcCF-So/copy) and **RENAME** the copy with your unit name.

**Step 2:** Send the link for the new Semper Connected Contact Information Form via your DRC/URC, your unit facebook page, or as determined by the command.

**2. Get Connected**

Making connections is very personal.

**PHONE CALLS:** Review "How to connect by phone" and begin making phone calls with the phone numbers collected from the Semper Connected Contact Information Google Form.

- Consider sending a **text message first** letting the spouse or family member know that you will be calling to say hello
- The Semper Connected Phone Call Log (Google Form) is a tool available to help you take notes while reaching out to spouses and family members

**EMAILS and LETTERS:** Review the Semper Connected Sample Welcome Letter that can be sent via email or USPS. Feel free to edit and "make it your own"; include your personal touch or use it as is.

- Include an invitation to the next unit or spouse/family social event
- Enclose your contact information
- Include the resource

**Resources**

- Using Google Forms to Create a Social Roster
- DOD Cyber: Identifying and Safeguarding Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
- OPSEC/PII Tipsheet

## Connect by Phone
A basic guide for making your first phone call to reach out to spouses and family members in your command/unit/office/shop.

**A few things to remember before calling:**

- Consider sending a text message first letting the spouse or family member know that you will be calling to say hello
- Be friendly, your tone sets the call
- Make your phone calls when you aren't rushed and can actively listen, with minimal interruptions.
- Some people don't like talking on the phone or may be nervous, wondering why you are calling.
- Our Marine Corps family is an incredible group to be part of ~ THANK YOU for helping to create meaningful Marine Corps family connections!!

**Lets get started making calls**

1. Introduce yourself (first and last name) If you have met the spouse, remind them where you met them, as they may not remember. My name is _________, we met at _____________" or "My spouse works with your spouse in the (name of unit/shop)"
2. Explain why you're calling. "My spouse works at _UNIT NAME_ and I am calling to welcome you and say hello."
3. Ask if they received the welcome letter you (or unit URC/DRC) sent with the local numbers and resources and unit Facebook page and unit social Facebook page?
4. Ask about them (if it seems appropriate):
   - Are they new to the Marine Corps?
   - How long have they been married?
   - Do they work?
   - Are they involved in their (base/unit) community?
5. Ask about their family (if it seems appropriate):
   - Do they have children?
   - What are their ages?
   - How are they settling in? Adjusting to the new community?
   - Where are they from? Do they have extended family in the area to help?
6. Let them know about upcoming events, LINKS (Lifestyle, Insights, Networking, Knowledge and Skills ) classes, the Facebook page, spouse support groups.
7. Let them know you will/might call or text again, if they would like you to.
8. If they do not want you to call them, let them know that's okay.
9. Let them know you enjoyed talking to them and look forward to talking to them again/ meeting them in the future.

**Keep a Semper Connected Phone Call Log:**

1. Make a Copy of the "Semper Connected Phone Call Log"
2. Rename the Semper Connected Phone Call Log
3. Click the Eye Icon "Preview" in the Upper Right corner to fill in the information
4. You can fill this form again with each new contact
5. View all responses with the "Responses" tab and create a spreadsheet by clicking the "Sheets" icon

- Write the date you called
- Notes about the individual and his/her family (this information helps connect individual to others with similar interests, children's ages, hobbies, careers, etc)
- Items that need follow-up. (Connections to URC/DRC, resources available, chaplain support, etc.)

## Connect in Writing
Sending a personal letter, greeting card, or email is a wonderful way to welcome an individual or encourage a large group to connect. Your personal touch, including a bit about your USMC spouse experience, provides a familiar language that you both understand and speak together.

**Tips and Tricks**

- To ease the burden of letter writing, consider making photo copies of a typed personal letter and writing a brief message at the bottom saying "Hello!" with your signature
- Include an invitation to a coffee, wine tasting, hike, or park meetup
- Include your personal business card with your contact information.
- Consider including your region specific Marine and Family Programs Resource Guide
- Ask the URC/DRC to share your "Welcome Letter" in one of their newsletters and advertise your Social group and/or Social roster
- Let your personality show through in your writing ~ a more relaxed tone could be more welcoming and put your recipient at ease and help encourage them to join
- Consider putting a note at the bottom of your email encouraging recipients to send it along to new spouses and family members
  - Language to consider "Feel free to forward this along to anyone that you might like to join our group, ALL are Welcome!" (if this language applies)
- If overseas:
  - Ask if you can include the letter in the welcome package provided by the spouse's sponsor.
  - Before you leave, purchase a bunch of cards of all types (Birthday, Thank you, Thinking About You, Congratulations) at a Dollar Store ~ there is nothing quite like receiving mail overseas!
- Letters can be left on the recipient's front step, as an alternative to postal mail

**Resources**

- Welcome Letter Sample - for use in an email or mailed letters

## Social Media Connections
Social media can be a great space for making personal connections. Social media is also an excellent way for military spouses and families to maintain social networks as it provides a space to check in on and connect with familiar faces and places, even when we can't be physically present due to our ever-evolving military lifestyle.

Semper Connected and Marine and Family Programs have created a guidebook on "How To" set up social media pages for your military spouse and family groups.

**Resources**

- Best Practices for Social Media

## Best Practices
Now you've created a roster, let's make connections!

**Resources**

- Suggested Best Practices

## Ask An Expert
This section connects you to base specific resources and our support team.

**Connect to Resources**

**In Crisis?** Visit Military OneSource

Installation Help Guides (PDFs): 29 Palms, Albany, Barstow, Beaufort, Camp Lejeune, Camp Pendleton, Cherry Point, Hawaii, Henderson Hall, MCAS Iwakuni, Miramar, New River, Okinawa, Parris Island, Quantico, San Diego (MCRD), Yuma

- **Ask the Expert** - Ask questions (hqmc.upfrp@usmc.mil) here about resources, programs, how to use the toolkit and more! Questions will be answered Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm EST

## Frequently Asked Questions
**1. What is Semper Connected and how was it formed?**

During the COVID-19 pandemic, a group of spouses felt there was an even greater need for Marine Corps spouses and family members to connect.

**2. Who can use the Semper Connected toolkit?**

The Semper Connected toolkit is available for spouses, service members or family who would like to make social connections.

**3. How can I use the Semper Connected toolkit?**

You can use the toolkit to communicate with other spouses and family members by creating a social roster. Some ideas for creating social rosters include supper clubs, creating sports teams (kickball, softball, basketball, etc), book clubs, running clubs, playdates at the park, monthly dinners at the barracks and SO MUCH MORE!!!

**4. Is there training available for the Semper Connected Toolkit?**

Yes, we have created a short, 10-minute training video under the Training button. Additional assistance is available through the "Ask an Expert" email at hqmc.upfrp@usmc.mil or semperconnected@gmail.com. (Questions will be answered M-F 8:00-4:30 EST.)

**5. Is there a social media Semper Connected page?**

We've got you covered - join our Facebook page and stay updated on Semper Connected new developments.

**6. How can I invite spouses and family members in my unit to connect?**

The link to the Contact Information Google form can be shared several ways including posting it on your unit social media pages, hanging a flyer in the unit with the link to sign up specific unit or group, or whatever other creative ways you have to share information in your unit!

**7. What is the role of the Uniformed Readiness Coordinator (URC) or Deployment Readiness Coordinator (DRC) and Semper Connected?**

The URC/DRC can help spouses and family members get connected to resources. If a spouse or family member shares with another spouse that they could use support in a specific area (new baby, relationship management, child development, financial support, education, employment, etc) the spouse can provide a bridge to the URC or DRC in the unit.

**8. If I call a spouse or family member and they express that they could use some resources for an issue that they are having at home, what should I do?**

The URC/DRC can help spouses and family members get connected to resources. If a spouse or family member shares that they could use support in a specific area (new baby, relationship management, child development, financial support, education, employment, etc) the spouse can serve as a bridge to the URC or DRC in the unit or they can check out Help Guides at USMC-MCCS/help. By providing the phone number for the URC or DRC, and then following up later, spouses can make sure the issue was addressed.

**9. What happens if I am talking to someone and they express concern about the safety of themselves or someone else in the home?**

**In the event of an active emergency, spouses should call 911 for assistance**. Support can also be provided through the **Military Crisis Line at 800-273-8255 (24/7)**.

**10. How is my personal information stored and safeguarded?**

Contact and similar information is collected with permission from incoming spouses/family members by another spouse/family members within the unit. This information may be shared with other members of the Semper Connected team and will be used as a resource to support individual spouses/family members. The provision of contact and similar information is completely voluntary but is highly recommended; connection with, and support from other spouses/family members who understand the military lifestyle is the greatest resource! Personal information is collected and maintained in accordance with The Privacy Act of 1974; 10 U.S.C. 5013; Secretary of the Navy; 10 U.S.C. 5041, Headquarters, Marine Corps: function; composition; Marine Corps Order (MCO) 1754.6C, Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB); E.O. 9397 (SSN), as amended; and SORN M01754-5.

**11. If I want to be removed from Semper Connected, how do I request my removal?**

To unsubscribe, send an email to the Semper Connected spouse coordinator and include the word "Unsubscribe" in the Subject line.

Contact: Semper Connected (Ask an Expert)
Email: hqmc.upfrp@usmc.mil
Email: semperconnected@gmail.com
Hours (Questions answered):
- Monday-Friday: 8:00 AM - 4:30 PM EST

Contact: Military Crisis Line
Phone (24/7): 800-273-8255
In the event of an active emergency, call 911.

pages.title: Family Advocacy Program
pages.text:
# Family Advocacy Program

We help service members and their families foster strong and meaningful relationships through skill-building classes and workshops.

## Classes and Workshops
Classes and workshops are available through the Family Advocacy Program (FAP).

Register for classes and workshops by using the "Upcoming Events" calendar located on the FAP webpage.

Not all classes and workshops are available at all installations.

**Anger Management**

This eight-week course teaches life skills that help you manage your anger and identify the stress related triggers in the workplace, relationships, and other life situations.

- Stress
- Empathy
- Response
- Self-talk
- Assertiveness
- Expectations
- Forgiveness
- Time-out

**Grow Parenting**

This class offers eight sessions that help parents develop life skills in the following areas:

- Praise and Encouragement: How to communicate with your child in appropriate ways.
- Managing Emotions: Understand how to help your child manage his or her emotions.
- Healthy Lifestyles: Developing healthy routines and schedules in your home.
- Managing Stress: How to manage stress and your reactions due to anger.
- Physical Health: How to promote an active lifestyle for you and your child.

**POWER Workshop**

Discover the dynamics of power and control techniques and their negative effect on relationships. In this 8-hour workshop you will learn to recognize how those techniques can result in destructive and sometimes abusive behaviors.

- Enhance Communication
- Manage Stress
- Resolve Conflict

**Seven Principles for Making Marriage Work**

This one-day workshop is designed for relationships of all kinds, focused on communication, repair, and deeper understanding.

- Grow Stronger
- Feel Closer
- Build Healthier Connections

**Stress Management / Warrior Maintenance**

Discover what stress is and how it influences behavior in the workplace, relationships, and life's challenges.

**Within My Reach**

This workshop explores the dynamics of healthy relationships.

- Enhance Communication
- Manage Stress
- Resolve Conflict

## Problematic Sexual Behaviors in Child and Youth
Problematic Sexual Behaviors in Child & Youth (PSBCY) refers to behaviors initiated by children and youth under the age of 18 that involve sexual body parts (genitals, anus, buttocks, or breasts) in a manner that deviates from normative or typical sexual behavior and are developmentally inappropriate or potentially harmful to the individual initiating the behavior, the individual(s) impacted by the behavior or others.

Sexual behaviors initiated by a child or youth under the age of 18 are more likely to deviate from normative or typical sexual behavior and be developmentally inappropriate and/or potentially harmful when they are characterized by one or more of the following:

- Occur at a higher frequency than is typical given the child's or youth's age and development.
- Are preoccupying or are a greater focus of the child's or youth's interactions and interests than other behaviors.
- Interfere with the child's or youth's social development and/or general functioning.
- Do not respond to caregiver or other adult intervention.
- Involve sexual knowledge, language and/or behaviors that are inappropriate for the child's or youth's chronological or developmental age.
- Include aggression, force, threats, or coercion.
- Include intrusive sexual behavior, such as penetration.
- Are deliberative rather than spontaneous or exploratory in nature.
- Include alcohol or other mind-altering substances.
- Involve aggressive or violent pornography.
- Engender strong upset feelings in any other child or youth involved in the behaviors.
- Are non-mutual.

Problematic sexual behavior usually takes place when a child feels anxious or angry, is reacting to a traumatic experience, is overly curious after seeing sexual materials, is seeking attention, is trying to imitate others, or is merely trying to calm him or herself.

Parents, caregivers, educators, and professionals should approach problematic sexual behaviors with sensitivity and address them in a supportive and non-punitive manner.

Contact your local Family Advocacy for more information, support, and counseling.

## What is domestic abuse?
Domestic abuse is the use, attempted use, or threatened use of force or violence against an intimate partner. An intimate partner is a current or former spouse, a person with whom the abuser shares a child or common domicile, or a person who is in a romantic relationship with the abuser.

Examples of domestic abuse include, but are not limited to, taking your cell phone or keys, not allowing you to leave a location, controlling what you wear or who you speak to, limiting your access to money, name calling, pushing, hitting, sexual contact without your consent.

If you or someone you know is dealing with domestic abuse, contact the Family Advocacy office.

## Reporting Options
**Unrestricted**

A person who has experienced domestic abuse who wants to pursue an official investigation of an incident should report to their chain of command, the Family Advocacy Program (FAP), or law enforcement.

**Restricted**

Restricted reporting allows an adult who has experienced or is experiencing domestic abuse to disclose the details of their abuse and receive medical care, counseling, and FAP advocacy without command or law enforcement involvement. Those electing to make a restricted report must report the abuse to a FAP clinician, FAP advocate, and in some states a DoD healthcare provider.

pages.title: Child Development Centers
pages.text:
# Child Development Centers

We foster physical, cognitive, social, and emotional development in a safe and nurturing environment for children ages 6 weeks to 5 years.

## Getting Started Is Easy
Offering guidance and resources to simplify child care registration.

#### How to Get Started

Families seeking child care are required to submit their requests through [Military Child Care](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome) (MCC).

To initiate a request, families must first create an account with MilitaryChildCare.com, log in, and complete their household profile using the steps outlined in the link below.

[Create an Account](https://www.mcccentral.com/training-center/components/family-user-account-and-household-profile#801)

#### Forms

The following forms are required for registering for child care.

Filling out pdf forms while using a government computer can be limited and recommend using a personal computer.

Please contact your local CDC with any questions, difficulties, or concerns you may have.

• Child and Youth Programs Health Assessment
• Child and Youth Programs Registration Form
• CYP Non-Medicated Topical Products Form
• Application for Department of Defense Childcare Fees

Download the files and save them to a folder on your MAC or Windows computer. If you do not have Adobe Acrobat Reader, please visit [Adobe](https://get.adobe.com/reader/) to download it for free.

#### Request a Tour

Touring one of the Child Development Centers (CDCs) through Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) can be an enlightening and heartwarming experience.

Taking a tour will allow you to see the care and dedication that go into nurturing your children.

**Meet the Dedicated Staff**
The staff at the CDCs are highly trained and dedicated professionals who are passionate about early childhood education.

**Engaging Programs**
The centers offer a variety of age-appropriate programs and activities that cater to the unique needs and interests of each child.

**Safety and Security**
The safety and well-being of your children are top priority.

**Community Focus**
Visiting a CDC also provides insight into the strong sense of community among military families.

**Tours are not available at all locations. Contact your local CDC to schedule a tour.**

## Child Care Resources
Providing flexible child care solutions for families.

#### Full Time Child Care

**Curriculum:**
All CDCs use the Early Learning Matters (ELM) curriculum as the primary classroom curriculum.

• Whole child focus on skills that bolster school readiness and life success
• Developmentally sequenced activities that embed strategies for individualizing
• Evidence-informed, friendly-to-use resources for classroom staff and families

At the heart of the ELM curriculum are activity plans that build on children's pathways of development in five infant/toddler areas and eight preschool areas.

**Accreditation & Certification:**
CDCs are required to be nationally accredited and must pass an annual Department of Defense inspection to obtain a certificate to operate.

#### School Age Care

School Age Care (SAC) offers vital support to military families. To enroll your children into SAC visit the [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).

**Key Benefits:**

• **Safe and Structured Environment** - Provides a secure, supervised setting for children ages 5-12, ensuring peace of mind for parents during work hours and deployments.
• **Academic Support** - Offers homework assistance, tutoring, and educational activities to help children excel in school and develop lifelong learning habits.
• **Social Development** - Encourages children to build friendships, improve communication skills, and develop teamwork through group activities and games.
• **Resilience Building** - Promotes emotional well-being and adaptability by offering programs that help children manage the unique challenges of military life, such as frequent moves and parental deployments.
• **Recreational Activities** - Provides engaging, age-appropriate recreational activities that promote physical fitness, creativity, and exploration.
• **Support for Military Readiness** - Enables military parents to focus on their mission, knowing their children are in a supportive, enriching environment.
• **Affordable and Flexible Care Options** - Offers cost-effective programs tailored to the needs of military families, with flexible care schedules to accommodate varying work hours.
• **Connection to MCCS Resources** - Provides access to other MCCS programs, such as Family Advocacy, Youth Sports, and the Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP), ensuring comprehensive support for families.

School Age Care programs are designed to strengthen military families and help children thrive, fostering a sense of community and stability within the Marine Corps lifestyle.

## Family Support Resources
Connecting families to essential tools and resources.

#### PCS Workshop

The Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Workshop is designed to guide Marines and their families through every step of the relocation process.

**Nine reasons to attend a PCS Workshop:**

1. **Policy** - Per MCO 1754.10B, attending the PCS Workshop is required for a smooth transition to your new duty station.
2. **Installation-specific Information and Contacts** - Get valuable information about your new installation, including key contacts and local services.
3. **Household Goods Weight Allowances & Entitlements** - Learn about your weight allowances for household goods and what entitlements you can access during your move.
4. **Travel Allowances, Budget, and Government Card** - Understand your travel allowances, how to budget for the move, and how to use your government travel card.
5. **Moving with Pets** - Receive guidance on transporting pets, quarantine regulations, and other related requirements.
6. **School Liaison & Exceptional Family Member Program Resources** - Access support for school enrollment and resources for family members with special needs.
7. **Spouse Employment Opportunities** - Discover job search assistance and career development resources for spouses.
8. **Personalized Relocation Plan & Online Relocation Resources** - Create a customized relocation plan and explore online resources to streamline your move.
9. **Sponsorship** - As per MCO 1320.11H, learn how to request a sponsor to help you adjust and settle into your new duty station.

Don't move alone. Contact your Information, Referral, and Relocation specialist for PCS Workshop information.

#### School Liaison

The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools.

**School Liaison support includes:**

• **School Enrollment** - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
• **Local School Information** - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
• **Home School Information** - Assisting families with guidance on registering with the DoDEA schools.
• **Exceptional Family Member Support** - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services.
• **Transition Assistance** - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

These services help ensure that children receive the support they need for a successful educational experience in their new community.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://yuma.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison) webpage on the MCCS website.

#### Exceptional Family Member Program

The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP helps families navigate the challenges associated with relocating by connecting them to specialized services and community resources tailored to their unique circumstances.

**EFMP Services Available Include:**

• **Enrollment Assistance** - Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
• **Specialized Support Services** - Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
• **Transition Assistance** - Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
• **Advocacy and Resources** - Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
• **Workshops and Training** - Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting [EFMP](https://usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program).

#### Marine Corps Family Team Building

Eligibility for participation in the Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) programs extend to individuals across various segments of the military community.

• Active Duty Service Members: Including all branches of the military, all ranks.
• Department of Defense (DoD) Employees
• Spouses of Military Personnel

MCFTB is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

**How to get started with MCFTB:**

1. **Identify Individual Needs:** Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.
2. **Connect with MCFTB:** Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone.
3. **Attend Workshops and Classes:** Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation.
4. **Connect with Other Families:** Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms.

#### New Parent Support

New Parent Support offers guidance, education, and support to our Marines, their families throughout our military community. Eligible participants can access resources provided by New Parent Support.

**Eligible Participants:**

• Parents with children up to age 5
• DoD Spouses
• DoD Families

Connect with your New Parent Support office to begin your journey with our caring professionals.

#### Information, Referral, and Relocation

**Information, Referral, and Relocation (IR&R) services** to support Marines and their families through life's transitions, whether it's a Permanent Change of Station (PCS), deployment, or other major milestones.

**Key Services Provided:**

• **Welcome Aboard Brief** - Provides newcomers with essential information about their new installation, local community, and available resources.
• **Relocation Assistance** - Offers one-on-one support for PCS moves, including help with planning, moving tips, and checklists to ensure a smooth transition.
• **Requesting a Sponsor** - Connects Marines and their families with trained sponsors to provide personalized support and guidance during relocation.
• **Lending Locker** - Supplies temporary household items, such as kitchenware and small appliances, to help families settle in while awaiting their belongings.
• **Base Housing Support** - Offers guidance on housing options, including on-base housing, rental listings, and off-base accommodations.
• **DEERS and ID Card Assistance** - Provides information and support for enrolling in the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) and obtaining necessary ID cards.
• **Child Care and School Liaison Support** - Helps families find child care and connects them with School Liaison Officers for school registration and educational resources.
• **Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) Support** - Ensures families with special needs have access to tailored relocation assistance and resources at their new duty station.

**Benefits of IR&R Services**

• Reduces stress and uncertainty associated with frequent moves.
• Enhances readiness by ensuring families are well-informed and prepared.
• Strengthens connections within the Marine Corps community.
• Provides access to resources that promote resilience and stability.

Whether you're transitioning to a new duty station or looking for local resources, IR&R services are here to support you every step of the way.

**What ages does the Child Development Center serve?**
The Child Development Center provides child care to children from 6 weeks to 5 years old.

Fees are based on total family income and follow the Department of Defense fee structure.

The Child Development Center provides age-appropriate activities that promote cognitive, social, emotional, and physical development through a structured curriculum.

**Who should I contact if I have additional questions?**

# Family Child Care

We provide your child, aged 6 weeks to 12 years, with a nurturing environment, that supports their development and helps them thrive within the community.

## Getting Started is Easy
Navigating steps to successfully register for child care.

## Registration Guidance
Welcome to Family Child Care (FCC), where your child will learn, grow, and thrive in a safe and supportive environment.

Registration is quick and easy—simply follow the steps below.

1. **Go to** [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
   • Set up an account if you don't already have one.
   • Add your child's information and request care at your installation.
2. **Join the Waitlist**
   • If space is not immediately available, your child will be placed on a waitlist.
   • You will receive an offer via email to inform you when a spot opens up.
   • If you are placed on a waitlist you have the option of contacting [MCCYN](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome/mccyn) which provides fee assistance to offset the costs of community-based care.
3. **Accept the Offer**
   • Once you receive an offer, follow the instructions to accept it within the given timeframe.
   • If you don't respond within the timeframe, the offer is removed, but you may request reactivation with supporting details if eligible.
4. **Complete the Registration Process**
   • After accepting the offer, you will receive forms to complete.
   • Provide necessary documents, such as proof of eligibility, immunization records, and emergency contacts.
5. **Attend Parent Orientation**
   • You will be required to attend an orientation to review program policies and expectations.
6. **Start Care**
   • Once all paperwork is submitted and fees are processed, your child can begin attending the program.

If you need help getting started please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## Eligibility
Family Child Care (FCC) provides a safe, enriching environment for children while supporting the unique needs of military families. FCC providers establish their own schedules and may provide care outside standard work hours.

**Family Child Care is available to children of:**

• Active-duty Service Members
• DoD Civilian Employees
• Reservists
• DoD contractors.

**Children:**

• Must be between the ages of 6 weeks to 12 years old.

**Enrollment:**

• Enrollment is guided by DoD priorities. Supplanting does not apply to FCC. To secure a spot, families are encouraged to register early, as availability may vary depending on demand.

**Department of Defense Polocies:**

• DoDI 6060.02
• MCO 1710.30A

For more information on eligibility, priority placement, and registration requirements, please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## MilitaryChildCare.com
MilitaryChildCare.com makes it easy to find and request Family Child Care (FCC), giving you peace of mind knowing your child is in a safe and supportive environment.

With just one online account, you can explore program options, submit a request, and manage your childcare needs from anywhere. Spaces are assigned based on DoD priority placement, so registering early ensures you have the best chance of securing care when you need it.

Start today by visiting [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome).

## Child Care Support
Exploring child care opportunities.

## I Need Child Care
Family Child Care is a great child care choice offered right in your community.

**Flexible, Home-Based Child Care for Your Family**

Family Child Care (FCC) offers a safe, nurturing, and home-like environment for children ages 6 weeks to 12 years. With small group sizes and flexible hours, FCC provides personalized care that fits your family's schedule, including full-time, part-time, evening, and weekend options.

**Eligibility & Requirements:**

Family Child Care (FCC) is designed to support military families by providing high-quality, home-based child care. Eligibility is based on priority and availability.

• Active-Duty Service Members
• Department of Defense (DoD) Civilians
• Reservists & National Guard Members
• Retirees
• DoD Contractors

To ensure a safe and developmentally appropriate environment, children enrolled in the Family Child Care (FCC) program must meet the following requirements:

**Age Requirements**

• Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old to enroll in FCC.
• School-age children (up to 12 years) may attend before/after school care, full-day care during school breaks, and summer programs.

**Health & Immunization Requirements**

• All children must have up-to-date immunization records, including age-appropriate vaccines as required by DoD and state regulations.

**Special Needs & Accommodations**

• The CYP behavior specialist, CYP nurse, and FCC providers work together to assess and accommodate children with special needs.
• Parents must disclose any medical, developmental, or dietary requirements during registration to ensure proper care and support.

If you have any question please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## I Want to Provide Child Care
As an Family Child Care provider, you'll offer safe, high-quality care for military children while enjoying flexible hours, professional training, and the ability to care for your own children at home. MCCS provides free training, support, and resources to help you succeed.

Start your journey today—make a difference in the lives of military families while building your own career!

**Why Become an FCC Provider?**

• Run your own home-based business while supporting military families.
• Enjoy flexible hours and the ability to care for your own children at home.
• Receive training and support at no cost, including CPR, First Aid, and child development courses.
• Gain access to resources and equipment, including a lending library of toys and materials.
• Participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program to receive meal reimbursements.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

• Must be at least 18 years old.
• Have a high school diploma or equivalent.
• Reside in government housing or approved off-base housing.
• Pass a comprehensive background check for all household members over 18.
• Complete a health screening for yourself and any family members who will be in the home.

**Steps to Get Started:**

1. Contact your local Family Child Care office to learn more about the application process and training requirements.
2. Download and complete the FCC Application or obtain it from the Resource and Referral office. Applicaton requires background checks.
3. Complete a family interview (provider applicant and spouse)
4. If interested in processing with the certification process, background checks are initiated.
5. Pay a non-refundable $50 training fee at Family Child Care office which covers the cost of the CPR/First Aid training. _Training fees are not required at all locations. Contact the Resource and Referral office about training fees._
6. Attend FCC Provider initial training - 40-hours (one-week)
7. Complete health requirements for all household members,
8. Set up home in accordance with regulatory requirements.
9. Home inspection by Fire, Safety & Sanitation.
10. Quality Review Board.
11. Documentation sent to SJA regarding successfully completion of requirements (to obtain authorization to operate a home business).
12. (Upon SJA approval) Provider files Housing Addendum, notifying Family Housing of FCC business
13. Purchase Liability Insurance.
14. Upon clearance to start, Resource & Referral will assist in setting up provider's profile on [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/)
15. Final walk-through by FCC staff.
16. Open for business!
17. Be committed to attending ongoing training sessions to guarantee the highest quality of care for children.

Homes should obtain certification from the command if they provide more than 10 "child care hours" per week. For instance, if a resident looks after two children for five hours, it amounts to 10 hours of child care. Detailed information can be found on page 6 of the Resident handbook.

The FCC program is not only about providing care but also about ensuring that the caregivers are well-trained, certified, and provide a safe and nurturing environment for the children. The command plays an active role in monitoring and certifying providers, ensuring the best care for the children enrolled in the FCC program.

If you have any questions please contact our Resource and Referral office.

[Schedule Virtual Info Session](https://eventactions.com/eareg.aspx?ea=Rsvp&invite=0gfhg4nvd1jc3t5rsk88a07md5n4fb0mx83w16dw3h05hfb1szca)

## Life Skill-building Resources
Developing essential skills for personal and professional growth.

## School Liaison
The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools.

School Liaison support include:

• **School Enrollment** - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
• **Local School Information** - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
• **Home School Information** - Assisting families with guidance on their local school district homeschool requirements.
• **Special Education Support** - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services to include warm hand offs to EFMP.
• **Transition Assistance** - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

For more information about support and services, visit the School Liaison webpage on the MCCS website.

## Exceptional Family Member Program
The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP Services Available Include:

## Budgeting Your Child Care
The professionals at Personal Financial Management can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

## Marine Corps Family Team Building
Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

How to get started with MCFTB:

• **Identify Individual Needs** - Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.
• **Connect with MCFTB** - Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone.
• **Attend Workshops and Classes** - Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation.
• **Connect with Other Families** - Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms.

## Libraries
The Library is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

• **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
• **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
• **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
• **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
• **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Visit the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org/).

## Guiding Growth & Resilience
Community Counseling provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**Who can become a Family Child Care provider?**
Any military spouse or eligible individual 18 years or older who lives in base housing or approved off-base housing can apply. Providers must complete training, background checks, and home inspections to become licensed.

**What are the benefits of becoming an FCC provider?**
FCC providers run their own home-based business, set their own hours, care for their own children while earning income, receive free training and resources, and participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program.

**What are the requirements for enrolling a child in FCC?**
Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old, have up-to-date immunizations, and meet health and safety requirements. Families must register through MilitaryChildCare.com or their local Resource & Referral (R&R) office.

**How is Family Child Care different from a Child Development Center (CDC)?**
FCC provides home-based care in smaller groups, offering more personalized attention, flexible hours, and a family-like setting compared to larger Child Development Centers (CDCs).

**How do I find an FCC provider for my child?**
Parents can search for available FCC providers and request care through MilitaryChildCare.com or contact their local FCC office or Resource & Referral (R&R) office for assistance.
