# MCCS School Age Care

We offer a safe, engaging environment for children ages 5-12, providing homework assistance, recreational activities, and social development opportunities to support their growth and well-being.

## Getting Started is Easy
Learn about eligibility and registration.

## Registration Guidance
Welcome to School Age Care (SAC), where your child will learn, grow, and thrive in a safe and supportive environment.

Registration is quick and easy—simply follow the steps below.

1. **Go to** [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
   • Set up an account if you don't already have one.
   • Add your child's information and request care at your installation.
2. **Join the Waitlist**
   • If space is not immediately available, your child will be placed on a waitlist.
   • You will receive an offer when a spot opens up.
   • If you are placed on a waitlist you have the option of contacting [MCCYN](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome/mccyn) which provides fee assistance to offset the costs of community-based care.
3. **Accept the Offer**
   • Once you receive an offer, follow the instructions to accept it within the given timeframe.
   • If you don't respond within the timeframe, the offer is removed, but you may request reactivation with supporting details if eligible.
4. **Complete the Registration Process**
   • After accepting the offer, you will receive forms to complete.
   • Provide necessary documents, such as proof of eligibility, Flu shot records, and emergency contacts.
5. **Attend Parent Orientation**
   • You may be required to attend an orientation to review program policies and expectations.
6. **Start Care**
   • Once all paperwork is submitted and fees are processed, your child can begin attending the program.

If you need help, contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Eligibility
School Age Care (SAC) is designed to provide a safe, enriching environment for children while supporting the unique needs of military families.

**School Age Care is available to children of:**

**Children:**

• Must be between the ages of 5 and 12 years old
• Enrolled in Kindergarten through 6th grade to participate in the program.

**Enrollment:**

• Enrollment is guided by DoD priorities. To secure a spot, families are encouraged to register early, as availability may vary depending on demand.

**Department of Defense Policies:**

• DoDI 6060.02
• MCO 1710.30A

For more information on eligibility, priority placement, and registration requirements, contact the Resource and Referral office.

## MilitaryChildCare.com
MilitaryChildCare.com makes it easy to find and request School Age Care (SAC), giving you peace of mind knowing your child is in a safe and supportive environment.

With just one online account, you can explore program options, submit a request, and manage your childcare needs from anywhere.

## School Age Care Support
Providing child care for the military community.

## Curriculum Focus
School Age Care (SAC) is designed to provide a safe, engaging, and enriching environment that helps children grow academically, socially, and emotionally.

• **Character & Leadership Development** - Encouraging responsibility, teamwork, and leadership skills to help children build confidence and a sense of community.
• **Education & Career Development** - Providing opportunities for hands-on learning, homework support, and activities that spark curiosity and future career interests.
• **Health & Life Skills** - Teaching the importance of healthy habits, personal responsibility, and essential life skills to promote long-term well-being.
• **The Arts** - Fostering creativity and self-expression through music, dance, visual arts, and drama.
• **Sports, Fitness & Recreation** - Promoting physical activity and teamwork through structured sports and recreational games.
• **Technology** - Offering STEM-based activities that introduce children to coding, robotics, and problem-solving in a fun, interactive way.

Our program follows nationally recognized standards and is affiliated with the Boys & Girls Clubs of America (BGCA) to ensure high-quality experiences that support the overall well-being of children.

By participating in the School Age Care, your child will gain valuable skills, make lasting friendships, and enjoy a supportive environment that helps them thrive.

If you have any questions about the curriculum please contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Meals Provided
School Age Care (SAC) ensures your child will enjoy balanced, nutritious meals and snacks that keep them energized and ready to learn, play, and grow.

**What's Included?**

• **Before & After School Care** - A nutritious breakfast and an afternoon snack are provided.
• **Early Release / Teacher Workdays / School Breaks** - Breakfast, lunch, and an afternoon snack are included.

**Special Dietary Needs**
Inform School Age Care staff of any food allergies or dietary requirements during registration.

**Encouraging Healthy Eating**
Our meals follow USDA nutritional guidelines, ensuring a well-balanced diet with a focus on fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and protein.

Meals offered can vary by location, check with the School Age Care center for details.

[USDA Non-Discrimination Statement](https://www.usda.gov/non-discrimination-statement)

For more information about meals offered and dietary accommodation requirements, please contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Transportation
School Age Care (SAC) provides safe and dependable transportation to help your child get to and from care with ease.

**What's Included?**

• **On-Base Schools** - Transportation is typically provided for children attending schools located on the installation.
• **Off-Base Schools** - Availability of transportation for off-base schools varies by location.
• **Field Trips & Special Activities** - During school breaks and summer camp, supervised transportation is provided for planned excursions and enrichment activities.

**Parent Responsibilities**
If your child attends a school that is not part of the SAC transportation service, you will need to arrange their drop-off and pick-up.

**Safety First**
Our transportation services follow strict safety guidelines, and all vehicles are operated by trained professionals.

Not all installations provide transportation.

## Youth Connections
Youth Connections is designed to help children adjust, make friends, and feel comfortable in their new community. Whether your family is new to the installation or transitioning from another program, we ensure your child feels welcome and supported from day one at School Age Care (SAC).

**How it works:**

• **Peer Support** - When a new child joins the program, they are paired with a friendly and experienced SAC ambassador—a peer who helps them navigate their new environment.
• **Guided Introductions** - The ambassador introduces them to other children, explains daily routines, and helps them feel included in activities.
• **Building Connections** - Through shared activities, games, and team projects, new children quickly become part of the SAC community.

**Why It Matters**

• **Reduces Anxiety** - Having a familiar face and a peer to guide them makes the transition easier and less overwhelming.
• **Encourages Friendships** - Children develop friendships faster when they have someone to introduce them to others.
• **Promotes Leadership** - SAC ambassadors take pride in their role, learning valuable leadership and mentoring skills.

**Becoming a SAC Ambassador**

• Children who have been in the program for a while and show leadership, kindness, and responsibility may be invited to become an ambassador.
• SAC ambassadors receive guidance on how to support new peers and foster a welcoming environment.
• Youth Connection helps children feel confident, connected, and ready to enjoy their time in School Age Care.

If your child is new or interested in becoming part of Youth Connections, talk to the SAC team to learn more!

## Parent Orientation
Parent Orientation is an essential step in ensuring a smooth and positive experience for both you and your child in School Age Care (SAC).

**What to Expect in Parent Orientation**
During the orientation, you will:

• **Learn About Program Policies & Expectations** - Review SAC guidelines on pick-up and drop-off procedures, behavior expectations, and communication with staff.
• **Understand Safety & Emergency Procedures** - Learn how SAC ensures your child's safety, including emergency plans, health protocols, and supervision standards.
• **Review Meals & Nutrition** - Get details about meal schedules, snack options, and dietary restrictions or allergies.
• **Meet SAC Staff & Ask Questions** - Connect with the SAC professionals, program directors, and support staff who will be working with your child every day.
• **Complete Required Paperwork** - Ensure all necessary forms, including medical information and emergency contacts, are finalized before your child starts care.

**Why Parent Orientation is Important**

• Helps you understand how the program operates and what is expected of both parents and children.
• Gives you a chance to meet the staff and ask any questions before your child's first day.
• Ensures a smooth transition, setting your child up for success in the SAC environment.

Attending Parent Orientation is the best way to get familiar with the program and feel confident that your child is in a safe, structured, and supportive environment.

If you have any questions or need to schedule your orientation, please contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Supporting Children with Special Needs
School Age Care (SAC) is committed to providing a supportive and enriching environment for all children.

**How We Support**

• We work closely with families to understand each child's specific needs.

**Trained & Caring Staff**

• Our staff members receive specialized training on working with children with various needs, including strategies for positive behavior support, communication techniques, and safety protocols.
• We collaborate with the family, SAC nurses, and SAC behavior specialists to provide the best care possible.

**Adaptive Activities & Programming**

• Activities are adapted, allowing all children to participate in a way that meets their needs.
• We foster a welcoming environment where all children feel valued and included.

**Facility Accessibility & Safety Measures**

• SAC facilities are designed to accommodate children with physical, sensory, or developmental challenges.
• Emergency preparedness plans consider the needs of all children, ensuring a safe environment.

**Ongoing Communication & Family Collaboration**

• School Age Care professionals communicate directly with parents to ensure the best experience for their child.
• Adjustments and accommodations can be made as needed to support each child's development and well-being.

**How to Request Accommodations**

• During the registration process, inform SAC staff that your child has special needs.
• Complete required Child & Youth documentations.
• Provide relevant documentation or recommendations from medical providers, or therapists if applicable.
• Work with SAC staff to develop a support plan that best supports your child's needs.

At School Age Care, we provide high-quality care that promotes positive outcomes in all areas of children's development.

## Seasonal Camps
Seasonal camps provide a safe, engaging environment where children ages 5-12 can explore new interests, build friendships, and develop essential life skills.

View the upcoming camps listed in our calendar or contact the Resource and Referral office.

## School Liaison
The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families.

**School Liaison support include:**

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://yuma.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison).

## Life Skill-building Resources
Learn additional life skills that support you and your family.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

**How to get started with MCFTB:**

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

## Exceptional Family Members
The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is dedicated to supporting military families by ensuring they have access to the resources and services needed to thrive. We understand that navigating military life with a family member who has special needs can be challenging, which is why EFMP works closely with the School Liaison Program to provide seamless support for educational transitions, school advocacy, and special education resources.

**How EFMP Supports Families:**

• **Lending Library** – Borrow sensory tools, assistive devices, and educational materials to support learning and development at home.
• **Respite Care Services** – Provides temporary relief for caregivers, ensuring they have time to recharge while their loved one receives quality care.
• **Assignment Coordination** – Ensures that families are stationed at locations with appropriate medical and educational services for their exceptional family members.
• **Advocacy & Support** – Assists families in navigating the special education system, including IEPs (Individualized Education Programs).
• **Workshops & Resources** – Offers educational sessions on topics like navigating the EFMP process, advocacy skills, and community resources.

By working together, EFMP and the School Liaison help ensure that your child receives the support they need—at home, in school, and throughout their military journey.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

• Blended Retirement System (BRS)
• Car Buying
• Consumer Awareness
• Continuation Pay
• Couple Financial Counseling
• Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis
• Saving and Investing
• Credit / Debt Management
• Developing a Spending Plan
• Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
• Individual Financial Counseling
• Major Purchases
• Military Pay & Benefits
• Retirement Planning
• Survivor Benefits Plan
• Thrift Savings Plan
• Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**Who is eligible for School Age Care?**
Children ages 5-12 who are enrolled in kindergarten through 6th grade are eligible.

**How do I register my child for care?**
Register online at [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://www.militarychildcare.com) and follow the steps to request care.

**Is there a waitlist for School Age Care?**
Yes, if no spots are available, your child will be placed on a waitlist, and you will be notified when a spot opens.

**What are the program hours?**
Hours vary by location but typically include before and after school care, full-day care on school breaks, and summer camp.

**Does School Age Care provide meals?**
Breakfast and snacks are provided on school days; lunch may be required on certain days, such as teacher workdays or school breaks.

Contact: Stone Street Youth Pavilion (details on https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/child-development-centers)

Contact: Tarawa Terrace Youth Pavilion (details on https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/child-development-centers)

# MCCS School Liaison

We support military families by prioritizing the educational needs of their children, providing resources, and ensuring smooth transitions between schools.

## Connect with a School Liaison
Getting connected is easy.

## Eligibility
Members of our military community with school-aged children (PreK-12) are eligible to access the services provided by the School Liaison Program.

• Active-duty Service Members
• DoD Civilian
• National Guard
• Reserves
• Retirees

## Getting Started
Figuring out schools during a move or facing school-related questions can be tough, but you don't have to do it alone.

**Contact the School Liaison**
Reach out to your local School Liaison office for personalized support.

**Schedule a Consultation**
Set up a meeting or phone call with the School Liaison to discuss your child's needs, school options, and any concerns you may have regarding the transition.

**Collect Important Documents**
Maintain important records, such as school transcripts, report cards, individual education plans (IEPs), and any other documentation that will assist the School Liaison in supporting your family.

**Learn About Local School Options**
The School Liaison can provide details on the local school districts, private schools, charter schools, homeschooling, and other alternative education options to help you make an informed decision.

**Explore Available Resources**
The School Liaison can direct you to resources such as tutoring services, scholoarships, extracurricular activities, and other programs.

**Stay Connected**
Maintain communication with the School Liaison throughout your assignment to receive ongoing support and updates on educational opportunities for your child.

Don't hesitate to contact your School Liaison, who is ready to support your family's educational journey!

## School Liaisons
School Liaison Officers help to navigate the challenges of school transitions, ensuring access to quality education, and providing valuable support for your children's academic success.

## Our Support
The School Liaison will provide you with important information, assist with enrollment, navigate grade and credit transfers, and ensure that your child receives support to connect to their new environment.

Empowering you with the information you need, they ensure you can make informed decisions about your child's education and be their strongest advocate.

Your School Liaison is the critical link between families, commands, communities, and schools.

• Promotes and enhances education services and programs.
• Provides incoming families with information regarding Local Education Agencies.
• Leverage the Interstate Compact and assist with grade/credit transferability.
• Ensure children/youth and LEAs are supported by military community.
• Facilitate command sponsored Adopt-a-School opportunities.

## Resources for Military Families
Additional services to strengthen and support military families.

## Adjusting to Changes
Moving to a new duty station can be challenging for military families, especially for children adjusting to a new school and environment.

Community Counseling provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling.

Life Skills Development Resources:

## Budgeting for Your Move
Personal Financial Management is here to support your military family during your move to another duty station. From budgeting for relocation expenses to understanding allowances, and managing housing costs, our experts provide guidance to help you stay financially secure throughout your transition.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

• **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
• **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
• **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
• **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
• **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration.

## Before & After School Care
School Age Care (SAC) programs support your military family with after-school care, learning opportunities in a safe environment.

**School Age Care (SAC)**
SAC offers child care for kids in kindergarten through age 12, giving them a structured and fun environment when they're not in school.

• **After-School Support** – Your child will have a safe place to go before and after school, during holidays, and over the summer.
• **Educational Services** – SAC provides homework help, tutoring, and learning activities that support what your child is doing in school.
• **Support for Military Families** – If your schedule changes due to training or deployment, SAC offers flexible hours so your child always has consistent care.

Register for School Age Care at MilitaryChildCare.com.

How EFMP Supports Families:

## Family Child Care
Family Child Care (FCC) gives you in-home child care from trained and certified providers, often military spouses, in military housing.

• **Home-Based Care** – Your child will be cared for in a safe, nurturing home setting with small group sizes and personalized attention.
• **Educational Activities** – FCC providers include age-appropriate learning, playtime, and rest in their daily schedules, helping your child grow and develop.
• **Flexible Child Care** – Whether you need full-time, part-time, or overnight care, FCC providers can work with your schedule, making it easier to handle deployments or unpredictable work hours.

## Information, Referral, and Relocation
Moving to a new duty station can be overwhelming, but you don't have to navigate it alone. Information, Referral, and Relocation (IR&R) services are here to help you and your family transition smoothly and feel at home in your new community.

**Here's how IR&R can support you:**

• **Relocation Assistance** – Get guidance on housing, base services, child care, and community resources to establish stability for your family.
• **Local School Information** – Connect you to the School Liaison, educational resources, enrollment requirements, and district policies to ensure a smooth school transition.
• **Welcome Aboard Resources** – Access newcomer checklists, area guides, and personalized referrals to help you get familiar with your new surroundings.
• **Lending Locker** – Borrow temporary household items to make settling in easier while you wait for your belongings to arrive.

Wherever your journey takes you, IR&R is here to provide the information and resources you need to make your transition as smooth as possible.

How to get started with MCFTB:

1. Identify Individual Needs: Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.
2. Connect with MCFTB: Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone.
3. Attend Workshops and Classes: Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation.
4. Connect with Other Families: Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms.

## FAQs
Find information and get quick answers to common questions.

**What does the School Liaison do?**
The program helps military families navigate the education system and assists with school transitions, special education services, and local school information.

**Who can use the School Liaison?**
The program is available to active-duty military families, National Guard and Reserve members on active orders, DoD civilians, and retired service members with school-aged children, whether families live on or off base.

**How can the School Liaison help during a PCS move?**
School Liaisons provide resources for enrolling in new schools, transferring credits, and ensuring a smooth transition.

**What educational resources are available through the School Liaison?**
School Liaisons provide access to resources such as tutoring, special education information, and connections to homeschooling or virtual school options.

**Can the School Liaison assist with special education needs?**
Yes, School Liaisons can help families understand the special education process, connect with local resources, and support children with IEPs (Individualized Education Programs) or 504 Plans.

**Can School Liaisons help with college readiness?**
Yes, School Liaisons provide resources for college planning, scholarships, and navigating the college admissions process.

**Do School Liaisons only work with DoDEA schools?**
No, School Liaisons support families regardless of whether their children attend public, private, DoDEA schools, or homeschool families.

## Contact Information and Resources

pages.text:
# Information, Referral, and Relocation

We connect service members and their families to valuable resources, helping them successfully navigate their military journey.

## Welcome Aboard
Helping you navigate relocation and connect to your community.

#### Welcome Aboard Brief

Discover essential information and resources to help you and your family adjust smoothly to life at your new duty station.

**Topics discussed will include:**

• Base Services and Amenities - Overview of essential services, such as medical facilities, commissary, exchange, and fitness centers.
• Relocation Assistance - Guidance on housing, transportation, and accessing resources through the Relocation Assistance Program (RAP).
• Childcare and School Information - Details on childcare options, school enrollment, and youth programs to support your family.
• Sponsorship and Family Readiness - Introduction to the Sponsorship Program and Family Readiness Officers (FRO) for ongoing support and connection to your new community.
• Local Area Orientation - Information on local attractions, shopping, dining, and community activities to help you settle in and explore your new surroundings.

View the event calendar for scheduled Welcome Aboard Briefs or reach out to the Information, Referral, and Relocation office for availability and registration.

## Your MCCS Connection
Welcome to the MCCS Enterprise Website!

Discover:

• Career and Education Resources
• Family Support Services
• Fitness, Recreation, and Leisure Programs
• Financial Management Tools
• And much more!

Explore [MCCS](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/) now.

## Permanent Change of Station (PCS)
Providing resources and support for your PCS journey.

## PCS Workshop
The Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Workshop is designed to guide Marines and their families through every step of the relocation process.

**Nine reasons to attend a PCS Workshop:**

1. It's Mandatory - Per MCO 1754.10B, attending the PCS Workshop is required for a smooth transition to your new duty station.
2. Installation-Specific Information and Contacts - Get valuable information about your new installation, including key contacts and local services.
3. Household Goods Weight Allowances & Entitlements - Learn about your weight allowances for household goods and what entitlements you can access during your move.
4. Travel Allowances, Budget, and Government Card - Understand your travel allowances, how to budget for the move, and how to use your government travel card.
5. Moving with Pets - Receive guidance on transporting pets, quarantine regulations, and other related requirements.
6. School Liaison & Exceptional Family Member Program Resources - Access support for school enrollment and resources for family members with special needs.
7. Spouse Employment Opportunities - Discover job search assistance and career development resources for spouses.
8. Personalized Relocation Plan & Online Relocation Resources - Create a customized relocation plan and explore online resources to streamline your move.
9. Request a Sponsor - As per MCO 1320.11H, learn how to request a sponsor to help you adjust and settle into your new duty station.

Don't move alone. Contact your Information, Referral, and Relocation specialist to schedule your appointment today.

## Relocation Assistance
Relocation Assistance is designed to help make your move as smooth as possible, offering a variety of services to support Marines and their families during the transition to a new duty station.

Relocation support includes:

• Housing - Get help finding on-base or off-base housing, temporary lodging, and understanding your options.
• Local Area Information - Access guides and insights on the local community, including schools, healthcare, and recreational activities.
• PCS Workshops - Attend workshops covering the entire relocation process.
• Request a Sponsor - Connecting with a sponsor at your new installation is an important step for a successful transition.
• Lending Locker Access - Borrow essential household items like kitchenware and small appliances while waiting for your household goods to arrive.

## Request a Sponsor
Connecting with your sponsor prior to your PCS move is an important step for a successful transition. Your sponsor is here to guide you through the challenges of relocation and help you integrate into your new community.

Sponsors support includes:

• Personalized Guidance - Receive tailored advice on housing, transportation, and base services.
• Quick Access to Resources - Get connected to key resources such as medical facilities, childcare, and recreation centers.
• Streamlined PCS Process - Navigate administrative tasks, like check-ins and paperwork, more efficiently.
• Support Network - Build connections within the base and local community, reducing the stress of transitioning to a new environment.

Request a sponsor by submitting the Sponsorship Request Form to the Information, Referral, and Relocation office.

## Explore Housing Options
Connecting you with housing and your military community.

## Base Housing
Base housing offers Marines and their families a comfortable and supportive living environment, making the transition to a new duty station smoother and more manageable.

**Important steps to securing base housing:**

1. Apply Early - Start the housing application process as soon as you receive your Permanent Change of Station (PCS) orders to secure your spot on the waiting list. Contact the housing office within 72 hours of arriving at your new installation.
2. Gather Required Documents - Prepare necessary documentation, including your PCS orders, ID, and any other relevant paperwork required by the housing office.
3. Contact the Housing Offices - Reach out to the base housing office for information on available units, policies, and specific requirements.
4. Schedule a Housing Inspection - Once assigned a unit, arrange for an inspection to ensure it meets your family's needs and is ready for occupancy.
5. Plan Your Move - Coordinate your moving logistics, including transportation of your household goods and any temporary lodging if needed.

Taking these steps will help ensure a smooth transition into base housing, allowing you and your family to settle in quickly and enjoy your new community.

Contact the Information, Referral, and Relocation for more information about housing at your new location.

## Support for Service Members and Families
Exploring resources and tools to help you and your family thrive.

## Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS)
Connecting to the [Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System](https://milconnect.dmdc.osd.mil/milconnect/) (DEERS) office is important for Marines and their families to ensure they receive the military benefits and services. The DEERS office provides support for enrollment and updates, helping to maintain accurate records for eligibility.

Support includes:

• Enrollment and Updates - Assistance with enrolling in DEERS and updating personal information such as address, marital status, and dependent information.
• ID Card Issuance - Issuance and renewal of military ID cards for service members and their eligible family members.
• Benefits Verification - Confirmation of eligibility for healthcare, education, and other military benefits.
• TRICARE Enrollment - Guidance on enrolling in TRICARE for healthcare coverage and accessing medical services.

Connecting with the DEERS office ensures that you and your family can effectively access and manage your military benefits.

## Child Care
Child Care services are essential for Marines and their families new to an installation, providing a safe and nurturing environment for children while offering crucial support to parents during their transition.

The following services are designed to support your family's needs, helping your children thrive in their new environment.

Child Care services available include:

• Child Development Centers (CDC) - Full-day care for infants and preschool-aged children, promoting early learning and development.
• Family Child Care (FCC) - Home-based care options that offer personalized attention in a family-like setting.
• Before and After School Programs - Supervised care for school-aged children, ensuring they have a safe place during non-school hours.
• New Parent Support Program (NPSP) - Resources and guidance for new parents, including home visits, parenting classes, and workshops.

Visit [militarychildcare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome) to enroll your child into one of the Child Development Centers.

When registering make sure you have your children(s) updated immunization records available.

School Liaison support include:

• School Enrollment - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
• Local School Information - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
• Home School Information - Assisting families with guidance on registering with the DoDEA schools.
• Exceptional Family Member Support - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services.
• Transition Assistance - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

EFMP Services Available Include:

• Enrollment Assistance - Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
• Specialized Support Services - Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
• Transition Assistance - Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
• Advocacy and Resources - Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
• Workshops and Training - Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting EFMP.

## Budgeting Your Move
The professionals at Personal Financial Management can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

## Lending Locker
The Lending Locker is an invaluable resource for Marines and their families, offering essential household items to borrow temporarily while awaiting the arrival of personal belongings during a relocation.

Available Items _May_ Include:

• Kitchenware (pots, pans, dishes, utensils)
• Small appliances (microwaves, toasters, coffee makers)

Take advantage of the Lending Locker to help make your move as seamless as possible!

_Not all items are available at all locations._

Contact the Information, Referral, and Relocation office to learn more about the Lending Locker.

## Family Member Travel Screening Cell
One of the most challenging parts of moving overseas is the suitability screening process – it can be confusing and complex. The Family Member Travel Screening Cell helps Marines and families successfully navigate the screening process by providing proactive support throughout the process.

Support includes:

• Providing detailed information on the screening process.
• Connecting Marines and families with the appropriate medical screening office.
• Ensuring the timely initiation and completion of screening.
• Resolving issues with medical screening offices.
• Offering transparency of screening status for Marines, families, monitors, and commands.
• Training and assisting commands in their screening-related roles.

For assistance, send an email to SMB_HQMC_FMTS@usmc.mil.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**What services does the Information, Referral, and Relocation program provide?**
The program helps connect Marines and their families to valuable resources that include housing, relocation, childcare, schools, and access to community resources.

**How can I request a sponsor for my move?**
You can request a sponsor by contacting the program directly or through your unit's command, and we will match you with a Sponsor.

**What should I do if I need temporary lodging during my move?**
You can access temporary lodging options through our program, which can provide a comfortable place to stay while you secure permanent housing.

**Are there resources available for spouses seeking employment at my new duty station?**
Yes, the Family Member Employment Assistance offers employment resources for spouses, including job search assistance, resume writing support, and networking opportunities.

**How do I update my DEERS information after relocating?**
You can update your DEERS information by visiting the ID Card Center or using the online [ID Card Office Online](https://idco.dmdc.osd.mil/idco/) portal to ensure your benefits remain active.

# Libraries

We enrich the lives of our military community by fostering opportunities for connection and providing equitable access to knowledge, innovation, and creativity.

## Eligibility & Getting Started
#### Access Requirements

We welcome all eligible members of our military community.

The Library services extend to individuals across various sections of the military community.

• Active-Duty Service Members
• Dependent Children
• Dependent Spouses
• DoD Civilians
• DoD Families
• Host Nation Staff Members
• Medal of Honor Recipients
• National Guard
• Reservists
• Retirees
• 100% Disabled Veterans

These are generalized categories; eligibility per [DoDI 1015.10](https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/101510p.pdf). Additional eligibility categories are determined per the installation commander.

#### New to the Library?

Get started and explore your library today!

1. **Visit and Explore the Library** - Discover all the resources the library has to offer through our selection of books, digital media, innovative makerspaces, computers for adults and children, interactive programs, and more!
2. **Bring Identification** - Make sure you can provide the proper identification that verifies your eligibility for access to the library, such as a military ID card or dependent ID card.
3. **Library Account** - Create an account in-person at your local library, or start using virtual library resources now at [dodmwrlibraries.org](https://dodmwrlibraries.org/). Search, reserve, and manage your account at [milrec.bibliovation.com](https://milrec.bibliovation.com/).
4. **Ask Questions** - Don't hesitate to ask library staff if you have any questions about your account or available resources.

#### Guidelines and Rules

Help us maintain a space for shared learning and enjoyment.

• We want to provide a safe recreation and learning environment for our Marines and families.
• Library accounts are free for authorized users and can be obtained at the library using your official DoD ID card.
• Your Library account or DoD ID is required to check out materials and use the library's services.
• Most materials can be checked out for three weeks. Overdue notices will be sent first to the user's e-mail.
• Renew borrowed items online through our website or by contacting the library.
• Children are always welcome at the library. Children under ten years of age may not be left unattended.
• Tobacco products are not allowed within the library.

Library Policies
• [Marine Corps Order: 1700.33](https://www.marines.mil/News/Publications/MCPEL/Electronic-Library-Display/Article/900492/mco-170033/)
• Department of Defense Instruction: 1015.10

#### Borrowing Policy

Enjoy books, DVDs, video games and more!

• All materials borrowed from Marine Corps MWR General Libraries are for 3-week check outs.
• Unlimited Books
• DVDs Limit: 10 per family
• Audio Books Limit: 10 per family
• Playaways Limit: 2 per family
• Video Games Limit: 2 per family
• Library of Things/Boardgames/Equipment: Check with your local library for availability.
• Items may be renewed twice as long as an item has not been requested by another user.
• Sponsor is responsible for lost or damaged materials. Material replacements must be approved by the Library Director prior to purchase.

#### DoD MWR Virtual Library

Access resources and services through a centralized digital hub.

With its convenient access, the DoD MWR Virtual Library empowers service members and their families to pursue their intellectual and recreational interests, no matter where they are stationed.

Visit dodmwrlibraries.org to learn more.

The online platform provides access to a vast collection of digital materials available for online browsing and borrowing.

• E-books
• Audiobooks
• Magazines
• Newspapers
• Research Databases

Users can explore curated reading lists, access educational resources, and participate in virtual programs and events tailored to diverse interests and age groups.

Access library accounts at milrec.bibliovation.com, which offers user-friendly tools for searching, reserving, and managing library materials, as well as personalized features for creating wish lists and receiving recommendations.

#### Volunteering

Support your military community as a volunteer at the library.

Through volunteering, individuals can make a positive impact on their community, gain valuable experience in library operations, connect with others, and support the well-being and enrichment of military families.

Not all locations currently offer volunteering opportunities.

Contact the Volunteer Coordinator to learn about Volunteer Opportunities at your installation.

## Programs, Resources & Information
#### Reading

Learn and development with our selection of books and resources.

Your base library is a valuable resource for lifelong learning and professional development. Whether you're preparing for advancement, seeking to expand your knowledge base, or simply looking for a good book, our library provides the tools and resources you need to succeed.

Reading Resources:

• Access to Overdrive by Libby
• Audiobooks
• Children & Teen Programming
• Children's Titles (Board Books through chapter books)
• Commandant of the Marine Corps Reading List
• DoD Summer Reading Program
• eBooks
• Early Childhood Literacy Programming and Resources
• Fiction and Nonfiction
• Marine Corps Professional Reading Program
• New Titles
• Paperback Book Kits for Deploying/Training units
• Storytimes
• Test Prep
• Young Adult/Teen titles

#### Electronics & Equipment

Explore and use equipment for personal and professional growth.

Your base library is a hub for practical learning and technological innovation. From computer workstations and 3D printers to digital design software and specialized equipment, we provide the resources to support your educational and creative pursuits.

• 3D Printers
• Black/White and Color Printing/Copying/Scanning
• CAC enabled Computers
• Charging Station
• Chompshop
• Faxing
• Gaming Consoles
• Makedo Tools
• Makerspace/Innovation Lab Equipment & Programming
• Video Games
• Virtual Reality/Augmented Reality
• WiFi access

Not all resources and services listed are available at each library.

#### Games & Movies

Discover our collection of games and movies available online and at your base library.

Recognizing the importance of recreation and mental resilience, your base library offers a wide selection of games and movies designed to provide relaxation and stress relief.

• Board Games
• Children's DVD movies & TV series
• DVD movies & TV series
• Gaming Consoles (in-house use only)
• Video Games (Xbox/PlayStation/Switch)

Not available at all locations. Contact your local base library for availability.

For online resources visit our Virtual Library.

#### Additional Resources

Special features at the library that promote learning and development.

Beyond our core services, your base library offers a range of services designed to foster continuous learning and personal development.

• 24/7 Return Box
• Adult Programs
• Individual and Group Study Areas
• Library of Things (items may vary by location)
• Local Collections
• Summer Reading Program

Not all resources and services listed are available at each library.

Contact your local library for availability.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find answers to commonly asked questions.

**Q: How do I register for library account?**
A: Visit the library with valid identification, typically a military ID or dependent ID, to register.

**Q: What resources are available for children?**
A: Resources may include Storytime, educational computers, and age-appropriate programming, reading materials, DVDs, TV series, and launchpads for children. Each summer we also offer the DoD Summer Reading Program which is open to all ages.

**Q: Can I access the library's digital resources off-base?**
A: Yes, you can access our digital resources off-base by logging in to dodmwrlibraries.org.

**Q: How many items can I borrow at once?**
A: Patrons may borrow an unlimited number of books, 10 DVDs, and two video games at a time.

**Q: Are study rooms available?**
A: Study rooms are available at most installation libraries. Please contact us for more information and reservation details.

**Q: Can I access Wi-Fi at the library?**
A: Free Wi-Fi is available in the library.

**Q: Do you provide printing, copying, and scanning services?**
A: Yes, printing, copying, scanning, and faxing services are available for library patrons. Some locations charge a small fee for this service.

**Q: Are there programs and events for adults?**
A: Yes, we offer a variety of programs and events for adults.

**Q: Can I renew borrowed items online?**
A: Yes, you can renew borrowed items online by logging into your account at milrec.bibliovation.com or by contacting the library.

**Q: How do I access online databases?**
A: You can access databases and all our online resources by logging in to dodmwrlibraries.org and selecting Databases.

**Q: Do you provide assistance with research or academic projects?**
A: Our staff are available for reference assistance and can help connect you with our resources.

**Q: Do you have collections dedicated to military-related topics?**
A: Yes, the Marine Corps MWR Library Program actively collects military history titles and supports the PME Marine Corps Professional Reading Program.

**Q: Can I donate books or materials to the library?**
A: In accordance with MCO 1700.33, the libraries do not accept donations of books or other materials. Please contact the library to see if there are any upcoming Book Swap/Art Swap/Puzzle Swap, etc. programs scheduled.

**Q: How do I access e-books and audiobooks?**
A: You can access e-books and audiobooks through our virtual library by logging in to dodmwrlibraries.org and selecting eBooks and Audiobooks.

**Q: What are the policies regarding overdue materials and penalties?**
A: Overdue materials may result in a blocked account for all account holders linked to a sponsor.

**Q: What happens if I lose/damage library materials?**
A: Lost/damaged materials must be replaced and approved by the Library Director.

# Chaplains Religious Enrichment Development Operation

The mission of CREDO is to deliver faith-centered programs to Sea Service Members and their families that promote spiritual readiness, resilience, and Navy Core Values.

CREDO provides an assortment of opportunities to sea service personnel and their families.

CREDO provides FREE workshops and retreats with a positive, safe, and supportive environment to:

• Receive a greater understanding about life and yourself
• Increase trust and self confidence
• Strengthen relationships
• Gain a clearer perspective about others
• Experience personal and spiritual growth
• Strengthen marriages
• Resolve personal skills
• Learn to handle anger more constructively
• Improve communication skills
• Establish new friendships
• Have fun
• Relax

[Submit Request](https://eventactions.com/eareg.aspx?ea=Rsvp&invite=gvjujbzrj97prf4tt5d7sh7jajkwxmhu7wbyr5936ae6v2tx8v02)

## Who can attend?
Per MCO 1738.1B, Active Duty and Reserve Component personnel, and their legally married spouse and dependents may attend workshops, seminars, and retreats at no cost to the service member.

Civilian government employees and contractors, as well as retired military, are not authorized participation at government expense, but may participate in workshops and other trainings.

## Standard Marriage Enrichment Retreat (MER)
CREDO Marriage Retreats are free (includes lodging and meals). Most retreats begin with dinner day 1 and conclude mid-morning day 3.

The current curriculum for MER's includes a program called PREP that utilizes 40 years of research in relationship science. Participants will learn positive communication skills, how to identify destructive communication patterns, and learn to appreciate the unique personality of their spouse.

Childcare is not provided.

## Standard Personal Growth Retreat (PGR)
Participants will explore values and beliefs that influence ethical decision making, gain understanding and appreciation for spiritual belief systems, have ample time for personal reflection, and much more. The Standard PGR is 48 hours in length beginning at 1300 on day 1. Retreats are free to those who attend. Two nights of lodging and meals (beginning with dinner day 1) are provided to authorized participants.

## Wilderness Leadership Development Expedition
These expeditions are by request only and for units.

Experience the adrenaline rush of lower yourself over the ledge as you rappel down a cliff.

This 4 day/3 night expedition includes camping in the mountains of Western NC, transportation to and from the event site, and professionally guided discussions and wilderness training events. Expeditions are Tuesday-Friday/10 person limit.

## Wilderness Marriage Enrichment Expedition
Experience the thrill of rappelling next to your spouse as you back over the edge of a cliff. Learn about trust as your spouse belays you as you rock climb. Unplug for a few days with your spouse in the wilderness and deepen your connection.

This a 4 night Expedition in the mountains of Western North Carolina. We will be camping all 4 nights. There will be activities designed to enhance your emotional connection with your spouse.

This expedition includes meals, backpacking gear (if needed), and transportation to and from the location.

Please make note, this will be a VERY PHYSICALLY DEMANDING event. You will be expected to carry 35-40 pounds on wilderness trails up and down mountains. There are EXTREMELY limited slots for this retreat, so sign up quickly!

This is an adults only event. No children allowed and childcare is not provided.

## Wilderness Personal Growth Expedition
This a five night expedition in the mountains of Western North Carolina. You will be expected to carry 35-40 pounds on wilderness trails up and down mountains. There are very limited slots for this retreat, so sign up quickly! Couples are not allowed to attend together.

## One-Day Marriage Enrichment Workshop
One-Day workshops provide many of the same benefits as the weekend retreats, just in a condensed presentation to allow busy couples who may not be able to get away for a weekend an opportunity to tune up their marriage. One-Day workshops may cover specific topics, or books proven to increase marital satisfaction, and improve marriage longevity.

Childcare is not provided.

## ASIST Workshop
Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST) is a two-day interactive workshop in suicide first aid.

• Understand the ways that personal and societal attitudes affect views on suicide and interventions
• Provide guidance and suicide first aid to a person at risk in ways that meet their individual safety needs
• Identify the key elements of an effective suicide safety plan and the actions required to implement it
• Appreciate the value of improving and integrating suicide prevention resources in the community at large
• Recognize other important aspects of suicide prevention including life-promotion and self-care

Workshop features:

• Presentations and guidance from two LivingWorks registered trainers
• A scientifically proven intervention model
• Powerful audiovisual learning aids
• Group discussions
• Skills practice and development
• A balance of challenge and safety

## SafeTALK Workshop
SafeTALK is a half-day training program that teaches participants to recognize and engage persons who might be having thoughts of suicide and to connect them with community resources trained in suicide intervention.

After training, participants in the safeTALK program should be able to:

• Challenge attitudes that inhibit open talk about suicide.
• Recognize a person who might be having thoughts of suicide.
• Engage them in direct and open talk about suicide.
• Listen to the person's feelings about suicide to show that they are taken seriously.
• Move quickly to connect them with someone trained in suicide intervention

# Exceptional Family Member Program

We support military families with special medical and/or educational needs and ensure availability of care during transitions to improve families' quality of life.

## How To Get Started
The Exceptional Family Member Program is comprised of 3 components:

## Eligibility Identification & Enrollment
**Eligible Exceptional Family Members Include:**

• Dependent(s) of an active duty service member
• Spouse, child, or parent
• Resides with the sponsor (51%)
• Requires medical specialty care _or_
• Chronic medical condition requiring more than annual visits with a primary care physician
• Eligible for early intervention services (IFSP)
• Eligible for special education or related services (IEP)

**Required form needed for registration:**

• DD Form 2792 (all family members)
• DD Form 2792-1 (children with an Individualized Family Services Plan or Individualized Education Program)

Supplemental documentation needed as applicable (i.e., IFSP, IEP, etc.)

Completed forms can be submitted to the local EFMP office or Headquarters EFMP at hqmc.efmp@usmc.mil.

All forms can be downloaded from the [DoD Forms Management Program](https://www.esd.whs.mil/directives/forms/).

## Assignment Coordination
When a family member's specific medical or educational needs are documented via the DD2792 and DD2792-1, HQMC EFMP Assignment specialist use the information to match documented needs to the capability of the proposed PCS location. While the military's mission guides these assignments, when MMOA/MMEA/RAM and EFMP work together, the goal is to find an assignment that supports mission, career progression and family member needs.

Schedule an Assignment Consultation by emailing hqmc.efmp@usmc.mil

## Family Support
Exceptional Family Member Program professionals help families become their own best advocates by providing:

• Information and Referrals
• Helping families successfully transition before, during and after a PCS.
• Supporting families with non-clinical case management.
• Connecting families to important resources and services, such as the School Liaison Officer.

## PCSing?
Moving from one duty station to another can be stressful.

• Ensure your EFMP enrollment paperwork is current. HQMC EFMP Assignment Case Managers utilize the DD 2792 and DD 2792-1 on file to determine the appropriateness of the proposed assignment. Ensuring your paperwork is accurate benefits the timeliness of the screening and helps to put you in a location where family members have access to needed care.
• Share your needs and concerns with your Family Caseworker.
• Request 3-months of medication.
• Visit usmc-mccs.org for MCCS events, services, and support for you and your family.
• Follow your local MCCS Facebook and Instagram to stay connected to your military community and learn about events, resources, and programs offered.

## Command Resources
Providing military leadership with the resources and knowledge they need to help support their Marines and their families.

• Operations Analysis Directorate Report: Analysis of the Impact of Exceptional Family Member Program Enrollment on Individual Marine Career Progression and Promotion
• Inspector General Checklist
• EFMP Brief for Leaders
• EFMP Continuation on Location

## Special Assistance Fire Emergency Response (SAFE-R) Program
The SAFE-R Program gives emergency responders access to a family's medical history and conditions before arriving on scene — helping ensure every patient receives the right care and is transported to the most appropriate facility.

Once consent and enrollment forms are completed, emergency responders (EMS, Fire, and PMO) will be able to view the information provided on the enrollment form during an emergency.

_This program is open to EFMP families living on Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune and Marine Corps Air Station New River._

_Families can register through their EFMP Family Case Worker or the Training, Education, and Outreach Specialist._

## EFMP Resource Library
The EFMP Resource Library is a welcoming space offering a wide range of materials to support learning, growth, and everyday life. The library features themed books, DVDs, and hands‑on resources covering topics such as ADHD, autism, anxiety, sensory needs, communication, early learning, parenting, military family life, and more.

In addition to traditional reading materials, families can also borrow practical support items—including sensory tools, safety devices, and developmental resources—to try at home and discover what works best for their needs. It's an easy, no‑cost way to explore helpful tools, build skills, and enjoy meaningful time together.

The EFMP Resource Library is open to all authorized patrons, regardless of enrollment in EFMP.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find quick answers to common questions about our services here.

**Q: How does enrollment in EFMP affect military assignments or postings?**
Enrollment in EFMP ensures consideration of a family member's needs during military assignments with the goal to place families in locations that can support those needs.

**Q: What specific services and support does EFMP offer family members with special needs?**
EFMP offers various support services, including information, referrals, and case management. Some families may be eligible for respite care.

**Q: How does EFMP impact travel or relocation, especially concerning healthcare access?**
EFMP helps facilitate necessary healthcare access during travel or relocation by making medical case management referrals to TRICARE.

**Q: Does EFMP enrollment qualify me for Priority Housing?**
Some individuals enrolled in EFMP will be eligible for priority housing. This status will be listed on your official enrollment letter and is part of the initial and updated enrollment process.

**Q: How often should information be updated or reassessed within the EFMP system?**
Families should update EFMP enrollment every 3 years or when there are changes in the family member's medical or educational needs.

**Q: How do I disenroll from the program?**
If the family member is no longer a dependent, update DEERS and contact hqmc.efmp@usmc.mil to request disenrollment. If the family member's medical and/or education condition has resolved, update DD 2792 and DD 2792-1, if applicable and submit with a request for disenrollment. If the condition still exists, we will not be able to facilitate the disenrollment, as EFMP is a DoD mandatory enrollment program, when qualifying conditions are present.

**Q: Are there resources available to help navigate the program or advocate for specific needs?**
The Exceptional Family Member Program has Family Support professionals who can assist families in navigating the program, accessing resources, and learning how to advocate for their needs.

**Q: How is personal and medical information handled within the EFMP?**
Personal and medical information within the EFMP is treated with strict confidentiality and follows privacy regulations.

**Q: What can families do if they disagree with a decision made within the EFMP?**
Families can address disagreements or concerns about EFMP decisions through established channels, often involving the EFMP office or higher-level appeals processes.

**Q: What is Respite Care?**
Respite Care is a non-entitlement benefit intended to provide brief rest periods for the primary caregiver(s).

**Q: Am I able to schedule an appointment?**
Yes. Contact the Family Support specialist at your local Exceptional Family Member Program to schedule an appointment.

# Family Member Employment Assistance Program

The Family Member Employment Assistance Program (FMEAP) supports military spouses and dependent family members with career readiness tools, resources, and services.

## Not sure where to begin? Start here.
The Family Member Employment Assistance Program (FMEAP) is designed to provide support and resources to family members, including spouses, of military service members to help them pursue and sustain meaningful employment despite the challenges of the military lifestyle.

## Eligibility, Services, and Support
#### Eligibility

The primary beneficiaries of the Family Member Assistance Program (FMEAP):

• Military spouses of active-duty service members.
• Dependent family member of active-duty service members.

#### Getting Started

Connect with your local installation's FMEAP office. This will allow you to schedule an introductory meeting and learn more about the program.

Attend FMEAP workshops.

Register for the Military Spouse Employment Partnership. Registration can provide you with access to a network of employer partners.

Explore MyCAA. If you're eligible and interested in pursuing further education, start the application process for the MyCAA scholarship.

Stay engaged.

#### Available Services

• Career Advising & Coaching
• Education, Entrepreneurial & Training Resources
• Individual Career Assessment & Planning
• Interviewing Skills
• Job Search Strategies
• Resume Assistance
• Salary Negotiations
• Volunteer & Skills Development
• Career Workshops

## Resources, Programs & Information
#### SpouseWorks

Discover a trusted career and education support in one place.

**Welcome, military spouses!**

The Office of Spouse Employment introduces **SpouseWorks** (formerly SECO).

SpouseWorks brings all your trusted career and education support into one easy-to-navigate platform.

• **Career Coaching & Advice:** Navigate every stage of your career journey.
• **Job Opportunities:** Find employers looking to hire military spouses.
• **Education & Funding:** Discover scholarships, fellowships, and training.

Connect to these valuable resources at [SpouseWorks](https://spouseworks.militaryonesource.mil/portal/).

[Learn more about SpouseWorks](https://spouseworks.militaryonesource.mil/portal/article/welcome-to-spouseworks) through FAQs and related articles.

#### [SpouseWorks Scholarship](https://mycaa.militaryonesource.mil/mycaa/)

Explore a workforce development program that provides up to $4,000 in financial assistance.

#### [Military Spouse Employer Partnership (MSEP)](https://msepjobs.militaryonesource.mil/msep/)

The Military Spouse Employer Partnership connects military spouses with hundreds of partner employers who have committed to recruit, hire, promote and retain military spouses.

#### [Military Spouse Licensure Reimbursement (MSLR)](https://myseco.militaryonesource.mil/portal/article/licensure-reimbursement-pcs-moves)

If your career requires a professional license or certification, you may be eligible for up to $1,000 in reimbursement for licensure and certification costs resulting from relocations within the United States or from OCONUS to stateside.

#### [Transferring Your Professional License](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/education-employment/seco/transferring-your-professional-license-what-s-involved)

Moving across the country – or around the world – can be a great adventure.

#### Spouse's Transition and Readiness Seminar (S.T.A.R.S)

This workshop is designed to provide support and resources for military spouses as they navigate various aspects of transition, particularly during periods of relocation or when their service member is transitioning out of the military.

pages.title: Marine Corps Family Team Building
pages.text:
# Marine Corps Family Team Building

We empower Marines, families, and units with valuable resources and problem-solving skills to help them navigate the demands of military life.

## Eligibility & How to Get Started
Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) offers comprehensive support to the entire military community through a variety of workshops and training programs.

#### Eligibility and Getting Started

Eligibility for participation in our program extends to individuals across various segments of the military community.

**How to get started with MCFTB.**

1. **Identify Individual Needs:** Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB program offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.
2. **Connect with MCFTB:** Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone.
3. **Attend Workshops and Classes:** Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation.
4. **Connect with Other Families:** Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms.

## Programs, Resources & Support
#### Unit, Personal and Family Readiness Program (UPFRP)

Marine Corps Family Team Building provides training in support of the Unit, Personal, & Family Readiness Program (UPFRP).

Training includes Family Readiness Command Team Training (FRCTT), Deployment Readiness and Uniformed Readiness Coordinator (DRC/URC) training, and Family Readiness Command Team Advisor/Assistant (FRCTA/FRA) training.

The UPFRP Family Readiness Program Training (FRPT) provides training to UPFRP personnel to include:

• Family Readiness Command Team Training (FRCTT)
• Deployment Readiness Coordinator (DRC)
• Uniformed Readiness Coordinator (URC)
• Family Readiness Command Team Advisors (FRCTA)
• Family Readiness Assistant (FRA)

The UPFRP provides comprehensive support and resources to Marines and families, with the goal to equip service members and their families with the skills necessary to overcome challenges and thrive during their military life journey.

For information about volunteering with your unit's UPFRP, please contact your DRC or URC.

#### LifeSkills Training

LifeSkills Training classes are designed to equip Services Members and their families with the necessary skills for successful interactions, both at work and home, ultimately leading to positive outcomes in all areas of life.

Workshops are comprehensive collection of personal and professional skill-building classes, promoting successful outcomes in various life challenges.

• **Four Lenses** - This interactive workshop focuses on four temperament styles that greatly influence one's life.
• **Five Love Languages** - This workshop is based on the #1 New York Times bestseller written by Dr. Millions of couples have learned the simple way to express their feelings and bring joy back into marriage.
• **Real Relationships** - This workshop helps to identify the hallmarks of meaningful relationships and how to build skills to make them stronger.
• **Say What?** - This workshop is design to teach valuable communication strategies to help individuals communicate more effectively fostering healthier relationships.
• **Basic Anger Management** - Although disagreements and anger are a normal part of life, violent expressions of feelings detract from personal and professional relationships and can negatively affect the efficient functioning and morale of Marine Corps units, individuals, families, and communities.
• **Basic Stress Management** - Learn what stress is and how to manage it by changing your response to it. Learn to apply helpful techniques to ease the weight of stress within your life. Learn how to apply a problem solving method to take action in high-stress situations.
• **Living My Best Life: Bridging the Generation Gap** - Bridging the Generation Gap shows participants the unique characteristics of the many generations that exist today providing a foundation to enable improved communication across generations through increased knowledge of generational characteristics, influences, and priorities.
• **Living My Best Life: Attitudes & Actions** - This course is designed to encourage military members and their families to maintain a positive focus and be engaged in their homes, at work, and in their communities.
• **Ready, Set, Prepare** - This workshop contains information regarding actions that service members and families should take to be informed and prepared in the event of natural and man-made hazards.
• **Prevention & Relationship Enhancement Program (PREP)** - PREP 8.0 is designed to help couples achieve their relationship goals.

Not all workshops are available at all locations.

Please contact your MCFTB office for workshop schedule and availability.

#### Readiness and Deployment Support

Readiness and Deployment Support provides service members and their families with the knowledge and skills to prepare and successfully navigate all phases of deployments.

The Readiness & Deployment Support workshops are designed to equip Service Members and their families with essential life skills necessary to effectively overcome the anticipated and often un-foreseen challenges that suddenly arise during deployments.

**Workshops:**

• **Pre-Deployment Brief for Marines & Families** - This brief is held per unit request 30 to 45 days prior to a service members deployment. For Individual Augments (IA) or short notice deployments, please call MCFTB for a personalized appointment.
• **Family Care Plan** - Learn who needs a family care plan, what should be included in an effective family care plan and how to construct one.
• **Mid-Deployment Success** - This workshop is designed to promote deployment success for the spouse or significant other at home and includes suggestions for fun things to do, goal setting, and resources. The workshop is an excellent opportunity to assess progress thus far, get new ideas for continued success, and network with other Marine Corps spouses and significant others.
• **Mid-Deployment Kids** - This workshop is designed to promote deployment success for kids, including reactions to deployment, ways parents can help their kids feel connected to the deployed parent, and resources to help you and your child thrive during a deployment.
• **Return and Reunion for Parents & Extended Families** - Spouses and significant others of returning Marines are eager to discuss homecoming anticipation, expectations, and concerns. This is a brief that is required to be provided to remain-behind family members and is part of the required Pre-Deployment Agreement form.
• **Return and Reunion for Parents & Kids** - Held in conjunction with Return and Reunion Workshops for spouses, MCFTB work with children ages 5 and up to help them prepare for their service member's homecoming in a fun and interactive setting.
• **Reintegration Success** - This educational workshop provides a forum for couples to assess their recent deployment experience, address the effect of reintegration on a relationship, and assess the level of relationship satisfaction.

Not all workshops are available at all locations. Contact your MCFTB office for schedule and availability.

#### Lifestyle Insights, Networking, Knowledge, and Skills (L.I.N.K.S.)

This is a volunteer-based, team-mentoring program, designed to teach participants about navigating the unique challenges of life in the military.

The L.I.N.K.S.

Curriculum Includes:

• Our Corps, Our Culture
• Events & Etiquette
• Navigating Resources
• Pay & Entitlements
• Deployments
• Safe and Sound All Around
• The Place You Will Go
• Building Your Network
• Investing in Your Community
• Kids Readiness
• Mentor Training

Contact your MCFTB office for more information about the L.I.N.K.S. workshops.

#### Volunteering

Volunteering helps you connect with your unit and community.

MCFTB provides opportunities for training and volunteerism with L.I.N.K.S.

**L.I.N.K.S. Volunteers**

If you are interested in becoming part of the LINKS team, call us or visit our office for more information.

• Host/Greet at Sessions
• Food Angel – Help to Feed our Participants.
• Administrative Support
• Present L.I.N.K.S. Session Topics
• Information Booth Support
• Event Support

**UPFRP Volunteers**

Family Readiness Volunteers are an integral part of the UPFRP.

To explore Family Readiness Volunteer opportunities, contact your unit's DRC/URC.
