# MCCS Personal Financial Management

We provide you and your family with professional training and guidance to help you manage money successfully.

## Get Started with Your Personal Finances
Taking the first steps toward financial stability and your future.

#### Eligibility and First Steps

Eligibility for participation in our program extends to individuals across various sections of the military community.

• Service Members
• Family Members
• DoD Employees

Getting started is easy!

**Contact us.** Get professional guidance and support tailored to your financial goals.

**Make an appointment.** Schedule your personalized financial consultation today! Making an appointment is easy – just reach out to our program office and take the first step towards financial success.

**Register for workshops or courses.** Sign up for our workshops and classes to enhance your financial literacy! Register now to secure your spot and gain valuable insights into managing your money effectively.

**Explore our webpage.** Discover helpful financial tools and resources provided by the Personal Financial Management Program. From workshop schedules to helpful resources, everything you need to get started is just a click away!

## Financial Services
Unlock your financial potential with our comprehensive services!

Contact us today to learn more about the services offered and how we can help you achieve your financial goals.

• Blended Retirement System
• Car Buying
• Consumer Awareness
• Continuation Pay
• Couple Financial Counseling
• Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
• Credit / Debt Management
• Developing a Spending Plan
• Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
• Individual Financial Counseling
• Major Purchases
• Military Pay & Benefits
• Retirement Planning
• Survivor Benefits Plan
• Thrift Savings Plan
• Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

## Become a Command Financial Specialist
Support Marines within your unit with financial resources, tools, and guidance.

Command Financial Specialists (CFS) are a vital resource for Marines, offering support throughout their careers.

In accordance with MCO 1700.37, the minimum requirements for assignment as a unit Command Financial Specialist are:

• Must be an E6, WO, O-1, and above.
• Have at least one year remaining at your present duty station.
• Highly motivated.
• Financially stable.
• Have no record of Letters of Indebtedness/Non-Sufficient Funds/NJP/Poor performance counseling above the rank of LCPL.
• Successfully complete the Leading Marines Course and MCI's 3420 and 3422 on Personal Financial Management.
• Participate in continuing education such as CFS forums and refresher training.

You do not need a degree in financial planning to succeed as a CFS.

The most successful CFSs are those who enjoy the process of identifying financial needs and thrive on the challenge of finding solutions.

As a Command Financial Specialist, you will help Marines and their families learn about managing money and making smart financial choices.

For more information contact your MCCS Personal Financial Manager.

## Financial Resources
Tools and services that support your financial well-being.

#### Budgeting Tools

Contact your local Personal Financial Management Program office for helpful tools for managing your money to take charge of your finances.

• [Financial Well-Being Assessment](https://finred.usalearning.gov/FWBA)
• [Spending Plan Worksheet](https://finred.usalearning.gov/assets/downloads/FINRED-Spendingplan-TK.pdf)
• [Personal Net Worth Tracker](https://finred.usalearning.gov/ToolsAndAddRes/NetWorth)
• [Financial Calculators](https://finred.usalearning.gov/ToolsAndAddRes/Calculators)
• [Sen$e App](https://finred.usalearning.gov/ToolsAndAddRes/Sen$e)

#### Financially Fit Kids

Children who learn to manage money early, grow up knowing how to budget, save, and spend wisely.

Providing kids with financial skills help them avoid debt and prepare for big expenses and the future.

Learn more about tips and tools available to help raise [Financially Fit Kids](https://www.milspousemoneymission.org/military-spouse-raising-financial-fit-kids/).

• Values & Habits
• Self Assessment
• Communication Skills
• Goal Setting
• All About Allowances
• System for Saving
• Create a Spending Plan
• Tips & Videos

#### [Thrift Savings Plan](https://www.tsp.gov/)

Designed to help your build financial security for the future with one of the finest retirement plans.

#### Blended Retirement System

The Blended Retirement System (BRS) is a way for service members to save for retirement, introduced in 2018. Unlike the retirement services in the past where only those who served for 20 years received a pension, the BRS offers benefits for almost all service members.

The BRS combines a regular pension for those who serve at least 20 years with a savings plan similar to a civilian 401(k), where the government also adds money to your savings.

The BRS makes it possible for military personnel to start building their retirement savings early in their careers, whether they plan to stay for the full length of service or not.

Learn more about the Blended Retirement System at [Blended Retirement System](https://militarypay.defense.gov/BlendedRetirement/)

#### Continuation Pay

Continuation Pay under the Blended Retirement System (BRS) is a one-time bonus offered to military members who agree to extend their service beyond their current enlistment period.

This bonus serves as an incentive for service members to continue their military career at mid-career points.

Accepting continuation pay comes with a commitment to serve for an additional number of years, and failing to fulfill this commitment may require the service member to repay the received bonus.

## Individual Appointments and Unit Briefs
#### [Book an Individual Appointment](https://eventactions.com/ea.aspx?ea=Rsvp&invite=gytjff73wpsf6xjgxht8b4nf1n128295gsndzhhrgs55agr2fc2a)

Request for an individual personal finance appointment.

#### [Book a Unit Brief](https://eventactions.com/eareg.aspx?ea=Rsvp&invite=08samd320xu5eat6cdvajx1cpjf5e21wd3the87ckujx879nvatu)

Request a finance brief.

#### Managing Stress

Financial emergencies and challenges can be stressful on you and your family. We are here to help.

#### Budgeting for Education

Support your financial goals by earning a degree or certifications!

Whether you're looking to earn a college degree, obtain a certification, or improve your skills, there are resources designed to support your personal and professional growth, preparing you for success both in the Marine Corps and in civilian life.

Contact the Education Center and speak with a coordinator.

#### Family Member Employment Assistance

Discover career readiness tools, resources, and services that support military spouses and family members.

Connect with your local Family Member Employment Assistance office to schedule an introductory meeting and learn more about the program.

**Available Services:**

• Career Advising & Coaching
• Career Workshops
• Education, Entrepreneurial & Training Resources
• Individual Career Assessment & Planning
• Interviewing Skills
• Job Search Strategies
• Resume Assistance
• Salary Negotiations
• Volunteer & Skills Development

## FAQs
Quick answers to common questions.

**Is there a fee associated with participating in the PFMP offered by MCCS?**
The services provided by PFMP are offered free of charge to eligible individuals and their families.

**How do I schedule an appointment for financial counseling through the PFMP?**
To schedule a counseling session, individuals can contact their local PFMP office or visit the office for appointment scheduling options.

**Are the PFMP workshops and seminars available online for remote participation?**
Yes, PFMP offers online workshops and seminars to accommodate service members and DoD employees stationed in various locations.

**Can family members participate in PFMP workshops and counseling sessions?**
Yes. Family members can participate in PFMP workshops and counseling sessions. Register for a workshop by using the calendar or contact the Personal Financial Management to register and schedule a counseling session.

**Is financial counseling provided by certified professionals?**
Yes, PFMP financial counselors are trained and certified to provide financial education, counseling, and assistance to service members and their families.

**Can DoD employees who are not military service members also access PFMP services through MCCS?**
Yes, PFMP services are available to DoD civilian employees to help them manage their personal finances effectively.

• [Fight Back Against Identity Theft](https://www.identitytheft.gov/#/)

# Community Counseling

We provide non-medical counseling services and help service members and their families develop skills to manage life's stressors and challenges.

## Eligibility & How to Get Started
#### Getting Started

Offering support to service members and their families within the military community.

#### Eligibility

Eligibility for participation in our Community Counseling Program extends to individuals across various segments of the military community.

• Active-Duty Service Members - All Branches
• Civilian Expeditionary Forces
• Spouses
• Families
• Children
• Recruits

#### How to get started with Community Counseling:

1. **Schedule an Appointment:** Contact the Community Counseling Program office and speak to a professional about scheduling an appointment with a mental health clinician.
2. **Assessment:** A Community Counseling Program clinician will conduct an intake assessment which typically involves a structured evaluation designed to identify an individual's needs, concerns, and goals regarding their mental health and well-being.
3. **Counseling Services:** Following your initial assessment, you and the clinician will identify appropriate services.
4. **Case Management Services:** If individuals or families are working with multiple providers and managing multiple systems, our staff and clinicians are available to assist you.
5. **Referral Services:** Our staff will help you to identify other services to meet your specific needs for those beyond what is offered at the Community Counseling Program.

pages.title: Domestic Abuse
pages.text:
# Domestic Abuse

## What is Domestic Abuse?
Domestic abuse is the use, attempted use, or threatened use of force or violence against an intimate partner. An intimate partner is a current or former spouse, a person with whom the abuser shares a child or common domicile, or a person who is in a romantic relationship with the abuser.

Examples of domestic abuse include, but are not limited to, taking your cell phone or keys, not allowing you to leave a location, controlling what you wear or who you speak to, limiting your access to money, name calling, pushing, hitting, or sexual contact without your consent.

## I Have Experienced Domestic Abuse
It's important to know where you can go for safe, judgment-free help when you are feeling unsafe in your relationship.

Everyone who experiences domestic abuse has a unique set of circumstances and concerns.

If you have experienced intimate partner abuse contact a FAP Advocate or FAP Clinician to learn about resources available to you and reporting options. You may be eligible to obtain a restricted report.

Victims may also decide to seek help outside the military. FAP can connect you to civilian or community-based resources, or you can visit the National Domestic Violence Hotline website.

**If you are experiencing domestic abuse,** visit the FAP office locator to find the closest FAP office, or go to the National Domestic Violence Hotline website or call 800-799-7233. Call 911 if you are in immediate danger. If you are on a military installation, call your military law enforcement office.

Three groups of professionals may keep information about domestic abuse confidential under the restricted reporting option:

• FAP Advocates
• FAP clinicians
• DoD Health care providers*

Making a restricted report means:

• FAP will not notify military law enforcement.
• Command is not involved.
• You have access to the full range of FAP services, including counseling and advocacy.

You are also entitled to the protections of privileged communication with a chaplain.

To prioritize victim safety, the restricted reporting option is not available if there is an immediate risk of serious harm. And the restricted reporting option does not apply to child abuse cases, which are required by law to be reported to law enforcement and child welfare services.

*Some state-specific laws may require medical providers to report known or suspected incidents of domestic abuse to law enforcement regardless of a victim's preferences.

When an unrestricted report is made, FAP will notify both military law enforcement and the service member's military command.

Making an unrestricted report means:

• Military law enforcement will conduct an investigation of the incident, which includes contacting the alleged abuser.
• Command will be notified.
• You can seek a Military and/or Civilian Protective Order.
• You have access to the full range of FAP services, including counseling and advocacy.
• You have access to legal services on military installations.
• If a service member is separated for domestic abuse, the victim may be eligible for transitional compensation

## I Need to Talk with Someone now
FAP advocates provide crisis intervention, immediate and ongoing advocacy services, and safety planning to victims of domestic abuse and non-abusing parents of child abuse victims. To speak with someone regarding services please call your local installation's 24 hours a day, 7 days a week helpline.

**24/7 Helpline For Your Local Installation**

• Quantico: 703-350-1688
• Iwakuni: 0827-79-7233
• TwentyNine Palms: 760-362-9837
• Albany: 229-347-2651
• Bridgeport: 760-362-9837
• Barstow: 760-577-6484
• Camp Butler: 098-970-2915
• Camp Fuji: DoD Safe Helpline 877-995-5247
• Camp Lejeune - New River: 910-376-5675
• Camp-Pendleton: 760-500-2633
• Cherry Point: 252-671-0377
• Hawaii: 808-216-7175
• Henderson-Hall: 202-439-6038
• MARFORRES: 877-432-2215
• Miramar: 858-864-3408
• Parris-Island: 843-592-0646
• Beaufort: 843-592-0646
• San-Diego: 619-279-6113
• Washington D.C.: 571-205-1298
• Yuma: 928-941-3650

For immediate assistance, the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-7233) provides lifesaving tools and support to enable victims to find safety and live lives free of abuse.

## I Want to Help Someone Else
**5 Ways to Help a Friend Who is Experiencing Domestic Abuse**

Everyone's situation is different — domestic abuse can happen to anyone and it's not their fault.

1. **Ask to connect** — "How do you prefer we connect?" Having a safe way to communicate is important.
2. **Stay in touch** — "Let's play a game online." Finding creative reasons to call, text, video chat or use social media check-ins may provide a lifeline for those who feel unsafe at home. Learn about privacy and safety tips for technology from the National Network to End Domestic Violence at [www.techsafety.org](https://www.techsafety.org/resources).
3. **Support and believe** — "I care about you and I'm here for you, no matter what." Remind your friend that they are not alone and that you are there for them.
4. **Chat about options** — "Let's create a safety plan." Options are empowering. Let them know that FAP advocates are available 24/7 to help them think through dangerous situations and create a safety plan.
5. **Share the hotline** — "Here is the information for that restaurant I told you about." It may be safer for your friend if you research support options for them - such as the National Domestic Violence Hotline at https://www.thehotline.org/ - on your device, provided you feel safe doing so. Create a secret code word, phrase or symbol that lets you know your friend is signaling for help, whether that means a call from you or for you to call the police. A call can sometimes disrupt abuse.

## I Don't Know Where To Start
Making the decision to seek help for domestic abuse can be difficult. Everyone deserves to be in a relationship that is free of abuse. If you are experiencing abuse, consider exploring your options with the National Hotline (1800-799-SAFE (7233)) or [www.thehotline.org](http://www.thehotline.org).

Through a FAP Advocate, you will be encouraged to develop a plan for safety and will explore local resources that are relevant to your specific needs. You will also learn about your options for reporting the abuse based on your current safety and eligibility for services from military resources.

The FAP provides a variety of supportive services including prevention, home visitation, advocacy and clinical services.

• **Clinical Program** provides screenings, assessments, evidence-based counseling, clinical case management, and appropriate referrals.
• **FAP Advocates** provide crisis intervention, ongoing advocacy services, and safety planning.
• **New Parent Support Program** offers parenting education and home visiting services to expectant parents and families with children ages zero to five. It is staffed with home visitors who are licensed social workers, licensed counselors and/or licensed registered nurses.
• **The Prevention and Education program** provides education and prevention-focused services to individuals, families, and the community.

## Leaders Resources
Per DODI 6400.06, Commanders have the overriding responsibility for the response to domestic abuse. They are required to respond to all known and suspected incidents of domestic abuse and support victims. DoDM 6400.01 V3 provides additional information about the IDC process. FAP provides training to Commanders and Senior Enlisted Advisors on their responsibilities per DODI 6400.06, IDC, FAP services, and local resources.

Taking care of Marines is the plan of the day, every day. Doing it well requires constant training.

## 5 Ways Command Leaders Can Unite Against Domestic Abuse
Domestic abuse is incompatible with military values and reduces mission readiness.

As a leader, it is important that you understand your responsibility to report and respond to allegations of domestic abuse, show compassion to victims, raise awareness of domestic abuse in the military and clearly communicate the Department of Defense's commitment to ending abuse with your command.

1. **Educate yourself** — Make sure you understand your responsibility to report and respond to allegations of domestic abuse. Find more information online: https://www.militaryonesource.mil/Leaders-End-Abuse
2. **Raise awareness** — Raise awareness of domestic abuse in the military and clearly communicate the Defense Department's commitment to unite against abuse within your command. This toolkit can help: https://www.militaryonesource.mil/abuse-help-leaders
   Share the following resources:
   • Immediate crisis support — National Domestic Violence Hotline, Call 800-799-7233, https://www.thehotline.org/
   • Local support, 24/7 — Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate Locator https://www.militaryonesource.mil/DAVALocator
   • Support for young people between ages 13 to 26 years old — Love is Respect | Text "LOVEIS" to 866-331-9474, https://www.loveisrespect.org/
3. **Take action immediately** — Show anyone who reports abuse to you that you take all their concerns seriously by:
   • Explaining how you will address their concerns and take action
   • Connecting them with a FAP advocate who can help them document their abuse, make a safety plan and access military and civilian services
   • Offering to follow up with them (via phone call or email) to ensure they received all the services and support they need
4. **Show compassion to victims** — Tell anyone who raises a concern about abuse that you believe them, that they are not alone and that help and support are available.
5. **Unite with other leaders against abuse** — Coordinate with other command leaders and departments throughout your installation to provide consistent and easily accessible domestic violence awareness and prevention education, resources and support.

## Top 3 Things You Can Say to Help a Victim of Abuse
• I take your concerns seriously. You are not alone in this.
• A FAP advocate can help you document the abuse, make a safety plan and access military or civilian services.
• I can follow up with you via phone or email to ensure you received all the services and support you need.

If you need to exit this website in a hurry, click the "Exit Site" button and you will be quickly redirected to Weather.com.

# Military & Family Life Counselors

Military & Family Life Counselors (MFLCs) are experienced behavioral health professionals assigned to installations, embedded in units, schools, and Child Development and Youth Centers, MFLCs augment and work in collaboration with other Marine Corps Behavioral Health programs.

## Need to Talk?
Military & Family Life Counselors are here to listen, and are available to help service members, spouses, family members, children and staff address:

• Deployment/Reintegration Issues
• Stress
• Marriage and Relationship Issues
• Decision-making
• Parenting/Sibling & Family Issues
• Grief and Loss
• Communication Challenges
• Daily Life Issues
• Transition Issues
• Emotional Well-being
• Improve Coping and Resilience

Counseling, consultation and training is **free** and **confidential**. **No records are kept.**

## Helping You Is Our Priority
After-hours and weekend appointments are available. Group or off-site meetings can be arranged.

## 7 Things To Know About MFLC
1. All MFLCs are licensed professional mental health counselors (LCSW, LPC, LMFT, etc.) who provide non-medical solution-focused "counseling" (no longer called "consultation") to military personnel and their families.
2. MFLCs are considered an augmentation, not a replacement, for existing family support services.
3. MFLCs do not keep records.
4. MFLCs maintain contact with Marines/Sailors (and their families) through their confidential cell phones and face-to-face communications.
5. The MFLCs' work day is flexible; however, it is a 40 hour work week. This provides the MFLCs the opportunity to meet with people prior to work, after work, and to support those who work a shift schedule.
6. MFLCs are embedded in units and also have the flexibility to meet at various locations on or off site, never in a person's home or vehicle.
7. People can meet with the MFLC for up to 12 sessions.

Contact: Military & Family Life Counselors

# Military OneSource

Along with resources provided at the duty station, such as counselors, chaplains, and other advisors, **Military OneSource** can also support Service members and their families.

Military OneSource, **[https://www.militaryonesource.mil/](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/)**, is your connection to information, answers, and support when Marine Corps life happens.

Military OneSource is a free service to Marines (active duty, veteran, wounded/ill/injured), attached sailors, family, and naval personnel supporting Marine Units. The Military OneSource Line is a confidential phone and chat support service that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The goal of the Military OneSource confidential support services is to help callers manage stress in all forms, ranging from relationship and career issues, to deployment and financial problems, and develop the necessary skills required to cope with the widely-varying challenges of life in the Corps.

A few of the types of help available:

• Relationship counseling
• Non-medical counseling for stress relief
• Financial counseling
• Document translation
• Spouse scholarships, education and career benefits
• Child care options
• Permanent change of station moves

[Learn more about Military OneSource support services](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/confidential-help/non-medical-counseling/military-onesource/military-counseling-for-stress/)

Military OneSource phone: 1-800-342-9647 · [Military OneSource Chat](https://www.militaryonesource.com/milone-support)

## Crisis Signs
These signs require immediate attention. If you are experiencing any of these and need medical attention, call 911 now. For immediate help in dealing with a suicidal crisis, call the Military Crisis Line at 1-800-273-8255 and Press 1 or dial 988.

• Thinking about hurting or killing yourself
• Looking for ways to kill yourself
• Talking about death, dying, or suicide
• Self-destructive behavior, such as drug abuse, risky use of weapons, etc.

For more information, visit the **[Military Crisis Line website](http://www.veteranscrisisline.net/get-help-now/military-crisis-line/)**.

# Prevention & Education

The Prevention & Education Program offers a series of evidenced-based courses designed to help Marines, Sailors and their families aboard Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River improve their lives and enhance their personal and professional relationships.

[Find a Class](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/prevention-education/prevention-education-calendar)

## Nurturing Fathers
This class provides men with the opportunity to learn how to be a nurturing parent. Open to all authorized patrons who are fathers or soon to be fathers.

## Positive Parenting
Known to be one of the most effective evidenced-based parenting class in the world. "Triple P" is based on 30 years of on-going research.

## Anger Management in the 21st Century
Take control of your anger before it wreaks havoc in your life.

## Building and Maintaining Successful Relationships (MALI)
Learn the positive aspects of being in a committed relationship.

## Within My Reach
Get what you deserve out of relationships.

This class is not intended for couples to attend together.

## 7 Principles for Making Marriage Work
This class is based on the best-selling book _The Seven Principles for Making Marriage Work_. Couples must attend together.

Stressful situations, if not dealt with effectively, can contribute to depression, anxiety, substance abuse and physical health problems. Call to schedule your unit workshop.

This class offers a fun way to learn about yourself, build self-awareness and identify ways to make choices that will benefit your goals and dreams.

Improve mission readiness by strengthening total fitness through workshops designed to teach Marines and Sailors skills to improve relationships, communication, finances, coping strategies, and spiritual fitness.

pages.title: Sexual Assault Prevention and Response
pages.text:
# Sexual Assault Prevention and Response

## SAPR RESOURCES
**24/7 Lejeune-New River Helpline: (910) 750-5852**

[DOD Safe Helpline Live Chat](https://safehelpline.org/)

## What is Sexual Assault?
Sexual Assault is a crime.

After a sexual assault occurs, some people may want to question what someone did before, during, or after the sexual assault, which can lead to "victim blaming." The person who was assaulted is never to blame for what happened to them.

## What Is Consent . . .
Consent is given with words or overt acts indicating a freely given agreement to the sexual contact by a "competent" person. You are considered "incompetent" if you are sleeping or incapacitated, due to alcohol or drug use, mental incapacity, or age.

## What Is NOT Consent . . .
Lack of verbal or physical resistance is not consent. For the full legal definition of consent, please see Marine Corps Order 1752.5C.

There are a few important things to remember about consent. Consent is required for all sexual encounters, but it is the bare minimum, not what someone should be striving for when it comes to sex.

## What Offenses Are Sexual Assault?
Sexual assault includes a broad category of sexual offenses, including rape, forcible sodomy (oral or anal sex), and other unwanted sexual contact that is aggravated, abusive, or wrongful (including unwanted and inappropriate sexual contact) or attempts to commit these acts.

## What Do I Do if I'm Sexually Assaulted?
If you were sexually assaulted, there are some things you may want to consider doing to keep yourself safe and healthy.

**Consider Taking These Steps**

• Go to a safe place away from the alleged offender. Note: You cannot file a 'Restricted Report' if you disclose a sexual assault to PMO/law enforcement and/or previously elected to make an Unrestricted Report by signing a DD Form 2910 on the same sexual assault incident.
• Preserve evidence of the assault. For instance:
   • Do not take a shower or a bath.
   • Do not wash your hands or brush your teeth.
   • Do not clean up or remove anything from the crime scene.
• Contact a Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC), or SAPR Victim Advocate (VA), who will:
   • Keep your report confidential.
   • Inform you of the Restricted & Unrestricted reporting options.
   • Provide you with resources and support.
• Seek medical care to take care of physical injuries, risk of pregnancy, or sexually-transmitted infections.
• Request a Sexual Assault Forensic Exam (SAFE) to collect evident from the assault.
• Consider a blood test or urinalysis if you suspect you were drugged. (Note: For unrestricted reports only)

**No matter where you are in the world, free and confidential help is available.**

Contact the DoD Safe Helpline - 24/7 Confidential Toll-free call at 1-877-995-5247 or at [www.safehelpline.org](http://www.safehelpline.org) and search by unit or installation name or zip code to find SAPR resources or rape crisis centers near you.

For those on or close to a USMC Installation, call your local 24/7 SAPR helpline.

## How 24/7 Support Lines Make A Difference
Survivors of military sexual assault are never alone – no matter when or where assistance is needed. Marines and their families have immediate access to resources and referrals by calling their installation's 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line.

The Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR) Victim Advocates (VAs) and Sexual Assault Response Coordinators (SARCs) who staff these support lines are dedicated to getting it right. A single phone call may be the only chance SAPR VAs or SARCs get to make a difference in the life of a survivor, so they are trained to give their best effort every time.

**24/7 Helpline For Your Local Installation**

Camp Lejeune – New River: 910-750-5852

**10 Things to Know about 24/7 Support**

1. **Anywhere** – Each United States Marine Corps (USMC) installation has a 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line to assist sexual assault survivors with appropriate care and critical information.
2. **Anytime** – 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines ring directly to cell phones held by the installation's SAPR VA or SARC.
3. **Knowledgeable** – All SAPR VAs and SARCs who answer the 24/7 Support Lines are credentialed by the Department of Defense (DOD) Sexual Assault Advocate Certification Program (D-SAACP).
4. **Dependable** – No call by a survivor ever goes unanswered. After five rings, a call to the 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line is automatically forwarded to the DOD Safe Helpline.
5. **Local** – After receiving a forwarded call, DOD Safe Helpline personnel will always try to connect the survivor back to the appropriate installation 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line.
6. **Supportive** – Whether assisted by DOD or the installation's SAPR VA or SARC, the survivor will always be provided with immediate crisis support and referrals to appropriate services.
7. **Personal** – If requested, a credentialed SAPR VA or SARC will meet with the survivor within two hours of the initial call for any reason related to the sexual assault.
8. **Confidential** – Calls to the 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines and the DOD Safe Helpline are strictly confidential.
9. **Professional** – 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines are audited monthly to make sure the response system is timely, efficient, and effective and to correct any identified issues.
10. **Quality Care** – The Marine Corps SAPR Program is committed to providing survivors of sexual assault with comprehensive, quality care.

24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines have connected hundreds of survivors with a trusted, confidential source of support since 2010. Whether looking for specific information or just someone to talk to about a sexual assault, round-the-clock help is just a phone call away.

If you are deployed or stationed at a non-USMC installation, contact your SAPR VA for assistance or call the DOD Safe Helpline at 1-877-995-5247.

## Supporting a Friend after Sexual Assault
You may have a friend, loved one, or family member who was sexually assaulted.

**DO listen.**
Sometimes the best thing you can do is just be a good listener.

**DO be patient.**
Recovery from trauma does not have a set timetable.

**DON'T judge.**
People who were sexually assaulted can be scrutinized or even blamed for what happened to them. The alleged offender is 100 percent responsible for the crime.

**DON'T ask for details.**
You don't need to know the "who, what, when, where, how and why" of the assault.

**DO use phrases such as:**
• "You're safe now" (only if that is true)
• "I'm glad you're talking to me."
• "I'm sorry it happened."
• "It wasn't your fault."
• "It's ok that you're reacting this way.
• "It must have been really upsetting to experience that."
• "I can't imagine how you must feel."

**DON'T use phrases such as:**
• "What were you wearing?"
• "How much did you have to drink?"
• "You're lucky that . . ."
• "It'll take some time, but you'll get over it."
• "I can imagine how you feel."
• "Don't worry; it's going to be all right."
• "Try to be strong for your children, spouse, etc."
• "Calm down and try to relax."

**DO ask if they are open to getting help.**
Ask if your friend is open to seeking medical care or talking to a Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC) or Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR) Victim Advocate (VA).

If your friend has just been through the assault, you may ask your friend about going to the SANE Emergency Department or offer to take your friend there yourself.

**DON'T leave them alone.**
People who are sexually assaulted are often overwhelmed with feelings, including fear, shock, helplessness, hopelessness, despair, anger, anxiety, panic, and even suicidal thoughts. Before you leave your friend, ask if you can call someone else to provide support, like a SARC or SAPR VA.

**DO take care of yourself.**
When we have a friend in need or in pain, it can be difficult not knowing how to help. [RAINN](https://www.rainn.org/articles/self-care-friends-and-family) (Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network), and the [SAFE Helpline](https://www.safehelpline.org/) have great self-care resources that can help you feel less overwhelmed.

For more information about how to help someone, visit the Sexual Assault Prevention and Response page or visit SAFE Helpline for more confidential services.

## I don't know where to start
When a victim of sexual assault decides to report, it's important to understand the options available.

**Who does the SAPR Program cover?**

The SAPR Program will continue to provide services to all adult sexual assault victims who are non-intimate partners and to adults of sexual assault who are unmarried intimate partners when they are not: a current or former spouse, share a child in common, currently or previously shared a domicile, and when domestic abuse is present. If the victim falls under one the categories (spouse/child/domicile/domestic abuse) the victim will be referred to Family Advocacy Program (FAP).

**Knowing Your Options**

Service members and military dependents (18 years and older) have two options when it comes to reporting sexual assault: Unrestricted or Restricted Reporting. The person will need to fill out a [DD Form 2910](https://www.esd.whs.mil/Directives/forms/dd2500_2999/) with assistance from a Sexual Assault Prevention & Response (SAPR) Victim Advocate (VA), or Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC).

**Unrestricted Reporting** - is recommended for someone who desires a law enforcement investigation, and the support of the chain of command; unrestricted reporting provides the person with access to ALL supportive service options:

• Advocacy Services (support, information, referral, and accompaniment)
• Medical/Counseling Services
• Victims Legal Counsel
• Military Protective Order
• Civilian Protective Order
• Expedited Transfer
• CATCH Program when the name of suspect is not known by law enforcement

For an **Unrestricted Report** - Someone can disclose a sexual assault to the following people:

• SAPR Victim Advocate
• Sexual Assault Response Coordinator
• Healthcare Personnel
• Chaplain
• Victims Legal Counsel
• Chain of Command
• Law Enforcement

With Unrestricted Report, knowledge of the sexual assault is limited to those with an official need-to-know.

In the event of an independent investigation that is initiated by a third party reporting from a source other than the victim. The victims can elect not to participate in the investigation by signing a 540k Victim Preference Letter. Speak to your SARC or SAPR VA for further information regarding the 540k Victim Preference Letter.

**Restricted Reporting** - is available for Service members and their SAPR eligible military dependents 18 years of age or older.

• Advocacy Services (support, information, referral, and accompaniment)
• Medical/Counseling Services
• Victims' Legal Counsel
• CATCH Program

A person who reported a sexual assault can choose to convert a Restricted Report to Unrestricted at any time.

One may still elect a Restricted Report if they did not personally report the sexual assault to law enforcement, including MCIOS, and/or did not previously elect to make an Unrestricted Report by signing a DD Form 2910 on the same sexual assault incident.

In the event a victim or third party discloses a Restricted Report to the command, it does not negate the command from the standard notification and reporting responsibilities.

For a **Restricted Report** - Some state and local laws require healthcare personnel to disclose sexual assault incidents to law enforcement. NDAA FY 16 Section 536 preempts mandatory reporting laws if the person reports to an MTF first, thereby preserving the Restricted Reporting option.

**Retaliation:**

The following individuals are eligible to report a retaliation in nexus to an Unrestricted Report to a SARC or SAPR VA via a signed DD Form 2910-2:

• Victims with an Unrestricted Report
• Adult sexual assault victim's adult family members
• Witnesses/Bystanders/1st Responders to include SARC and SAPR VAs

## Leaders Resources
As a leader, you may encounter a situation where there is a sexual assault in your unit.

**Command Leadership Responsibilities**

Per DoD policy, there are requirements that must be met to ensure the health and safety of survivors and to maintain unit cohesion through a positive command climate, if sexual assault occurs or is reported at your unit. [DoDI 6495.02](https://sapr.mil/policy) outlines in detail Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Program Procedures for the Department.

Service members have two reporting options: Restricted and Unrestricted. If a Service member discloses a sexual assault to law enforcement and/or previously elected to make an Unrestricted Report by signing a DD Form 2910 on the same sexual assault incident they are not eligible to make a Restricted Report. You can access the guide [here](https://www.sapr.mil/?q=reporting-options).

Survivors of sexual assault shall be protected from coercion, retaliation, and reprisal in accordance with DoDI 6495.02. Retaliation has no place in the military and you must do your part to ensure an ethical and just command intolerant of such behavior. For more information about retaliation, including reporting resources for survivors go to [Resources](https://www.hqmc.marines.mil/igmc/Resources/).

To help ensure a comprehensive and appropriate response, DoD SAPRO has compiled a checklist of what should happen within the first 30 days of a survivor's disclosure of sexual assault. You can access the checklist [here](https://www.sapr.mil/?q=toolkit-for-commanders-and-sarcs).

Throughout the military investigative and justice process, Service members who make an Unrestricted Report of sexual assault are entitled to certain rights. To learn more about these rights, please go to [Victims' Bill of Rights](https://www.sapr.mil/victims-bill-rights).

**Tips on How to Talk to a Survivor**

Knowing what to say after a survivor has disclosed an assault can be difficult.

**"I'm so sorry this happened to you."** Showing a survivor empathy can build rapport and trust between you and the survivor.

**"I'm here to help you get support."** A survivor trusted you and shared what happened to them.

**"How can I help?"** Let the survivor know that you are there for them.

This is not a comprehensive list of what you can say to a survivor to show empathy.

**What is Safe Helpline?**

Established in 2011, Safe Helpline is the Department of Defense's (DoD) sole hotline for members of the DoD community affected by sexual assault. Safe Helpline is a completely anonymous, confidential, 24/7, specialized service—providing help and information anytime, anywhere. A Safe Helpline user can access one-on-one support, peer-to-peer support, information, resources, and self-care exercises 24/7 to aid in their recovery.

**How Safe Helpline Can Support You and Your Unit**

**Telephone Helpline** - Our highly trained Safe Helpline staff are available to answer your questions, provide resources and get you contact information for a variety of on-base and off-base resources. You can connect with a staff member by calling 877-995-5247.

**Online Helpline** - The Online Helpline, an anonymous online platform, provides the same services as the Telephone Helpline described above. You can access the anonymous Online Helpline 24/7 by logging on to our website at [safehelpline.org](https://safehelpline.org/).

**Marine Corps Resources**

• Inspectors General Checklist SEXUAL ASSAULT PREVENTION AND RESPONSE PROGRAM (SAPR) (1752)
• Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR) Program Guidance

pages.text:
# MCCS Substance Misuse

## SUBSTANCE MISUSE RESOURCES
HOW CAN WE HELP YOU?

**800-662-HELP(4357)**

## Signs of a Drinking Problem
Recognizing patterns takes awareness.

**Changes in Body and Focus**

• Needing to drink more to feel the same effect or to cope with stress, or difficulty concentrating.
• Noticeable decline in physical health, recurring hangovers, or trouble staying focused on daily tasks.

**Friction in Relationships**

• Pulling away from the unit, friends, or family in favor of drinking alone.
• Increased arguments or tension with the people who matter most to you.

**Losing Your Way**

• Finding yourself making choices that don't align with the person you want to be.
• A persistent feeling of being "stuck," losing hope, or feeling like your work lost its meaning.

**Substance Misuse Assessment**

If you recognize these signs in yourself, a loved one, or friend, connect with a professional for confidential, non-clinical guidance.

**Need help now? Support is available 24/7.**

• Immediate danger: Call 911
• Crisis line: Dial 988 (press 1) or Chat Online: [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
• SAMSHA Helpline: 1-800-662-4357

## Regain Balance
Use these strategies to stay in control and reduce risks.

**Control Your Environment**

• Participate in activities that do not involve alcohol.
• Practice your "No" before heading out.

**Set Your Limits**

• Aim for no more than three standard drinks per occasion.
   • ➤ **Beer (5%):** 12 oz
   • ➤ **Wine (12%):** 5 oz
   • ➤ **Liquor (40%):** 1.5 oz
   • ➤ **Malt (7%):** 8 oz

**Protect Your Why**

• Keep your "why" visible on your phone as a consistent reminder of your priorities.
• Choosing environments and people that support your goals rather than testing your determination.

**Support Resources**

You do not have to regain your balance by doing it alone. Connect with professional support:

• [Community Counseling Program](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling)
• [Family Advocacy Program](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/family-advocacy-program)
• [Chaplains](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/chaplains-religious-enrichment-development-operation)
• [Military and Family Life Counseling (MFLC)](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/resources/tools/mflc-locator)
• [OSCAR](https://manpower.usmc.afpims.mil/Divisions/Marine-and-Family-Programs/Marine-Corps-Total-Fitness-Directorate/#combat-power-preservation)
• [Other resources](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling)

Contact your local installation to inquire about services.

**Need help now? Support is available 24/7.**

## Immediate Help and Support
You are not alone. Support is available 24/7.

**Call 911**

If you're in immediate danger or experiencing a crisis related to substance misuse, please call **911** or your local emergency services number.

**SAMSHA National Helpline**

Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMSHA) National Helpline: 1-800-662-4357

**988 Lifeline or Veterans Crisis Line**

• Call or Text: Dial 988 and Press 1.
• Chat Online: [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
• Text: Send a message to 838255 or 988

**Unit Support**

• Chaplains
• OSCAR Team
• Substance Assessment Coordinator Officer

**Military OneSource**

[Confidential counseling](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/confidential-counseling/) provides service members and their loved ones with resources and support to address a variety of issues and build important skills to tackle life's challenges.

## Support Others
Your encouragement can be the turning point for a fellow Marine or loved one.

**How to Start the Conversation**

• **Be Direct:** Share specific behaviors you've noticed and why you are worried.
• **Express Care:** Ensure the person knows your concern comes from a place of support.
• **Offer Support:** Offer to go with the person to seek professional care.

**Warning Signs of Medication Misuse**

The DoD maintains a zero-tolerance policy for illicit substances.

• **Unauthorized Use:** Taking medication prescribed for someone else.
• **Incorrect Dosage:** Taking a larger dose or using it longer than prescribed.
• **Improper Administration:** Crushing, snorting, or injecting medication.
• **Unknown Substances:** Consuming any substance without knowing its exact contents.
• **Expired Medication:** Using old or expired prescriptions.

For more information, see [SECNAVINST 5300.28F.](https://www.secnav.navy.mil/doni/Directives/05000%20General%20Management%20Security%20and%20Safety%20Services/05-300%20Manpower%20Personnel%20Support/5350.4E.pdf)

Need help now? Support is available 24/7.

• Immediate danger: Call 911
• Crisis line: Dial 988 (press 1) or Chat Online: [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
• SAMSHA Helpline: 1-800-662-4357
• Military OneSource: 1-800-342-9647

## Leaders' Resources
Leaders, you are the first line of defense in maintaining the wellness and readiness of your units.

**Foster a Healthy Culture**

• **Lead by Example:** Demonstrate and encourage healthy coping mechanisms for stress, such as exercise and open communication, rather than turning to alcohol.
• **De-glamorize Alcohol:** Shift the focus away from alcohol at unit events and gatherings.

**Know the Warning Signs**

• **Performance:** Unexplained drop in work quality or tardiness.
• **Appearance:** Decline in personal hygiene or unkempt uniform.
• **Behavior:** Personality shifts, mood outbursts, or high-risk actions.

**Combat Stigma**

• **Engage with Empathy:** When you notice a Marine is struggling, engage with the individual in a supportive and non-judgmental manner, avoiding negative labels.
• **Challenge Stereotypes:** Actively challenge and correct negative stereotypes or inappropriate comments made about individuals with alcohol-related problems.
• **Promote Self-Referral:** Make it known that voluntarily help-seeking is a sign of strength and is designed to be career-safe.

**Take Action**

• **Refer for Screening:** Direct the Marine to a Substance Assessment and Counseling Center for professional assessment at the first sign of a problem.
• **Follow Up:** Continue to support and check in on the Marine.

**Policies & Tools**

**Policies**

• **DoDI 1010.04:** Establishes enterprise-wide substance misuse policy.
• **DoDI 1010.01 & 1010.16:** Directs military drug testing programs.
• **MCO 5300.17A:** Provides policy and procedural requirements for the Substance Assessment and Counseling Program (SACP)

**Unit Support**

• Substance Assessment Coordinator Officer
• Chaplains
• Embedded Preventive Integrated Capability (EPIC)
• OSCAR Team
• Primary Prevention Integrators (PPI)

**Online Resource**

[National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism](https://www.niaaa.nih.gov/) supports and conducts research on the impact of alcohol use on human health and well-being.

**Related Articles**

• [Binge Drinking: What You Need to Know and How to Prevent It](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/news/binge-drinking-what-you-need-to-know-and-how-to-prevent-it)
• [Five Practical Tips for Low-Risk Drinking](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/news/five-practical-tips-for-low-risk-drinking)
• [Less Alcohol/More Fitness Gains](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/news/less-alcohol-more-fitness-gains)
• [Protect What You've Earned - Know the Signs of Alcohol Misuse](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/news/protect-what-youve-earned-know-the-signs-of-alcohol-misuse)
• [Alcohol and the Body](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/news/alcohol-and-the-body)

## Prevention Briefs Offered
**Low-Risk Substance Abuse Brief (General)**

This presentation focuses on low-risk substance misuse education tailored for the military population.

**DWI Laws and Regulations**

This presentation provides a comprehensive overview of DWI (Driving While Intoxicated) laws and regulations as they apply to military personnel. It covers the legal consequences at both the civilian and military levels, including UCMJ implications and impacts on career and security clearances.

**Delta 8/9, Hemp**

This presentation explores the legal and health implications of THC and hemp use for military personnel.

**Trending Drugs/Prohibited Drugs**

This presentation explores trending and prohibited drugs within the military, focusing on their impact on readiness, discipline, and overall force health. Attendees will gain a clear understanding of the consequences of drug use and the importance of maintaining a drug-free force to ensure mission success and unit cohesion.

**Vaping/ "Catch My Breath"**

"Catch My Breath" is a prevention program designed to educate about the dangers of vaping and empower individuals to make healthy choices.

**Prime For Life (PFL) 4.5 (4 hr. 30 min class)**

This curriculum empowers commanding officers to deliver interactive substance abuse training at the unit level, facilitated by certified PFL trainers from the Substance Abuse Counseling Program (SACP).

**"Rethink that Drink" Tour (2-4 hours)**

Cultivating conversations and awareness about the consequences of alcohol misuse and encouraging learners to make no risk or low risk choices.

## Additional Briefs
**Marine Corps Total Fitness & Wellness**

Focusing on the DoDs Operation Supplement Safety and Marine Corps Total Fitness, a new set of briefs focused on overall health and wellness of the marine with a focus on how their substances affect their athletic performance and mental health.

• Substance Misuse and Athletic Performance

• What's in your pre-workout?

HIIT Pockets (10-15 min briefs associated with PT or other physical workouts)

**Problem Gambling & Sports Betting**

This presentation explores the growing issue of sports betting and problem gambling within the military community.

pages.title: MCCS Suicide Prevention
pages.text:
# MCCS Suicide Prevention

## Suicide Prevention Resources
**Call or Text:** Dial 988 and Press 1

**Chat Online:** [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)

**Text:** Send a message to 838255 or 988

## How Can We Help You?
• I need to talk to someone
• I have thoughts of suicide
• I want to help someone else
• Leaders resources
• Prevention skills you can use

## I'm Having Thoughts of Suicide
If you are struggling or in pain, you don't have to face it alone.

**How to Connect:**

• **Call or Text:** Dial 988 and Press 1
• **Chat Online:** Veterans Crisis Line or 988 Lifeline
• **Text:** Send a message to 838255 or 988
• **Talk to Someone:** Reach out to your Chaplain or a trusted friend immediately

## International Dialing (OCONUS)
If you are calling from a DSN phone, dial 988. If calling from off-base:

• **Northern Command:** Dial 988 then Press 1
• **Indo-Pacific Command:** +1 844-702-5493
• **European Command:** +1 844-702-5495
• **Central Command:** +1 855-422-7719
• **Africa Command:** +1 888-482-6054
• **Southern Command:** +1 866-989-9599

If you are OCONUS without a U.S. phone plan, use the online chat at Veterans Crisis Line. These services are free, confidential, and available 24/7.

## Create a Safe Space
When you feel overwhelmed, your brain may tell you that things will never change.

**Secure Your Firearms**

Firearms are the most lethal method of suicide.

• **Off-site Storage:** Use your unit armory, a local gun shop, or a shooting range
• **Lock It Up:** Use a cable lock or trigger lock and give the key to a trusted friend
• **Ask for Help:** Contact your Suicide Prevention Program Coordinator (SPPC) or Officer (SPPO) for local options

**Manage Medications**

Keep medications locked and safely dispose of unneeded pills using these methods:

• **The Bag Method:** Mix pills with coffee grounds or kitty litter in a sealed bag and throw it in the trash
• **Drop-off Locations:** Take them to any military or local pharmacy. Find a location at [Safe.Pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/drug-disposal/)

**Identify Other Risks**

Think about your home.

## Unit Support
The Marines in your unit know what you're facing and are ready to help.

• **Chaplains:** 100% confidential support for any life challenge
• **OSCAR Team Members:** Peer-to-peer support from fellow Marines trained to identify stress
• **Mental Health Providers:** Direct clinical care within your medical network
• **Resilience & Wellness Specialists:** Experts focused on mental fitness and proactive health
• **Suicide Prevention Officers:** Your unit's primary contact for prevention resources

## Community Support
You belong to a community of families and professionals dedicated to your resilience.

• **[Military & Family Life Counselors](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/benefits/military-family-life-counseling-program/):** For non-medical, confidential counseling
• **[Community Counselors](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling):** Clinical counseling for individuals, couples, and families within the MCCS network
• **[Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/):** 24/7 access to specialized support for all aspects of Marine Life
• **[Semper Support](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/semper-support):** Free counseling sessions accessible from anywhere, on your schedule

**MCCS is Here for You**

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is committed to your well-being.

Connect to local base resources at [usmc-mccs.org](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/).

## I Want to Help Someone Else
If you believe a fellow Marine, friend, or loved one is in immediate danger, **do not leave them alone.** Please share the information below immediately:

**How to Connect:**

**International Dialing (OCONUS)** — same numbers as above; if OCONUS without a U.S. phone plan, use the online chat at Veterans Crisis Line.

## Step 1: Know the Signs
Trust your instincts and monitor for behavioral changes that often follow a challenging life event or loss.

**Listen for what the person says:**

• **Being a Burden:** "Everyone would be better off without me"
• **Hopelessness:** "There's no way out" or "I just want the pain to stop"
• **Finality:** Making statements about saying goodbye or talking about death (including dark humor)

**Watch for what the person does:**

• **Seeking Means:** Looking for firearms, pills, or other lethal items
• **Withdrawal Socially:** Backing away from the unit, friends, or family
• **Performance Drops:** Sudden decline in work, fitness, or personal hygiene
• **Mood Shifts:** Extreme agitation or sudden, unexplained "calm"

## Step 2: Use the A.C.T. Tool
**Ask:** "How are you feeling?" ...

**Care:** Listen actively, with respect. No judgement. Let them know they're not alone.

**Take Action:** Secure lethal means. Connect them with mentors, leaders, and resources.

## Step 3: Share Support Resources
**Unit Support**

• **Chaplains:** 100% confidential support
• **OSCAR Team Members:** Peer-to-peer identification of stress
• **Mental Health Providers:** Direct clinical care
• **SPPC/SPPO:** Your unit's primary contact for prevention

**Community Support**

• **Military & Family Life Counselors:** For non-medical, confidential counseling
• **Community Counselors:** Clinical counseling for individuals, couples, and families within the MCCS network
• **Military OneSource:** 24/7 access to specialized support for all aspects of Marine Life
• **Semper Support:** Free counseling sessions accessible from anywhere, on your schedule

**MCCS is Here for You**

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is committed to your well-being.

Connect to local base resources at usmc-mccs.org.

## Leaders Resources
**Seeking Help Is a Sign of Strength**

As a leader, you play a critical role in educating your Marines and their families about suicide prevention and mental fitness. You must foster an environment where seeking help is seen as essential to maintaining readiness and well-being.

If you believe one of your Marines is in danger, **do not leave them alone.** Please share the information below immediately:

**The Military & Veterans Crisis Line**

Free, confidential, and available 24/7 for Service members and their families.

• **Call or Text:** Dial 988 and Press 1
• **Chat Online:** Veterans Crisis Line or 988 Lifeline
• **Text:** Send a message to 838255 or 988

**International Dialing (OCONUS)** — If you are calling from a DSN phone, dial 988. If calling from off-base: Northern Command: Dial 988 then Press 1; Indo-Pacific Command: +1 844-702-5493; European Command: +1 844-702-5495; Central Command: +1 855-422-7719; Africa Command: +1 888-482-6054; Southern Command: +1 866-989-9599. phone plan, use the Veterans Crisis Line online chat.

## Step 1: Identify Risk in Your Unit
Suicide and self-harm are often associated with stressors like relationship distress, work performance issues, pending legal actions, or transitions in duty status.

**Listen for what the person says:**

**Watch for what the person does:**

• **Seeking Means:** Looking for firearms, pills, or other lethal items
• **Withdrawal Socially:** Isolation, backing away from the unit, friends, or family
• **Performance Drops:** Sudden decline in work, fitness, or personal hygiene
• **Mood Shifts:** Extreme agitation, reckless behavior, or unexplained "calm"
• **Digital Cues:** Posting self-destructive or hopeless content on social media

**Command Individual Risk & Resiliency Assessment System (CIRRAS)**

Use the Marines Corps' official system of record to proactively identify and manage risk and resiliency factors.

• **Standardize Force Preservation:** Access transferable data on risk factors during PCS moves
• **Inform Leadership Decisions:** Use real-time data to drive Force Preservation Councils (FPC)
• **Train Your Team:** Ensure subordinate leaders are proficient in using CIRRAS securely

## Step 2: Use the A.C.T. Tool (Leaders)
**Ask:** "How are you feeling?" ...

Don't avoid the question. Don't be afraid of the answer.

**Take Action:** Secure lethal means.

## Step 3: Use Command Resources, Assets, and Support
**[The Warfighter Mental Readiness Playbook](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=ab2955d1-7357-42a5-839b-282b3b018703&v=4)**

Use this playbook to foster a culture where mental readiness is prioritized. It includes:

• **Effective Conversations:** Strategies for talking to Marines in need
• **Mental Health Roadmap:** A clear path for navigating care and resources
• **Commander Assets:** Tools to foster unit connection and well-being

**Command Assets**

• **Chaplains:** 100% confidential support for any life challenge
• **OSCAR Team Members:** Peer-to-peer identification and stress management
• **Mental Health Providers:** Direct clinical care within your medical network
• **Resilience & Wellness Specialists:** Experts focused on mental fitness and social skill building
• **SPPC/SPPO:** Your unit's primary contact for prevention resources and local safety

**Community Support**

• **Military & Family Life Counselors:** For non-medical, confidential counseling
• **Community Counselors:** Clinical counseling within the MCCS network
• **Military OneSource:** 24/7 access to specialized support for all aspects of Marine Life
• **Semper Support:** Free counseling accessible from anywhere, on your schedule

**MCCS is Here for You**

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is committed to your well-being.

Connect to local base resources at usmc-mccs.org.

pages.text:
# MCCS Free Barracks Wi-Fi

Stay connected to what matters. Free barracks Wi-Fi just got a major upgrade. MCCS, in partnership with MCICOM, is now providing eligible Marines in participating barracks aboard Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River with download speeds of up to 100 Mbps, up from the previous 1 Mbps service, at no cost.

Stay connected with family and friends, take an online class, stream your favorites, game with friends, or enjoy your downtime.

• Up to 100 Mbps download speeds
• Up to 20 Mbps upload speeds
• Free filtered Wi-Fi
• No monthly cost

## CONNECTION IS PART OF TOTAL FITNESS
Wi-Fi does more than help you get online.

Marine Corps Total Fitness recognizes Social Fitness as an important part of overall well-being. [Learn more about Marine Corps Total Fitness and Social Fitness](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/news/why-marine-corps-total-fitness).

## GETTING CONNECTED IS EASY
1. From inside a participating barracks, select the MCCS Free WiFi network on your device.
2. Open your web browser.
3. Follow the on-screen instructions to create your free account.

Each free account supports up to three devices.

NEED TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE? Boingo 24/7 Customer Support: 1-866-726-4646.

## Frequently Asked Questions
**Who is eligible?**
Eligible Marines residing in participating barracks; availability varies by location.

**How much does it cost?**
The complimentary service is provided at no cost to eligible Marines.

**Can I connect multiple devices?**
Yes, up to three per free account.

**Can I use my account elsewhere?**
Yes, at participating Marine Corps installations when connected to MCCS Free WiFi.

**What if I cannot connect?**
Verify that you are inside a participating barracks, connected to MCCS Free WiFi and following registration prompts.

Contact: Boingo 24/7 Customer Support
Phone (Customer Support): 1-866-726-4646

# MCCS Transition Readiness Program

We prepare Marines for the civilian workforce through the Transition Readiness Program by providing guidance and training for transitioning success.

## Steps to Success
#### Step One: Individualized Initial Counseling

**Complete the Individualized Initial Counseling (IC) no later than 365 days prior to EAS date.**

• Contact your Unit Transition Coordinator (UTC) for IC pre-work instructions and assistance with scheduling IC with your installation's TRP office.

**IC pre-work requirements include:**

• Launching your DD Form 2648
• Registration on VA.gov
• Downloading your VMET and JST
• Completing the NAVMC 17031
• Review of the [Pre-Separation Counseling Resource Guide](https://www.tapevents.mil/Assets/ResourceContent/TAP/Pre_Separation_Counseling_Resource_Guide.pdf)
• Completion of the virtual Reserve Obligations and Opportunities Brief (ROOB)
• Update personal email address in MOL

#### Step Two: Pre-Separation Counseling Brief

**Attend the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief no later than 365 days prior to your EAS date.**

• You must complete your IC before attending the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief.
• The Pre-Separation Counseling Brief is an in-person class which provides high level information on the many benefits, services, resources, and programs available during and after transition.
• Contact your UTC or TRP office for assistance with scheduling your attendance to the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief.

#### Step Three: Transition Readiness Seminar Courses

**Attend the Transition Readiness Seminar (TRS) courses no later than 180 days prior to your EAS date.**

• You must complete the Individual Initial Counseling (IC) and attend the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief to register for the TRS courses.
• Contact your UTC for assistance with scheduling your attendance to the TRS courses.

#### Step Four: Capstone Review

**Conduct Capstone Review no later than 120 days prior to your EAS date.**

• You must attend all the TRS courses before you can complete the Capstone Review.
• You and a TRP Advisor will review your completion of all mandated Career Readiness Standards (CRS) and discuss your transition plans.
• Your DD Form 2648 will be forwarded to your commander or commander's designee at the conclusion of Capstone Review.
• You must contact your UTC or TRP office to schedule your Commander's Verification.

#### Step Five: Commander's Verification

**Complete Commander's Verification no later than 90 days prior to your EAS date.**

• You must complete the Capstone Review before the Commander's Verification.
• At Commander's Verification, your CO or designee will validate your overall preparedness to transition and will conduct any warm handovers to services or resources as needed based on your transition plan.
• Your CO or designee will digitally sign your DD Form 2648 at the conclusion of Commander's Verification.
• You will need to provide a copy of your completed and signed DD Form 2648 to your UTC.
• You will also need to provide a copy to IPAC in order to receive your DD214.

## Programs, Resources & Support
Get started on your steps for the Transition Readiness Seminar with a detailed checklist, documents, and downloads, preparing you for success as you begin your transition from military service to civilian life.

## Getting Started
Your success transitioning from Military service to civilian life depends on you being proactive, persistent, and prepared.

**Individual Initial Counseling Check List**

• Launching your DD Form 2648
• Registration on VA.gov
• Downloading your VMET and JST
• Completing the NAVMC 17031
• Review of the Pre-Separation Counseling Resource Guide
• Completion of the virtual Reserve Obligations and Opportunities Brief (ROOB)
• Update personal email address in MOL

**Tier Level Checklist**

• Tier Level 1
• Tier Level 2
• Tier Level 3

**[Participant Guide](https://www.tapevents.mil/resources/documents/)**

• Review Pre-Separation Counseling Resources
• Pre-Separation Counseling Guide
• Managing Your (MY) Transition
• Military Occupational Code (MOC) Crosswalk
• Employment Fundamentals of Career Transition
• VA Benefits & Services
• Employment Track: DOL Employment Workshop (DOLEW)
• DOL Career & Credential Exploration (C2E) Vocational
• Managing Your (MY) Education (MYEd)

## Direct Affiliation Program
Marines transitioning to the Marine Corps Reserve through the [Direct Affiliation Program](https://www.manpower.marines.mil/Manpower-Management/Enlisted-Assignments/Stay-Marine/Direct-Affiliation-Program/) qualify for up to a $25K signing bonus, choice of duty station, and lateral move opportunities.

## SkillBridge
[SkillBridge](https://skillbridge.osd.mil/) connects Marines to real job opportunities, offering training, apprenticeships, or internships for civilian work experience.

## Marine For Life Network
Marine For Life Network (M4L) connects transitioning Marines and their family members to education resources, employment opportunities, and other Veterans services that aid in their career and life goals outside of military service.

## Personal Financial Management Program
A solid understanding of personal finances will prepare Marines and their family members for a successful transition from military service to civilian life - building confidence when facing financial challenges and responsibilities. Connect with the PFMP office today!

## Contact Information and Resources
• [Distribution Management Office (DMO)](https://www.lejeune.marines.mil/Offices-Staff/Distribution-Mgmt/)
• [Regional Personnel Administration Center (RPAC Outbounds)](https://www.lejeune.marines.mil/Offices-Staff/Regional-Personnel-Administration-Center/Personnel-Support-Branch/Outbounds/)
• [Marine for Life](http://www.usmc-mccs.org/services/career/marine-for-life-network/)
• [NC4ME](https://www.nc4me.org/)

pages.title: Marine For Life Network
pages.text:
# Marine For Life Network

We connect transitioning Marines, family members, and veterans to educational resources, employment opportunities, and services that support their career and life goals.

## Connect with a Regional Network Manager
Receive professional support and valuable information.

• I am a transitioning Marine wanting to connect to resources.
• I am a family member wanting to grow my network.
• I am a veteran wanting support and services.
• I am a military-friendly resource wanting to support and mentor Marines.

## Marine For Life Network Representatives
Supporting your journey from military service to civilian careers.

Marine For Life Network Representatives (M4L Reps) are dedicated to supporting transitioning Marines, veterans, and their families by connecting them to a strong network of military-friendly resources and opportunities.

With Marine Individually Mobilization Augmentee (IMA) Reservists strategically located across the country, M4L Reps offer expert guidance and support to help you navigate the shift from military to civilian life.

**Why Connect with a M4L Rep?**

• **Personalized Networking Support** - Our M4L Reps offer one-on-one guidance to help you expand your professional network.
• **Build Local Networks for Career Success** - Each M4L Rep builds and maintains a network of Marine-friendly employers, veteran services, and resources within 100-150 miles of their location.
• **Mentorship and Leadership** - With military and civilian career experience, M4L Reps provide mentorship to help you navigate civilian networking challenges.
• **Monthly Networking Events** - M4L Reps host monthly networking events where Marines, veterans, and local community members can connect and explore career opportunities.
• **Advocacy and Ongoing Support** - M4L Reps are committed to advocating for you throughout your transition and beyond military service.
• **Building a Network for Success** - The Marine For Life Network ensures you have access to tools, knowledge, and connections needed to thrive in civilian life.

## Regional Industries Highlights
Exploring the unique opportunities each region has to offer.

**West** - The West Region is a prime location for tech careers, with Silicon Valley in California and tech centers in Washington offering plenty of opportunities.

**Southeast** - In the Southeast Region, manufacturing is a key industry, especially in automotive, aerospace, and electronics in states like Alabama, South Carolina, and Georgia.

**Central** - The Central Region offers strong opportunities in manufacturing, particularly in automotive, steel, and machinery, with a focus in Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana.

**Northeast** - The Northeast Region is a key hub for finance and insurance, with major centers in New York City and Boston.

## Grow Your LinkedIn Network
Connecting with professionals and resources.

Join the Marine for Life Network regional LinkedIn groups for resources specific to the following states:

• **[Northeast Region Group](https://www.linkedin.com/groups/5145719)** - Pennsylvania, Ohio, New Jersey, New York, Delaware, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Vermont, Maine
• **[Southeast Region Group](https://www.linkedin.com/groups/6778386)** - Maryland, DC, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, West Virginia, Kentucky, Tennessee, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Florida
• **[Central Region Group](https://www.linkedin.com/groups/5145715)** - Texas, Louisiana, Missouri, Nebraska, Arkansas, Iowa, Kansas, Oklahoma, Minnesota, South Dakota, North Dakota
• **[West Region Group](https://www.linkedin.com/groups/6777653)** - California, Arizona, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Colorado, New Mexico, Idaho, Utah, Montana, Alaska
• **[National Group](https://www.linkedin.com/groups/5145640/)**

## Transition Readiness Resources
Navigate your military to civilian career transition with professional support.

• **Transition Readiness** - Preparing Marines for the civilian workforce
• **DoD SkillBridge** - Industry partners offer training and work experience for future employment
• **Information, Referral & Relocation** - Connect to valuable resources and services
• **Direct Affiliation** - Marines transitioning to the Marine Corps Reserve qualify for up to a $25K signing bonus
• **Leadership Scholar** - Enroll into a college or university after you transition from the Marine Corps
• **M4LN Newsletter** - Highlighting tools, resources, and view upcoming events

## Life Skill-building Resources
Develop essential skills for personal and professional growth.

• **Voluntary Education** - Whether you're looking to earn a college degree, obtain a certification, or improve your skills, there are resources designed to support your personal and professional growth.
• **Tuition Assistance** - Your tuition costs could be covered, up to 100%! The Tuition Assistance Program is designed to help active duty service members pursue higher education, develop new skills, and enhance their career opportunities.
• **Marine Corps COOL** - Your military skills and experience could provide you with credentials, certifications, and licenses.
• **Family Member Employment Assistance** - Empowering military spouses and families with career readiness tools, resources, and services.
• **Managing Your Stress** - Transitioning from military to civilian life can be a challenging process.
• **Personal Financial Management** - Prepare for financial changes with budgeting, savings, and managing transitioning expenses.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find quick answers to commonly asked questions.

**What is the Marine for Life Network?**
The Marine for Life Network is a resource and support network designed to assist transitioning Marines, veterans, and their families with employment, education, and community reintegration.

**What services does the Marine for Life Network provide?**
The Marine for Life Network provides a variety of services, including career counseling, job search assistance, networking opportunities, educational resources, and connections to local community support.

**How can the Marine for Life Network help with my job search?**
The network connects you with employers who value military experience, provides resume and interview preparation assistance, and offers access to job fairs and networking events.

**Can I join the Marine for Life Network if I'm still on active duty?**
Yes, transitioning Marines can join the network while still active duty.

**Is there a cost to join the Marine for Life Network?**
No, the Marine for Life Network is a free resource available to Marines, veterans, and their families.

Contact: Marine For Life Network
Phone (Call): 910-451-3781
Email: m4lops@usmc.mil
Hours:
- Sunday: CLOSED
- Monday–Friday: 8AM - 4PM
- Saturday: CLOSED
Holiday hours may vary.

Related pages:
