pages.text:
# SkillBridge

Connecting Marines to real job opportunities – offering training, apprenticeships, or internships for civilian work experience.

## Eligibility & Getting Started
Begin your journey toward a rewarding career.

#### Eligibility Requirements

Eligibility for participation in the SkillBridge includes:

• Active Duty Service Members

Participation in the SkillBridge program is not an entitlement and is at the commander's discretion based on the needs of the Marine Corps and mission requirements.

You are encouraged to attend the SkillBridge Information Session to learn how to successfully navigate through the SkillBridge program.

**Eligibility Requirements**

• Marines who have served a minimum of 180 days on active duty and received honorable discharge, including general discharge (under honorable conditions) within 180 days.
• Marines in the process of separating or retiring, must ensure adequate time remaining on contract prior to EAS by identifying their Category type, permitted timeline and final approval authorities for SkillBridge Program participation.
• Complete the Transition Readiness Seminar requirements at least 180 days before separation.
• Obtain command approval before participating in a Marine Corps SkillBridge program. Information on how to apply through your command will be provided during the SkillBridge Information Session.
• Marines enrolled in the Individual Disability Evaluation System or assigned to the Wounded Warrior Transition Program will require Commander consideration and approval of a SkillBridge Program packet and a separation date within 180 days.

**Timelines for SkillBridge Participation and Approval Authority**

The following indicates the maximum amount of time before your actual separation or retirement date that you can begin the program, pending the required approval from the appropriate authority.

• **Category I (E1-E5)**: up to 120 days, requires approval from Commanders at the grade of O5 or above.
• **Category II (E6-E7, WO-CWO3, O1-O4)**: up to 90 days, requires approval from Commanders at the grade of O5 or above.
• **Category III (E8-E9, W4-W5, O5 and above)**: up to 90 days or less, requires General Officer approval and Marine's SkillBridge participation must not result in a gapped billet.

**Program Policy and Guidance:**

• NAVMC 1700.2B
• [MARADMIN: 280/24](https://www.marines.mil/News/Messages/Messages-Display/Article/3809908/interim-guidance-on-the-implementation-of-the-skillbridge-program/)
• DoDI 1322.29

#### Application Process

Learn how to successfully submit your SkillBridge application.

The application process may vary from installation to installation.

We encourage you to contact your SkillBridge coordinator and attend the SkillBridge Information Session before you process your application.

**Selection / Acceptance**

Applying does not guarantee your acceptance with a SkillBridge industry partner. Please adhere to the due dates and any additional information required.

**Your Responsibility**

You will be responsible for contacting the specific SkillBridge industry partner directly for information; a SkillBridge Coordinator will guide you through the application process. Authorization is obtained by uploading your packet and routing through NCMIS for final approval from your CO.

1. **Attend the SkillBridge Brief** - Participate in the mandatory brief at your installation.
2. **Confirm Eligibility** - Ensure you meet the eligibility criteria for the SkillBridge program.
3. **Command Approval** - Discuss your interest in SkillBridge with your command to obtain their support.
4. **Check-Out/Separation Coordination** - Connect with your local administrative office regarding check-out/separation procedures.
5. **Research SkillBridge Opportunities** - Explore and apply to MOU-approved DoD SkillBridge organizations that match your career goals.
6. **Selection/Acceptance** - Receive confirmation of your acceptance into a DoD-approved SkillBridge opportunity.
7. **Complete Application Packet** - Gather and complete all necessary documents for the SkillBridge application.
8. **Submit for Review** - Submit your completed packet to your installation's SkillBridge office for review and conditional approval.
9. **Command Authorization** - Submit your application through MyMarineEducation for final command authorization.
10. **Finalize Your Approval** - Download and print your SkillBridge Approval Document from MyMarineEducation.

**Downloads**

• Sample Program Acceptance Letter

You must provide an acceptance letter for the program you are attending. The letter must include dates, times, location and a point of contact for the training.

#### Information Session

Your first step to successfully navigating through SkillBridge.

We want to help you successfully transition into the civilian workforce by using the SkillBridge DoD-approved opportunities.

We encouraged you to attend the SkillBridge Information Session to learn essential details about the program:

• Eligibility Requirements
• Available DoD-Approved SkillBridge Opportunities
• How to Successfully Navigate the Application Process

During the session, you'll gain a comprehensive understanding of the program's requirements, timelines, and the commitment involved.

The session also offers a chance to ask questions, ensuring that you are fully informed before moving forward with any applications. Completion of the SkillBridge Information Session is required before you can engage with the program or submit any further documentation, making it a crucial step in your transition journey.

View the calendar section of this webpage or contact your local SkillBridge representative for session dates and times.

## Program Resources
#### SkillBridge Coordinators

Connect with SkillBridge coordinators to explore opportunities and receive guidance throughout your transition to civilian life.

If you are currently not located on a Marine Corps base, please contact the SkillBridge coordinator nearest to your location.

• Camp Blaz: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Camp Elmore: careerservices.mccshr@usmc-mccs.org
• Camp Fuji: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Camp Lejeune - New River: clnrskillbridge@usmc.mil
• Camp Mujuk: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Henderson Hall: HNHL_Skillbridge@usmc.mil
• MARFORRES: mfreducation@usmc.mil
• MCAGCC 29 Palms: plmsppd@usmc.mil
• MCAS Beaufort: bfrt_Vol__ed@usmc.mil
• MCAS Cherry Point: CherryPoint.SkillBridge@usmc-mccs.org
• MCAS Iwakuni: ombiwakuni.transitionreadiness@usmc-mccs.org
• MCAS Miramar: smbmiramarmccs.skillbridge@usmc.mil
• MCB Hawaii: mcbh.skillbridge.smb@usmc.mil
• MCB Quantico: mccs_quantico_tamp@usmc.mil
• MCB Albany: MCLBASkillbridge@usmc.mil
• MCI-West Camp Pendleton: CPSDP@USMC.MIL
• MCMWTC Bridgeport: plmsppd@usmc.mil
• MCRD San Diego: mcrdsd.wrr-trp@usmc.mil
• MCRD Parris Island: parr_Vol_ed@usmc.mil
• Okinawa- Camp Courtney: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Okinawa- Camp Foster: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Okinawa- Camp Hansen: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Okinawa- Camp Kinser: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Okinawa- Camp Schwab: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Okinawa - MCAS Futenma: skillbridge@okinawa.usmc-mccs.org
• Yuma: MCASYumaSkillBridge@usmc.mil

#### Industry Training

Industry training programs offer a chance for service members to gain industry-specific skills, certifications, and work experience through internships, apprenticeships, on-the-job training, and classroom instruction with approved civilian employers.

**Apprenticeship** - On-the-job training means learning both the hands-on and theoretical parts of a skilled job through a mix of practical experience and related lessons.

**Employment Skills Training** - Job skills training means training or education for job skills required by an employer to provide an individual with the ability to obtain employment.

**Internships** - A system of on-the-job-training offered by a JTEST-AI provider to eligible service members to develop jobs skills and employment skills training.

**On the Job Training** - A method of preparing teaching employees how to perform tasks by showing them, letting them try, and giving feedback.

**Pre-Apprenticeship** - Programs that offer an overview of trades, including qualifications, skills, and on-the-job-training and related instruction.

#### DOW SkillBridge

Explore DOW-approved SkillBridge opportunities.

## Skill-Building Resources
#### Earn a Degree

Advance your education while serving!

Visit your Education Center and speak with a coordinator.

#### Enroll in a University or College

Earn a degree after you transition from the Marine Corps.

The [Leadership Scholar Program](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/news/leadership-scholar-program-how-can-marines-prepare-to-go-to-selective-colleges-and-universities) is a valuable resource for service members seeking to leverage their military experience into academic success and civilian career opportunities.

Service members interested in the Leadership Scholar Program should start by visiting the Volunteer Education and speaking to an education coordinator or the Transition Assistance Program coordinator.

#### Credentialing Opportunities Online

Your military skills and experience could provide you with credentials, certifications, and licenses.

The [Credentialing Opportunities Program](https://www.cool.osd.mil/usmc/index.html) is an excellent way to leverage your military experience and prepare for a successful career both within the Marine Corps and in civilian life.

Marines interested in the COOL program should visit their local Volunteer Education Center and speak to an education coordinator to explore available credentials, understand the application process, and get started on obtaining valuable certifications and licenses.

#### Budgeting for Your Future

Learn how to save and manage expenses during and after your transition.

We can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing expenses during and after your transition. (Personal Financial Management)

#### Managing Stress

Transitioning can be a complex and challenging process, both professionally and personally.

Establish a connection with professionals from your Community Counseling Program and discover a successful journey toward overcoming life's challenges.

## FAQs
Find information and get quick answers to common questions.

**How do I verify which DOW SkillBridge organization I am eligible for?**
Marines may only participate with MOU-approved DOW SkillBridge organizations. Verify that participation will take place prior to the MOU-expiration date by identifying the MOU-expiration date by visiting, [www.skillbridge.mil/organizations](https://www.skillbridge.mil/organizations)

**Will I get paid during the SkillBridge program?**
Yes, service members continue to receive their military pay and benefits during the SkillBridge program, as they remain on active duty while participating in the program.

**Do I have to accept a job offer from the SkillBridge program?**
No, there is no obligation to accept a job offer from the SkillBridge program.

**Can SkillBridge participation delay my separation date?**
No, participation in SkillBridge does not delay your separation date.

**Can I relocate for a SkillBridge program?**
Yes, relocation for a SkillBridge program is possible, but it requires command approval and coordination. Any relocation costs are typically the responsibility of the service member unless otherwise arranged with the SkillBridge provider.

**Can I participate in SkillBridge while on terminal leave?**
No, SkillBridge participation is not allowed while on terminal leave. The program must be completed before starting terminal leave, as it is designed to be an active duty training opportunity.

**Is there a cost associated with SkillBridge?**
While the SkillBridge program itself is offered at no cost to service members, there are instances where industry partners may require the use of benefits like the GI Bill.

Contact: SkillBridge Program
Email: clnrskillbridge@usmc.mil

pages.title: Voluntary Education
pages.text:
# Voluntary Education

We provide professional guidance, tools, and support to help you successfully reach your education and career goals.

[Book an Appointment with an Education Advisor](https://eventactions.com/eareg.aspx?ea=Rsvp&invite=g8bp1k71mke3xjc5egf7ajv2adnz912ed1re2exw9n5mh0dcma1r)

## Getting Started Is Easy
Advance your knowledge and career.

## Your Eligibility Guide
Discover if you can use these valuable resources.

Education Centers support your quest for a degree, certification or professional development. Requirements may vary depending on your educational goals, but typically include maintaining good academic standing, completing any necessary applications for Tuition Assistance (TA) or other financial aid, and working with an education counselor to develop your Individualized Education Plan (IEP).

**Eligibility:**

• Service Members
• Spouses
• Family Members
• Reservists
• Veterans
• Retirees
• DoD Civilians

**Program Policy and Guidance:**

• [MCO: 1560.25](https://www.marines.mil/Portals/1/Publications/MCO%201560.25.pdf)
• [DoDI 1322.25](https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/132225p.pdf)
• [TA Guidelines: 687.14](https://www.marines.mil/News/Messages/Messages-Display/Article/896895/fy15-tuition-assistance-ta-guidelines-update/)
• [NAVMAC 1560.25](https://www.marines.mil/Portals/1/Publications/NAVMC%201560.25%20(SECURED).pdf)

## Navigating Your Education Journey
Steps and guidance to help achieve your academic and career goals.

Starting your education journey can feel overwhelming, but the right guidance and resources can make all the difference.

These steps will help you navigate the Voluntary Education program and make the most of the resources available for you to successfully reach your educational goals.

**Contact the Education Center**
• Connect with an education advisor by visiting, calling or emailing your local Education Center.

**Research Educational Pathways**
• Determine your personal and professional education goals.

**Meet with an Education Counselor**
• Schedule an appointment with an education advisor.

**Explore Education Funding Options**
• Learn about funding options such as Tuition Assistance (TA), GI Bill, and Leadership Scholar Program (LSP). The education advisor can help you understand eligibility and application processes for all education programs and resources.

**Choose an Institution or Program**
• Decide on a college, university, or program based on your goals and funding availability.

**Complete the Application Process**
• Apply to the selected educational institution or program. Be sure to follow their admissions process and meet any deadlines for enrollment.

**Submit Tuition Assistance (TA) Requests**
• If eligible, submit a request for Tuition Assistance through the WebTA system. Ensure you understand the TA policies and requirements to remain in good standing.
• DoD civilians and family members are not able to submit TA applications.

**Start Your Education Journey**
• Once accepted and funding is secured, begin your coursework or program.

**Seek Support**
• Regularly check in with your education advisor to monitor your progress and adjust your education plan as needed.

## Education Services
Explore resources that help you successfully pursuit life-long learning.

Our Education Centers offer a variety of services to support you in achieving your educational goals.

• Academic, Technical, and Career Advising
• Colleges or Universities with Satelite Offices on Base
• Commissioning Programs
• Financial Aid / Scholarships
• GI BILL
• Joint Service Transcript
• Leadership Scholar Program
• Marine Corps COOL
• Military and Civilian Testing
• Online Academic Skills Course
• Researching Schools
• Spouse and Family Member Educational Resources
• Tuition Assistance
• Unit Briefs
• United Services Military Apprenticeship Program
• Workshops and Classes

Not all services are available. Please contact the Education Center on availability and eligibility.

## Education Services and Support
Successfully reach your goals with tools and resources.

## Testing Services
Using testing resources to help you earn college credits and certifications.

Voluntary Education offers testing services in the areas of military professional testing, high school equivalency (GED), college proctored testing, career entrance qualification exams, as well as professional certification and licensure testing.

Testing services are available at little to no cost and are designed to support your educational and professional development.

Contact the Education Center for more information on testing resources and support.

**Military Testing**

All tests are by appointment only. Service members must register in advance. On the day of the exam, service members must be in the uniform of the day and show their military ID at check-in. For more information or to schedule an appointment, contact the Education Center.

• Armed Forces Classification Test (AFCT)
• Aviation Selection Test Battery (ASTB)
• Defense Language Aptitude Battery (DLAB)
• Defense Language Proficiency Test (DLPT)
• Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI)
• Test of Adult Basic Education (TABE)

Not all tests are offered at all locations. Please contact the education center for availability.

**CLEP and DSST Exams**

• College Level Examination Program (CLEP) - CLEP now offers test takers the option to take a CLEP exam with remote proctoring. Visit https://clep.collegeboard.org/about-remote-proctoring/take-clep-exam-remote-proctoring for specific information.
• DANTES Subject Standardized Tests (DSST) - DSST does allow remote proctoring of exams for eligible service members. Civilian and non-eligible military test takers cannot take an exam via Remote Proctor. Visit https://www.prometric.com/exams/dantes for specific information.

**Graduate Records Exam (GRE)**

• Graduate Records Exam (GRE)
• Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT)
• Praxis I and II

**General Education Diploma (GED)**

To schedule an exam date, you must create an account by registering on [GED Testing Service](https://www.ged.com) and selecting the jurisdiction you are testing under. You can call the GED Testing Service at the following:

• 1-877-EXAM-GED (877-392-6433) (North & South Americas Region)
• +85-2-3077-4923 (Asia Pacific Region)
• (toll) +44 204-602-9757 (Europe, Middle Eastern)

Not all tests are offered at all locations. Please contact the Education Center for availability.

**GED Study Materials**

GED study materials can be found at the local library or online.

• Free practice tests and e-books are available from [EBSCO Learning Express](https://www.learningexpresshub.com/ProductEngine/LELIndex.html#/learningexpresslibrary/libraryhome) (DoD MWR Library).
• The Online Academic Skills Course (OASC) helps build and refresh basic math and verbal skills. Access to OASC is free for the military community and can be accessed by creating an account at [DANTES](https://dantes.petersons.com/).
• [MyGED® Dashboard](https://ged.com/): Learn more about the test, policies, and try sample test questions.
• [Official GED Marketplace](https://www.GEDmarketplace.com)

**SAT and ACT**

• American College Testing (ACT)
• Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT)

For both the SAT and ACT you will first need to register and create an account with [College Board](https://mysat.collegeboard.org/login). Please visit the appropriate websites for information as well as registration deadlines.

Students can request to have their official ACT results sent to the Education Center.

**Digital SAT**

The SAT can also be taken digitally through [SAT Suite College Board](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat).

## Joint Service Transcripts (JST)
Converting your military training into college credits to save time and money.

The Joint Service Transcripts (JST) program provides you with an official record of your military training and experience, converting it into civilian academic credit.

The JST includes courses, certifications, and job experience you gained during military service and is used by colleges and universities to assess and award valid credits toward degree programs.

This helps you save time and money by earning credit for what you've already learned in the military and facilitating your educational and career advancement.

Credits awarded from the Joint Services Transcript (JST) are determined solely by the individual learning institution.

For more information, visit [Joint Service Transcript](https://jst.doded.mil/jst/) or contact the Education Center.

## United Services Military Apprenticeship Program (USMAP)
Earning an apprenticeship certification while performing your military duties.

Take advantage of the United Services Military Apprenticeship Program (USMAP) and earn an apprenticeship certification while performing your mitary duties.

This Department of Defense-sponsored program allows you to earn a Department of Labor-recognized apprenticeship certification while performing your regular military duties.

USMAP combines on-the-job training with academic instruction to help service members gain valuable skills, enhance their career prospects, and earn credentials that are recognized by civilian employers.

The program is offered at no cost and covers a wide range of occupations aligned with military specialties, helping Marines transition smoothly into the civilian workforce.

Learn more about the apprenticeship certification at [USMAP](https://usmap.osd.mil/index.htm).

## Online Academic Skills Course (OASC)
Building your academic skills to achieve long-term career success.

The Online Academic Skills Course (OASC) helps you improve essential skills in math, reading, and writing. This free, self-paced program is designed to enhance academic performance, prepare for exams, and support career development, making it a valuable tool for those pursuing further education or career advancement.

The OASC can help service members prepare to take the Armed Forces Classifications Test (AFCT).

Visit [DANTES](https://dantes.petersons.com/) to learn more about OASC.

## Marine Corps COOL
Obtaining credentials, certifications, and licenses based on your military skills and experience.

Marines interested in the COOL program should visit the Education Center and speak to an advisor to explore available credentials, understand the application process, and get started on obtaining valuable certifications and licenses.

[MarineCorps COOL](https://www.cool.osd.mil/usmc/index.html)

## Career Path Decide
Discovering careers that align with your military background, education, and civilian work experience.

Career Path Decide is an assessment tool that can help you focus your efforts and resources on a specific goal, leading to greater fulfillment and success.

Learn more about the assessment and how it can help you at [Career Path Decide](https://www.careerpathdecide.org/career-planning/build-your-target).

## Spouse Works
Bringing together trusted career and education support in one place with no changes to services, eligibility or partnerships. ([Spouse Works](https://spouseworks.militaryonesource.mil/portal/))

## Leadership Scholar Program
Attending college or university after you transition from the Marine Corps.

## Financial Resources
Achieve your goals with expert financial services and support.

## Personal Financial Management
Helping you prepare financially by offering guidance and resources on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses. (Personal Financial Management)

## Federal Student Aid
Reaching your personal and professional development goals with support from financial aid. ([Federal Student Aid](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa))

## Tuition Assistance
Exploring financial aid opportunities that support your education journey.

Tuition Assistance (TA) is a higher education benefit available to you as an active duty service member if you are pursuing or want to pursue college-level coursework. You can receive up to $4,500 per fiscal year to cover up to 100% of tuition and eligible fees toward a college-level diploma, credential, certificate, or degree program.

**Eligibility Requirements – follow steps 1 through 4:**

1. **Complete the USMC TA Brief** - Complete Intro to Tuition Assistance Brief (MFRPRETA01) on [MarineNet](https://www.marinenet.usmc.mil/my.policy).
2. **Complete the Personal Financial Management (PFM) training** - Complete Personal Financial Management (PFM) training through one of the two options (PFM Training Exemptions: Marines with MOS 34XX or 8844):
   • Virtual/Online option: Complete the following PFM courses via MarineNet: Setting Financial Goals & Recordkeeping (MFRGOALS01), Exploring your Financial Values & Habits (MFRPFVH001), Developing a Spending Plan (MFRSPEND01), and Establishing Savings (MFRSAVE001); OR
   • In-person option: Attend an in person Lejeune-New River Personal Readiness Seminar (PRS).
3. **Upload Your Career Path Decide Results** - Complete the Skills and Interests Surveys at Career Path Decide and upload your completed goals report to your TA portal.
4. **Meet with an Education Advisor at the Education Center** - Attend a Career and Education Workshop for Warfighters; OR Schedule a personalized, individual counseling appointment
5. **Visit the Education Center** - Education Center advisors can assist with selecting the best academic program for your educational and career goals.
6. **Enroll in a School** - Request a degree plan, select your first class, send transcripts, and send your Joint Service Transcript obtained from JST.
7. **Identify Your TA Command Approver** - Be sure to get command approver's email and phone number to add to your TA portal later.
8. **Log-in to Your Tuition Assistance (TA) Portal** - You can log into your TA portal by visiting [Navy Education and Training Command](https://myeducation.netc.navy.mil/webta/). Complete your "Update Your Profile" tab with your contact and command approver information.
9. **Submit Your TA Request** - On your TA portal, you can submit your request for your class. You have up to 60 days in advance prior to your course start date to submit applications! You must include specific course information and term dates on the application. The information on your TA Application must be confirmed and accurate. To ensure accuracy, your course must be included on your Degree Plan and a Cost Verification Sheet must be uploaded for each TA term.
10. **Forward to your Command Approver** - When you submit your request to your command approver, they will be able to review your course information and approve or deny your request. Once your command approver has approved your request, the Education Center will review your request for eligibility and authorize a TA voucher. Be sure to allow time for the approval process as TA cannot be authorized after the start date of the class.
11. **Pay For Your Class** - After your TA request has been authorized by the education center, print and send the voucher from your TA portal to the school to make tuition payment.

**Tuition Assistance Approval**

Tuition Assistance (TA) can only be approved for courses starting within 60 days and needs to be applied for each term. To apply for TA for another term, applicants should repeat steps 8-10. Only 2 classes are funded at a time. Only 1 class is funded for first time users, applicants with a TA GPA below 2.5 (undergraduate level) or 3.0 (graduate level), or those who failed or withdrawn from their last class.

**Payment:**

You can receive up to $4,500 per fiscal year (Oct 1 - Sep 30). TA covers up to $250 per semester hour, $166.67 per quarter hour, and $16.67 per clock hour. Classes you fail (grade D, F, W, or I) will require repayment.

**Reimbursements**

Marines who fail to complete a course successfully must reimburse received TA funds.

**Waivers**

Waivers for repayment are available for students who withdraw due to duty, medical, or emergency circumstances. The Education Services Officer determines if justification for a waiver is warranted, and if so, forwards the waiver onto [Naval Education and Training Professional Development Center](https://www.netc.navy.mil/NETPDC/) (NETPDC) with additional support statements.

**Tuition Assistance Restrictions**

• TA cannot be used for flight training.
• TA is not available if you're in duty-under-instruction status or an officer accession program with full-time civilian institution instruction.
• You cannot use TA for the same course that was previously funded.
• TA will not be approved after the course start date

For more information, reach out to your Education Center.

## GI Bill
Empowering you to advance your skills, further your education, and achieve long-term success.

The GI Bills provide you with valuable educational benefits to support your personal and professional growth. Whether through the Post-9/11 GI Bill or the Montgomery GI Bill, you can access funding for tuition, housing, and other expenses, making higher education and career training more accessible.

**Post-9/11 GI Bill**

• Available to service members who served after Sept. 10, 2001, with at least 90 days of active duty. Service members will only earn 50% of benefit with only 90 days of service.
• Covers up to 100% of tuition and fees for public schools (or up to a capped amount for private schools), provides a monthly housing allowance, and includes a stipend for books and supplies.
• Allows eligible service members to transfer benefits to dependents under certain conditions.
• Benefits are generally available for 15 years after discharge.

**Montgomery GI Bill**

• Requires active duty service for at least two years and an enrollment in the program with a monthly contribution during service.
• Pays a set monthly amount to the service member, based on the number of classes taken, without a housing allowance or book stipend.
• Does not offer the option to transfer benefits.
• Benefits must be used within 10 years of discharge

For more information visit the [U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs](https://www.va.gov/education/).

## My Career Advancement Account (MyCAA)
Providing up to $4,000 of tuition assistance to eligible military spouses.

The My Career Advancement Account Scholarship pays tuition costs for education and training courses and examinations leading to an associate degree (excluding associate degrees in general studies, liberal arts and interdisciplinary studies that do not have a concentration). The scholarship also covers the costs for obtaining a license, certificate, or certification at an accredited college, university or technical school in the United States or approved testing organization that expands employment or portable career opportunities for military spouses.

**Who is Eligible?**

Spouses of service members on active duty in pay grades E-1 to E-9, W-1 to W-2 and O-1 to O-3 who have successfully completed high school and have the ability to request tuition assistance while their military sponsor is on Title 10 military orders are eligible.

Spouses married to members of the National Guard and reserves in these same pay grades are eligible.

Learn more about opportunities by visiting the [My Career Advancement Account](https://mycaa.militaryonesource.mil/mycaa/) website.

## Managing Stress
Pursuing higher learning can be challenging.

Community Counseling can help you manage stress, balance personal challenges, and improve overall well-being, enabling you to focus on your educational goals and academic success.

**Life Skills Development:**

Learn more about Community Counseling's services and support.

## Libraries
Fostering opportunities for connection and providing access to knowledge, innovation, and creativity.

We provide access to study materials, research databases, test prep resources, and quiet study spaces, helping Marines succeed in their academic pursuits.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

• Computer and Internet Access
• Live, Personalized, 24/7, World-wide Tutoring
• Quiet Study Areas
• Study Resources
• Test Prep Materials
• Virtual Library

Visit your local library or the virtual library at [DoD MWR Libraries](https://www.dodmwrlibraries.org/).

## Family Member Employment Assistance Program
Supporting military spouses and dependent family members with career readiness tools, resources, and services.

The Family Member Employment Assistance Program (FMEAP) supports your Voluntary Education by offering career counseling, job search assistance, and access to educational resources, helping you develop skills, pursue certifications, and advance your career alongside your educational goals.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

• Military Spouse Education & Career Opportunities (MySECO)
• My Career Advancement Account Scholarship Program (MyCAA)
• Military Spouse Employment Partnership (MSEP)
• Military Spouse Licensure Reimbursement (MSLR)
• Transferring Your Professional License
• Spouse's Transition Readiness Seminar (S.T.A.R.S)

Learn more about the services and support available at FMEAP.

## Marine For Life Network
Building connections for transitioning Marines and family members to help them successfully reach their career goals.

The Marine For Life Network (M4LN) connects you to valuable educational resources, networking opportunities, and mentorship.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

• Networking
• Career Planning
• Job Searching
• Communication Skills
• Leadership Development
• Problem Solving

Grow your network through M4LN.

## SkillBridge
Developing hands-on experience with an industry partner to gain practical skills and enhance your career potential.

SkillBridge is available to all eligible service members.

Visit your local SkillBridge and learn more about opportunities, services, and support.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find information and get quick answers to common questions.

**What is Voluntary Education?**
Voluntary Education provides access to educational resources, counseling, and financial support to pursue higher education, certifications, and professional development.

**What types of degrees or certifications can I pursue?**
The program supports a variety of educational goals, including associates, bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees, as well as certifications and vocational training in various fields.

**Can I use my GI Bill benefits with the Voluntary Education Program?**
Yes, Marines can use their GI Bill benefits in combination with the Voluntary Education Program to help cover the cost of tuition, books, and other educational expenses.

**How do I transfer my GI Bill benefits to my dependents?**
To transfer Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits to dependents, you must meet specific eligibility requirements and apply through the Department of Defense's online platform, typically after completing at least six years of service.

**How does the Joint Service Transcripts (JST) work?**
The JST captures military training and occupation experience, which may be eligible for civilian academic credits.

**Is there a limit to how much Tuition Assistance I can receive?**
Yes, TA typically covers up to $250 per semester, with an annual cap of $4,500 per fiscal year for eligible Marines.

**Where can I go to take the SAT/ACT?**
The Education Centers are not authorized to offer either exam. For the SAT or ACT, register and create an account with the College Board or [ACT.org](https://www.act.org/).

**Is military testing offered through the Education Center?**
Yes.

pages.title: MCCS Volunteer Opportunities
pages.text:
# MCCS Volunteer Opportunities

We connect you with meaningful volunteering opportunities that strengthen the military community and enhance the well-being of Marines and their families.

## Start Volunteering Today
Make a difference by giving your time, sharing your skills, and supporting the community.

## Eligibility
**Requirements:**

• Must be 13 years of age or older.
• Minors must have parental permission to volunteer.
• Must be willingly to offer, be accepted, and provide voluntary services.
• Must be in an off-duty status, if active duty or a civilian employee.
• Cannot count any fundraising activity as volunteerism.

## Getting Started
Getting started with volunteering is easy!

• Browse the volunteer webpage and calendar for available volunteer roles that match your interests and skills.
• Contact the Volunteer Coordinator for more information about specific opportunities and application processes.
• Fill out the volunteer application form, providing necessary details such as your availability, interests, and any prior experience.
• Attend the required orientation or training to familiarize yourself with the program, expectations, and guidelines.
• For certain roles, especially those working with children or sensitive information, a background check may be required.
• After your application is approved, you'll be matched with a volunteer position that suits your skills and interests.
• Start your volunteer journey, making a positive impact on your community while gaining valuable experience.

Volunteer Application (NAVMC 5380.2)

Volunteer Hours (NAVMC 5380.1)

## Why Volunteer?
Volunteering offers many benefits, from personal growth and skill development to making meaningful connections and giving back to the community.

**Volunteering Benefits:**

• Community support
• Develop lasting relationships
• Enhances resumes
• Grow networks
• Personal growth and development
• Professional development
• Receive on-the-job training
• Teen volunteer opportunities
• Work flexible hours

**Life Skills Developed:**

• Communication
• Empathy and Compassion
• Strengthening Relationships
• Leadership
• Personal and professional development
• Problem-solving
• Networking
• Teamwork
• Time management

**Honorable Recognition:**

• Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal (MOVSM)
• President's Volunteer Service Award (PVSA)
• Volunteer Service Award (VSA)

## Request for Volunteers
Supporting organizations seeking volunteers for programs, events, or activities.

## Volunteer Request Policies
Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) supports our military community partners with volunteers from both on-installation Government Affiliated Agencies and off-installation Non-Federal Entities (NFE).

MCCS will advertise volunteer opportunities that can reasonably be expected to bring credit to the individuals involved and to the Navy and Marine Corps team as well as being consistent with Department of the Navy and Marine Corps policies.

## Requirements
Before MCCS will advertise any volunteer opportunity, volunteer participation in the event must be considered suitable in accordance with the following criteria:

1. On-installation federal entity request must meet the established requirements in accordance with all applicable orders, regulations, and directives.
2. It is appropriate to associate MCCS and the command with the NFE's event, and volunteer support of the event will not bring discredit to the Marine Corps, II MEF, or MCCS.
3. The NFE's event is of interest and benefit to the local civilian and military community, and volunteer support of the NFE's event will not appear to endorse or favor any private individual, special interest group or business, religion, ideology, commercial venture, political candidate or organization.
4. The NFE's event is not intended to provoke controversy or public confrontation.
5. Partisan political organizations, ideological movements, and NFEs whose constitution, by-laws, membership qualifications or ritual are not made public, are ineligible to be advertised.
6. The NFE must not require service member volunteers to wear their uniforms while volunteering off the installation in their personal, unofficial capacities.
7. MCCS will not advertise volunteer opportunities where the NFE seeks to use service members as ushers, guards, parking lot attendants, runners, messengers, baggage handlers, crowd control or any other similar, menial capacity that would be deemed inappropriate pursuant to community outreach standards.

## Volunteer Request Form
If the volunteer opportunity meets the above criteria, the organizations point of contact is requested to complete the following steps:

1. Email MCBCL_MCASNR@usmc.mil and request the Volunteer Opportunity Request Form.
2. Review form and completely fill in all required areas.
3. Submit completed form to MCBCL_MCASNR@usmc.mil

Once a completed form is received by MCCS personnel, you will be notified that your request has been received and is being considered according to established checklist. All requests will have an approved or denied determination within 5-7 working days.

All approved requests will be uploaded to the MCCS Volunteer Opportunities Portal and will remain active until the event has expired.

## Volunteer Opportunities
Discover resources in your community.

## L.I.N.K.S
Lifestyle Insights, Networking, Knowledge, and Skills

The L.I.N.K.S.

**Curriculum Includes:**

Are you wanting to make a difference in the lives of military families?

Learn more about L.I.N.K.S. by visiting Marine Corps Family Team Building.

## Single Marine Program
Volunteering with the Single Marine Program (SMP) supports the community, events, and helps enhance the quality of life for Marines and their families.

The Single Marine Program offers a wide variety of volunteer opportunities each month with flexible times, days, and locations to meet the needs of our diverse community.

Volunteer opportunities are available for single and geo-bachelor Marines.

Learn more about the volunteering opportunities through the Single Marine Program.

## Coach Youth Sports
Volunteering for youth sports is a fantastic way to inspire young athletes while fostering teamwork, discipline, and a love for physical activity.

• Tee-Ball
• Baseball
• Basketball
• Flag Football
• Soccer
• Track

Not all sports listed are available at all locations.

Explore volunteer opportunities with Youth Sports.

## Base Schools
Marines and their families have valuable opportunities to volunteer at schools located on Marine Corps bases, contributing positively to the educational environment and fostering community engagement.

Here's how you can get involved:

• Explore Volunteer Opportunities: There are a variety of volunteer opportunities that connect military personnel, their families, retirees, veterans, and civilians with local schools.

**Benefits of Volunteering**

• Personal Growth: Develop new skills and gain experiences that can enhance personal and professional growth.
• Community Connection: Strengthen ties within the military community by supporting local schools and educational programs.
• Recognition: Eligible volunteers may receive awards such as the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Award or the President's Volunteer Service Award.

**Volunteer Roles**

• Classroom Assistance: Supporting teachers with instructional activities and classroom management.
• Tutoring: Providing one-on-one or small group academic support to students.
• Extracurricular Activities: Assisting with clubs, sports, and other after-school programs.

**Initiate the Application Process**

• Contact the Volunteer Coordinator: Reach out to the Installation Volunteer Coordinator at your base to express interest and learn about available opportunities.
• Complete Necessary Forms: Fill out the required volunteer application forms, which may include background checks and other necessary documentation.

**Commit to a Schedule**

• Determine a volunteer schedule that aligns with your availability and the needs of the school. Consistency is often appreciated, but many programs offer flexibility to accommodate varying schedules.

**Maintain Communication**

• Stay in regular contact with the school's volunteer coordinator to ensure a positive and effective volunteer experience.

Not all installations offer volunteer opportunities with base schools.

## Navy Marine Corps Relief Society
The Navy Marine Corps Relief Society (NMCRS) is accepting professional volunteers to assist service members and eligible family members.

**Volunteer requirements:**

• Must have base access
• Be available between Monday through Friday from 8 a.m.-4 p.m.

**Volunteer opportunities include:**

• Client services - reception duties
• Casework - providing one-on-one financial education and assistance
• Budget for Baby - teaching workshops to military families expecting a child
• Well Baby Clinic - working with our visiting nurses to administer health checks and clothing exchange

All volunteers will be properly trained to support and assist with confidence.

Learn more about volunteer opportunities at the [Navy Marine Corps Relief Society](https://www.nmcrs.org/).

## Honoring Our Volunteers
We honor the outstanding commitment to volunteer service.

## Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal
The Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal is for members of the armed forces and reserve components. Service members will want to volunteer in their civilian and military communities for normally a period of three years, which do not need to be consecutive years.

Learn more about the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal by contacting the Volunteer Coordinator.

## Behind the Camouflage Spouse and Community Awards
The Marine Corps Association is excited to announce the launch of the **Behind the Camouflage Awards Program** to highlight the exceptional work Marine Corps spouses and community members are doing within their communities.

There are three opportunities to nominate spouses and community members who contributed to building the community and driving positive change.

**Spouse Spotlight**

Celebrating Marine Corps Spouses who excel in building community and driving positive change.

Nominate a spouse today at [Spouse Spotlight](https://www.mca-marines.org/btc-spouse-spotlight/)!

**Changemaker**

The Changemaker of the Year Award honors individuals who have made a significant, tangible impact within the Marine Corps community. This award recognizes those who have driven meaningful change by identifying challenges and implementing solutions that positively affect the lives of Marine Corps families, spouses, and the broader community.

Learn about eligibility and requirements, and nomination process at [Changemaker](https://www.mca-marines.org/community-change-maker/).

**Community Catalyst**

The Community Catalyst of the Year Award recognizes a member of the Marine Corps community who has shown exceptional dedication to building and nurturing a supportive environment.

Learn about eligibility, requirements, and nomination process at [Community Catalyst](https://www.mca-marines.org/community-catalyst/).

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**How do I sign up to volunteer?**
You can sign up by visiting the Volunteer office, contacting a volunteer coordinator, or checking the MCCS website for available opportunities and application instructions.

**What types of volunteer opportunities are available?**
MCCS offers a wide range of opportunities, including roles in youth sports, the Single Marine Program, special events, and community support.

**Do I need prior experience or training to volunteer?**
While some positions may require specific skills or training, many volunteer opportunities offer on-the-job training and welcome individuals of all experience levels.

**How do I track my volunteer hours?**
Volunteer hours are typically tracked through sign-in sheets, volunteer logs, with verification by a coordinator or supervisor.

**Can I earn awards or recognition for my volunteer service?**
Yes, volunteers may be eligible for awards such as the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal, the President's Volunteer Service Award, and other local or organizational recognition.

# Extended Veteran's Access

Effective 1 January 2020, newly eligible veterans and caregivers under the Purple Heart and Disabled Veterans Equal Access Act of 2018 have access to many Department of Defense and Coast Guard MWR retail activities.

These activities are generally self-sustaining and do not rely on appropriated funds to operate. # Sponsorship & Advertising

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is a comprehensive set of programs that supports and enhances the operational readiness, war fighting capabilities, and life quality of Marines, their families, retirees and civilians.

_by partnering with Marine Corps Community Services._

MCCS Advertising and Sponsorship can help integrate your brand’s products or services within the Marine market through an array of platforms, promotions and events.

Show your commitment to the military community by sponsoring beloved programs.

From large-scale advertisements to social media campaigns, we ensure your message reaches the right audience.

# AMP-IT

Aquatics Maximum Power Intense Training (AMP-IT) is an in-water physical training program that consists of a variety of scientifically-proven, high-intensity exercises provided in an aquatic workout suitable for rehabilitating and reconditioning injured military personnel.

## AMP-IT Unit PT
Units may request an instructor to lead an AMP-IT Unit PT session at either the MCB Camp Lejeune Area 2 Pool or the MCAS New River Indoor Pool. Call for availability.

## AMP-IT Group Exercise
Classes are offered at the Area 2 Indoor Pool.

*Group Exercise fees apply.*

## AMP-IT Instructor's Course
Become an instructor and conduct AMP-IT sessions for your unit. Open to NCOs and above with command authorization. This course falls in line with MCO 6100.13 and will facilitate training for the Unit CCI.

## AMP-IT Instructor's 2-Day Course
**Instructor Course Sessions:**

- Jan. 14: 8AM - 5PM & Jan. 15: 11AM - 3PM
- May 17: 8AM - 5PM & May 18: 11AM - 3PM

This is our instructor's course to teach Aquatics Maximum Power Intense Training (AMP-IT). To attend the two-day training you must be a NCO or above and get clearance through your command. This course aligns with MCO 6100.13 and facilitates training for the Unit CCI.

**Subject matter covered:**

- Strength training using drag equipment
- Passive and assistive stretching
- Deep water interval cadence training
- Balance and core activities
- Safety skills with working with injuries
- General benefits to water workouts

pages.title: Health & Wellness Education
pages.text:
# Health & Wellness Education

This program provides awareness and education to all members of the military community that encourages people to increase control over and to improve their full health potential.

Health & Wellness Education supports the achievement and sustainment of a fit and mission ready force and healthy populations, at home and abroad, in peacetime and in conflict. Each of these programs aligns with the US Department of Health and Human Services’ Healthy People 2020 and the DOD’s Operation Live Well and the Healthy Base Initiatives.

MCCS encourages and supports the participation of individuals of all abilities in its programs and facilities.

## Unit Brief Requests
Our Health Education Technician delivers tailored unit briefs and guidance on topics such as performance nutrition and body composition principles, dietary supplements, sleep hygiene, injury prevention, and sexual health and responsibility – and more.

A full list of unit brief requests, which can be modified for operational specificity, can be viewed here.

## General Nutrition
This presentation provides foundational knowledge on healthy eating, covering macronutrients, portion sizes, food labels, and how to make informed choices at the grocery store, mess hall, and restaurants.

## Performance Nutrition Education
Designed with Human Performance Optimization in mind, this presentation explores how to fuel the body for training, recovery, and optimal performance.

## Dietary Supplements Education
This presentation provides an in-depth look at dietary supplements, including their benefits, risks, and proper use for performance.

## Sleep Hygiene
This brief explores the importance of sleep for overall health, performance, and well-being. Participants will learn practical tips for managing stress, creating a bedtime routine, and optimizing rest—especially in challenging schedules like shift work.

## Injury Prevention
This injury prevention brief focuses on reducing musculoskeletal injuries that impact combat readiness.

## Sexual Health
This brief covers the foundations of sexual health, including its place in overall well-being, connection to mission-readiness, consent, common STIs and testing procedures, preventive care practices, and birth control options.

## Individual Wellness Services
One-on-one consultations are available to active-duty personnel for general nutrition counseling, body composition testing, and resource referral. Please email to request an appointment. Appointments are subject to availability.

## Recurring Briefs
Monthly, recurring nutrition and sleep briefs are made available to all units and patrons with no reservation needed.

Be advised that more locations and dates are becoming available.

**Monthly Nutrition Brief**

- 2nd Wednesday of each month, 9:30AM, Warrior Athlete Readiness & Resilience (WARR) Center
- 2nd Thursday of each month, 9:30AM, Bldg. AS4024, HITT Center, MCAS New River

**Monthly Sleep Brief**

- 4th Wednesday of the month, 10AM, WARR Center Classroom

## Other Services
Beyond unit briefs and wellness services, Health Promotions supports installation events through tabling, demonstrations, and tailored partnerships. Please email us to request support, information, or to discuss collaboration opportunities.

pages.text:
# Marine Corps Half Marathon

Experience the storied legacy of the Marine Corps at the Marine Corps Half Marathon on Camp Lejeune.

**SOLD OUT**

**September 19, 2026 | 7AM | MCB Camp Lejeune**

Presented by FirstLight Home Care and USAA

## Course Details
You will travel between the fairways of the Paradise Point Golf Course, where the Heroes Mile pays homage to fallen service members.

_This course is not USATF certified._

**This race is open to the public.**

## Base Access Requirements
The pass-request deadline has now passed, but base access requirements remain in effect for all participants and spectators.

Due to increased security measures, the Trusted Traveler Program has been suspended. All runners and spectators ages 18+ who do not have a valid DoW ID with credentialed base access MUST have a base pass.

## Spectator Information
**Cheer on runners!** Not running but want to support this year's participants? For questions or additional information, please email mccslejeunesemperfitraces@usmc-mccs.org.

_Base access is required._

## Registration Requirements
- Must be 14yrs+ to register
- All runners must complete the race within 3.75 hours
- This course is not a USATF certified course
- Only registered runners are allowed on the course
- No pets allowed on the course

## Awards
**ALL FINISHERS WILL RECEIVE A FINISHER MEDAL**

- Overall Awards will be given to the top 3 overall male and female finishers
- Overall Masters Awards will be given to the top 3 overall male and female finishers ages 40 and up
- 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place medals will be given to the top 3 male and female finishers in each age bracket: (14-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65+)

Note: Overall winners will receive an Overall plaque award and Overall placement medal. Overall award winners are not eligible to also place in their age category.

## Hydration and Fuel Available on Course
**Hydration:** Powerade and water

**Gels:** UnTapped Energy Gels in Salted Cocoa and Salted Citrus varieties will be available on the course.

## Installation Access Instructions
ALL RUNNERS AND ALL PASSENGERS (18YRS AND OVER) NEEDING A BASE PASS must complete the instructions below AFTER race registration has been completed.

Due to increased security measures, the Trusted Traveler Program has been suspended. All runners and spectators who do not currently possess a valid DoW ID with credentialed base access will need to obtain an event base access pass.

1. Register for a base pass at https://www1.mcieast.usmc.mil/IARA/
2. Locate the event and select "Request Sponsor"
3. Agree to the Privacy Act Statement
4. Select the Visitor Type drop down menu and choose either driver or passenger
5. Complete the registration. Please have the following information available:
   - **Drivers:** Social Security number, DOB, email, phone number, driver's license, auto insurance policy, and auto information
   - **Passengers:** Social Security number, DOB, government ID, email, and phone number

**Deadline to submit information is 30 days prior to the event date.** No additional event passes will be issued past this date. Registration fees are non-refundable and non-transferable if you do not request a pass by the deadline.

Once approved, your pass(es) will be available for pick up at the Visitor's Gate the morning of the race. The pass is only good for the day of the event. Registered runners will receive more information on how to receive their pass(es) the week prior to the race.

**REAL ID Requirements:** All visitors with non-REAL ID driver's license and State issued identification cards requesting access to MCIEAST-MCB Camp Lejeune or MCAS New River must provide an approved identity source document or combination thereof to access the installation(s).

An example of identity source documentation includes a U.S. passport, or the combination of an original or certified true copy of a birth certificate bearing a raised seal, social security card, and non-REAL ID compliant driver's license or State issued identification card – all three documents must bear the same name.

For questions on the REAL ID, contact Base Security at 910-450-0282.

Contact: Race Staff

# Paradise Point Golf Course

Paradise Point Golf Course was designed by George Cobb, a world renowned golf architect and former Marine.

## Course Information
Paradise Point Golf Course has two golf courses, the Scarlet and the Gold. The Scarlet is an 18 hole course with par of 70. The Gold is an 18 hole course with par of 72. Also available are two driving ranges, one green grass and the other covered with 20 bays.

# Marinas

Gottschalk Marina is a recreational marina designed for authorized patrons seeking outdoor experiences on the water.

You can enjoy fishing, cruising, or spending quality time outdoors with family and friends.

Gottschalk Marina is a certified NC Clean Marina, meeting the standards of the NC Clean Marina Program.

## Safety Conditions
For the safety of our patrons, all motorized and non-motorized watercraft cannot be issued under the following conditions:

- The marina is under Thunderstorm Condition 1, lightning, or high wind advisory.
- Water is deemed too rough to safely launch or handle watercraft.

## Rental Requirements
- All patrons must have a valid DoD ID card.
- Non-Motorized Watercrafts 16 years of age or older
- Motorized Watercraft - 18 years or older with completion of a boating safety course*

# Onslow Beach

Enjoy your stay at Onslow Beach with family-friendly accommodations and RV camping options. During your visit, take advantage of numerous activities suitable for all ages.

## Base Access
The Trusted Traveler Program is **suspended until further notice**. The Trusted Traveler Program previously allowed DoD-affiliated sponsors to vouch for vehicle occupants for installation access.

**At this time, all unvetted visitors must report to the installation Visitor Center to request access.**

[Click here for more details.](https://www.lejeune.marines.mil/Offices-Staff/Provost-Marshals-Office/)

## Lodging Rates

**Pet Fees (Allowed in Lodges & Ospreys only)**

Pet fees include a $25 non-refundable fee, plus daily pet fees.

| Number of Pets | 3-Nights | 4-Nights | 7-Nights |
|---|---|---|---|
| One Pet | $49 | $57 | $81 |

## Check-in/Out
- **Check-in:** 4PM
- **Check-out:** 10AM
- **Check-in days:**
  - **Lodges**: 3 Days - Mon or Tue | 4 Days - Thu or Fri | 7 Days - Mon, Tue, Thu or Fri
  - **Ospreys**: 3 Days - Tue | 4 Days - Fri | 7 Days - Tue or Fri
  - **Rank Homes**: 3 Days - Thu | 4 Days - Thu | 7 Days - Mon or Thu

_If arriving after business hours, please see host camper._

## Lodging Reservation Policy
Onslow Beach reservations can only be made by authorized patrons with a valid military or DoD ID card. A maximum stay of 7 consecutive days is permitted in any lodging unit. For additional reservations during this time, a consecutive two week time frame is required between reservations.

## Reservations
Make your reservations for any of our facilities by calling 910.440.7502 or by stopping by our on-site Guest Services Office, BA-275 Beach Road Camp Lejeune, North Carolina 28547. Onslow Beach reservations can only be made by authorized patrons with a valid military or DoD ID card. We do not accept reservations electronically.

## Payment
Payment is due in full upon making reservation. All major credit cards accepted.

## Cancellation Policy
Reservations cancelled less than 7 days prior to check in date will be charged a processing fee equivalent to one night's stay. A full refund will be granted for cancellations made 7 or more days prior to check in.

## Booking Window
| Category | Weeks in Advance |
|---|---|
| Active Duty, Reservist and Eligible Dependents | 20 |
| Retired Military and Veterans eligible under the Veterans Equal Access Act of 2018 | 18 |
| Inactive reservists and DoD employees | 16 |

For more information on Extended Veterans Access, visit [Military OneSource](https://download.militaryonesource.mil/12038/MOS/Factsheets/expanding-access-fact-sheet.pdf).

## Lodges
Conveniently located on the second row of the island and just a short walk to the ocean! All lodges include a living room, full kitchen, master bedroom with a queen size bed, 1 bath and a loft area. Please bring your own air mattress or sleeping bags if you will be using the loft area (extra linen is provided). Lodges can accommodate 2 - 4 if using loft area. Smoking is prohibited in MCCS facilities.

**Amenities**

- Air-Conditioning
- Basketball Courts
- Cable
- Kitchenware
- Complimentary Wi-Fi*
- Linens
- Pet Beach
- Volleyball Courts
- Smart TVs
- Picnic Table
- Onslow Beach Marine Mart
- Lifeguards (Memorial Day - Labor Day)

**\*Due to Onslow Beach being located on an island, cable and WIFI service may be interrupted intermittently throughout your stay.**

We ask that patrons adhere to all posted signs and caution areas. In accordance with [MCIEAST-MCB CAMLEJO 1710.2B](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=cf06dc5c-f72b-4ea6-ba2f-f06e175870c3), failure to follow posted warnings and signs can result in forcible removal from Onslow Beach by the Camp Lejeune Police.

**Check In/Out**

- **Check-in:** 4PM
- **Checkout:** 10AM
- **Check in days during Peak Season:**
  - All Lodges: Monday and Tuesday (staying 3 or 7 days)
  - Thursday and Friday (staying 4 or 7 days)

If arriving after business hours, please see host camper.

**Lodging Reservation Policy**

Onslow Beach reservations can only be made by authorized patrons with a valid military or DoD ID card. Authorized users are entitled to reserve a maximum of 2 Lodge units per stay. A maximum stay of 7 consecutive days is permitted in any lodging unit. For additional reservations during this time, a consecutive two week time frame is required between reservations.

**Reservations**

Make your reservations for any of our facilities by calling 910.440.7502 or by stopping by our on-site Guest Services Office. Onslow Beach reservations can only be made by authorized patrons with a valid military or DoD ID card.

## Ospreys
Beautifully situated on the second row of the island and just a short walk to the ocean! All Ospreys include a living room, full kitchen, three bedrooms (Queen, Queen, 2 Twin Beds) and 2 full baths. Smoking is prohibited in MCCS facilities.

ADA units are available.

**Amenities**

- **Check-in:** 4PM
- **Checkout:** 10AM
- **Check-in days during Peak Season:**
  - All Ospreys: Tuesday (staying 3 or 7 days) and Friday (staying 4 or 7 days)

If arriving after business hours, please see host camper.

## Rank Homes
**E-9 Homes** - 3 Bedrooms, 2 Bathrooms (Sleeps 6 - Queen, Queen, 2 Twin Beds).

**Gold View Suite at Sand Dollar Shores** - 2 Bedrooms, 2 Bathrooms (Sleeps 4 - Queen, 2 Twin beds) Includes an open floor living and dining area with a breakfast bar. **May only be reserved by E9s, O5s, O6s and Gold Star Families. Gold Star families can book reservations 20 weeks in advance.**

_Disclosure: Gold Star Families eligible to stay include those with service member registered on the [goldstarfamilyregistry.com.](http://goldstarfamilyregistry.com/)_

**LtCol House** - 3 Bedrooms, 1 Bathroom (Sleeps 6 - Queen, Queen, 2 Twin Beds).

**Col House** - 3 Bedrooms, 1 Bathroom (Sleeps 6 - Queen, Queen, 2 Twin Beds).

- **Check-in:** 4PM
- **Checkout:** 10AM
- **Check in days:** Monday (staying 3 or 7 days) and Thursday (staying 4 or 7 days)

_If arriving after business hours, please see host camper._

## RV Park
Our RV Campground on the Intracoastal Waterway has 33 full hook-up sites.

- **Check-in:** 12PM
- **Checkout:** 11AM
- Check-in available to reserve 7 days a week

**Pets**

Pets staying in personal RV units, and Service Animals with proper ID cards are exempt from fees. Pets are only allowed at designated areas and must be on a leash (no longer than 10 ft.) at all times. You must clean up after your pet(s).

_The Environmental Conservation Branch implements an integrated program for the protection of nesting turtles and shorebirds on Onslow Beach.

**Amenities**

- 30 amp/ 50 amp / 110 amp electrical outlets
- Water & Sewage available at RV spaces (not available at tent sites)
- Spectrum Cable
- Picnic table with gazebo at each space
- Bathhouse
- Coin-Operated Laundry Room
- Picnic Pavilion with charcoal grill
- Business Center inside Guest Services Office
- Dog Park
- Army Corp. fishing dock within walking distance
- Host Campers on site for any of your after-hour needs

**RV Space Regulations**

Each space is only entitled to house one RV and two vehicles per space.

Each patron should be considerate of the overall appearance of the RV Park. Personal property must be capable of being stored within each patron's RV at any time. Personal items located on the outside of the guests' RV must be stored neatly under RV and should not be an excessive amount.

Non-RV household furniture, gymnasium exercise equipment, and animal cages are not permitted to be stored outside at any given time. Guests are not permitted to install permanent fences, outdoor appliances, tarps, or shading cloth.

Clotheslines are permitted to hang in the space of the gazebo, but please make sure to bring down towels once they are dry. Fire Pits, tiki torches, and contained fires are prohibited.

Propane tanks must be secured at all times to the RV or appropriate equipment. All propane tanks must be tightly secured to prevent leakage.

**Campground Reservation Policy**

Onslow Beach reservations can only be made by authorized patrons with a valid military or DoD ID card.

During our peak season (April 1 - October 31), RV & Tent patrons may stay up to a maximum of 30 days, based on availability. During our non-peak season (November 1 - March 31), RV & Tent patrons may stay an unlimited number of nights, based on availability.

## Pet Rules & Guidance
Pet beach area starts at the Turtle Pavilion and extends east to the Training Beach South training area as well as Starfish Point Pavilion and extends west to the Training Beach North.

Pets are only allowed at designated areas and must be on a leash (no longer than 10 ft.) at all times. You must clean up after your pet(s).

**Pets staying in units at Onslow Beach**

Pets are permitted inside designated Pet Friendly Lodging units for an additional fee. Please note pet owners found to have pets in non-authorized units must remove the pet immediately and will be charged a $250 per day fee for each day they were in violation.

All pets must be confined inside a pet carrier when left unattended. If at any time it is determined that a pet is not caged and left unattended in the unit, the guest will be asked to leave and will forfeit any fees paid for the unit.

## Additional Facilities
The following facilities are available for anniversaries, birthday parties, weddings, retirement ceremonies, and any other special events:

**Gazebo**

Gazebo with grill, picnic tables and parking.

Available daily: 8AM - 10PM
Daily Rate of $60

**Pavilions**

Three pavilions are located along Onslow Beach (Starfish Point, Sand Dollar Shores, and Turtle Trail).

Units wishing to reserve Gazebos/Pavilions must do so through their MCCS coordinator.

**Starfish Point Multi-purpose Room:**

Available Mon - Fri: 8AM - 10PM
Available Sat & Sun: 9AM - 10PM
Daily Rate of $60 (Max capacity of 30 people)

Located oceanfront, equipped with 6 tables and 30 chairs, refrigerator, sink, and microwave. For rental regulations and reservations, call 910-440-7502.

## Activities at Onslow Beach
**Swimming**

Guarded swimming areas are provided Memorial Day thru Labor Day from 9AM - 6PM daily. Please swim in guarded areas only. Swimming is not permitted from dusk until dawn.

**Fishing**

Any individuals 16 years or older must purchase a NC Coastal Recreational Fishing License (CRFL) prior to recreationally fishing in any water designated as coastal or joint waters of North Carolina. Base permits are required to hunt, fish, trap, or launch a boat on the installation. For information on how to obtain a permit, visit [https://lejeune.recaccess.com](https://lejeune.recaccess.com/) or the Conservation Law Enforcement Office (CLEO), Bldg. SAW-400, Old Sawmill Rd. Hunting is not permitted in the Onslow Beach recreational area.

**Onslow Beach Fishing Access Road Closed**

As part of the Task Force Florence hurricane reconstruction projects, the dirt road north of the Onslow Beach Bridge on the Eastside of the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway will be closed for repairs.

## OB Rocks!
Ways to play our Hide & Seek Rock Game! Open for everyone to join in on the fun.

## Onslow Beach Water Conditions

pages.title: Outdoor Adventures
pages.text:
# Outdoor Adventures

Outdoor Adventures hosts a variety of recreational activities including Unit Recreation, Youth Summer Camps, Kayak Tours, Archery events and more! We also offer outdoor facility rentals such as Hospital Point Picnic Area and Orde Pond Picnic Area as well as 7 primitive campsites at our Brewster Recreation Area.

## Customer Entrance & Parking
Due to construction, West Road is closed.
- Use the customer entrance on Ash Street
- For Event Parking: Park in the SNCO Thrift Store parking lot to access Building 1108

## Unit Recreation
**Did you know we have Unit Recreation/PT Alternative?**

**Monday-Friday**

**7:30AM | 9:30AM | 11:30AM**

(Additional times may be requested)

Each activity is designed to assist with building resiliency, unit cohesion, morale, teamwork, physical fitness, and communication.

1. ONLY open to Active Duty unit groups
2. For best service (though not a requirement), reservations should be made at least one weeks in advance
3. Requests are confirmed via email and are finalized upon receipt of upfront and minimum fee
4. Minimum group size is 10 participants
5. The upfront down payment is $50 for Unit Packages (covers the first 10 participants)
6. $5 fee for each additional participant
7. No discounts for groups smaller than 10
8. Participant maximums vary by activity
9. A blanket Hold Harmless Waiver and a Gear Use Agreement will be on site for your group to sign before the event
10. Music devices are discouraged

**Call 910-451-1368 to register.**

## Unit Mountain Biking
If you are a leader and are looking for a perfect team building activity or alternative to running, this is it.

This is the most Challenging and REWARDING UNIT PT offering on all of Camp Lejeune.

**Cost**
- Down Payment: $50.00 (covers first 10 people)
- Additional Participants: $5 per person

**Details**
- Location: Big Branch Trail, 261 NW Corridor Blvd, Jacksonville, NC 28540
- Length: 5.4 miles
- Difficulty: Moderately Strenuous
- Max of 30 Participants
- ODA brings the bikes to the trail
- Drinking water is not available
- No water bottle cages on bikes, bring a hydration pack or backpack for a bottle

## Unit Kayaking
Enjoy the serenity of Wallace Creek and paddle with the jumping mullet and to the lucky group, dolphins!

**Details**
- Location: Gottschalk Marina, Camp Lejeune
- Duration: up to 1.5 hours
- Difficulty: Easy
- Max of 50 Participants
- Bring a hydration pack or water bottle, sunscreen, bug spray, a hat, sunglasses
- A change of clothes is recommended
- Custom paddling experiences may be available at your request

## Unit Archery Tag
If you've enjoy archery, dodgeball, or are just plain competitive, Archery Tag® is for you! Played with teams of 5 - 15 players, Archery Tag® may be played in a tournament or round robin format, with up to 4 teams playing on 2 courses at once.

**Details**
- Location: This is a mobile event, there are several options for playing field and we can come to you!
- Duration: Up to 1.5 hours
- Difficulty: Easy/Competitive Sport
- Max 100 participants
- Bring your own water, sunscreen, and bug spray
- Rules and safety will be covered in a brief prior to the start

## Unit GelBlaster Battle
Gel ball is a game similar to paintball or laser tag. Total of 30 Gel Blaster Surge Markers (guns), and each Marker comes with 800 Gellets® (ammo).

**Details**
- Location: This is a mobile event, there are several options for playing field and we can come to you!
- Duration: Up to 1.5 hours
- Difficulty: Easy/Competitive Sport
- Bring your own water, sunscreen, and bug spray
- Rules and safety will be covered in a brief prior to the start

## Bounce & Play Party Package
Enjoy hours of fun where you can bounce, play, and celebrate with an all-in-one party package!

- 2 hours of bounce time
- 5 inflatables
- Max of 50 people total per party
- $300

Package includes indoor staging in our spacious facility on Camp Lejeune, so you can focus on the fun without worrying about the weather, set-up or clean-up! Plus, tables and chairs are provided for your guests. Bring your own food and supplies.

Contact us at 910-451-1368 to book your party today!

## Brewster Campground
**Features**
- 6 primitive tent camping spaces
- 1 group campsite
- Canoe & kayak launch
- Potable water & port-a-john toilets
- Most of the campsites are equipped with a picnic shelter, picnic table, and fire ring.

**Reservations & Pricing**
- Reservations must be made at least 48 hours prior to date requested.
- Reservations aren't confirmed until payment is received.
- Single site (12 people): $15
- Group site (40 people): $30

**Check-in & Checkout**
- Check-in: after 12PM
- Check-out: before 11AM (On your own)

Please contact the Outdoor Recreation Office with your check-in time.

**Rules & Regulations**
1. All individuals are to adhere to the Leave No Trace principles.
2. Pets must remain under the guest's control and in sight at all times.
3. Owners are responsible for their pet's behavior.
4. Please clean up after your pet at all times
5. Children under the age of 10 must be supervised at all times.
6. Quiet hours are between 10PM - 6AM. No excessive noise will be permitted at any time.

**Emergency Information**
- Base Emergency: 911
- Base Emergency Communication Center: 910.451.3004

**Fires**

Ground fires are allowed in the fire ring. Fires are ONLY permitted in assigned areas.

To have a fire at your campsite, you must have the following items on your site:
- Bucket of water (5 gallons)
- Rack or shovel

Fires ARE NOT permitted under the following conditions:
- If the National Weather Service issues a red flag for burning
- When the base is in a Class V Fire Condition

To verify fire conditions, visit https://www.ncagr.gov/divisions/nc-forest-service/fire-control-and-prevention/sit-report

## Picnic Areas
**Picnic Area Reservations:**
- Great for Birthday Parties, Cookouts, Farewells, Retirements, Baby Showers, or Reunions
- $50 per day
- Covered Shelters
- Maximum Capacity 300
- Reservations can be made by calling or emailing.

**2 Locations**
- Hospital Point Picnic Area
- Orde Pond Picnic Area

Picnic area open for daytime use only.

## Fishing
Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune offers a variety of fishing opportunities for the hobbyist angler.

- Gottschalk Marina: 910.451.8307
- Base Game Warden: 910.451.2196

**Rules of Conduct**
1. Always pick-up litter and deposit it in an approved trash receptacle.
2. Never spade or dig bait along shoreline that can lead to soil erosion.
3. Only use rowboats, canoes, or boats powered by electric trolling motors within the Base Ponds, to decrease the effect of pollution.

It is everyone's responsibility to ensure that our natural resources remain in good order for the next recreational fisherman to enjoy.

## Fishing Ponds
Camp Lejeune currently maintains eight ponds, 46.5 acres total, which are managed by the Fish and Wildlife Section of the Environmental Management Division.

\* BL= Bluegill, BA=Bass, C=Channel Catfish

## Fishing Permits & Licenses
**Licenses** (Required for individuals 16 years or older)

Any individuals 16 years or older who want to recreationally fish in any water designated as coastal or joint waters of North Carolina must purchase a NC Coastal Recreational Fishing License (CRFL).

**Base Fishing Permits**

Current Base Order requires anyone over the age of 16 that wants to fish to have a NC state fishing license and a base fishing permit. Children under the age of 16 do not need a state fishing license nor a base fishing permit but must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

# Swimming

## Age Requirements
Children under 10 are welcome at all pools (except Wallace Creek Fitness Center) accompanied by an adult; Children between the ages of 10 and 15 who demonstrate the ability to pass the swim test do not require direct supervision. The swim test consists of swimming 25 yards followed by a one minute tread or float.

## Free Swim Lessons for Active Duty
Any Active Duty military personnel may request a 30-min free swim lesson at any pool where there is a Water Safety Instructor on deck. Personnel may call ahead to see if someone will be there on the day they wish to learn.

Host a Pool Party!

We schedule parties when our facilities are not open to patrons, giving you a private pool party setting. We provide a fun, safe, and clean atmosphere and you bring the rest! Feel free to bring food and refreshments as well.
